# Bloxwap HIG 0.8.1

## ADR 001: platform renderers, shared contracts
Source: docs/architecture/001-packages.md

# ADR 001: platform renderers, shared contracts

Status: accepted for candidate 0.1.0. Issues #4, #5. Evidence: `evidence/upstream-inventory.json`.

```mermaid
graph TD
  Tokens[HIG tokens] --> Web[HIG React]
  Tokens --> Native[HIG Native]
  Contracts[HIG contracts] --> Web
  Contracts --> Native
  Contracts --> Feedback[optional feedback adapters]
  Web --> Docs[docs and consumer fixtures]
  Native --> Expo[Expo gallery]
```

HIG publishes one package, `@bloxwap/hig`; each area below is a subpath entry of it, built from its own `packages/hig/<entry>` source folder. `@bloxwap/hig/tokens` owns palette, density, units and generation; `@bloxwap/hig/contracts` owns platform-neutral types and formatting. `@bloxwap/hig/react` and `@bloxwap/hig/native` own renderers. `@bloxwap/hig/chart` owns the web adapter for `@bloxwap/chart` (`PriceChart`, `chartTheme`), and `@bloxwap/chart` is the package's only required peer (#96). No other entry imports `@bloxwap/chart`, and the peer is never optional: an optional peer on it made npm 11 drop chart's workspace copy when that repository regenerated its lockfile. `@bloxwap/hig/feedback` owns optional adapter entry points. `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts` ships the static native TTFs (#64), and `@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts` ships the five byte-identical Latin faces that Satori/`next/og` cards need (#99). Both are generated from pinned `@bloxwap/font` sources by `npm run generate:fonts`, and their `fonts/` folders are the only places in the package allowed to contain font binaries. Web entries never resolve them. Base controls never load audio, haptics, charts, Expo or another platform. Each component has an individual export; CSS is explicit and side-effectful. Plain HTML consumers use tokens/CSS alone.

Candidate validation matrix: Node 22.22+, TypeScript 5.9, React/DOM 19.1, RN 0.81.5 with Expo 54 and RN 0.83.10 with Expo 55 (React 19.1.0 and 19.2.0 respectively, #68), Vite 6.4. Next 16.4.0 webpack is verified by M5 production/packed consumer checks. NativeWind styling remains outside the supported StyleSheet consumer path. Use StyleSheet on RN and plain CSS on web; Tailwind may refer to `var(--hig-*)` without scanning HIG sources. The pinned monorepo source now documents web/native rem roots of 16; see source reconciliation. Never infer native sizes by replacing `rem` with `dp`.

Prefer built-in semantic controls; modal/disclosure behavior must retain keyboard, focus restoration and descriptions. The `@bloxwap/hig/chart` entry imports the chart SDK only on the client. Libraries retain upstream licenses; extracted tokens and mark have commit provenance, no vendor engine source is copied. Font binaries remain owned by @bloxwap/font (OFL-1.1).

Deprecation plan: inventory all live references, map variants to intent/density, run migration diff and consumer validation, switch a pilot behind a host flag, then delete unused copies. App comfortable targets and Pro compact rows are intentional. HIG cannot retire owning-repository copies within this hig-only change. API/token/behavior changes follow semver; breaking accessibility behavior counts as breaking. Support upgrades require web, SSR and Metro evidence with a documented rollback before changing the matrix.


## Attribution and provenance
Source: docs/architecture/attribution.md

# Attribution and provenance

HIG code: MIT. @radix-ui/react-dialog, dropdown-menu, popover, tooltip: MIT, consumed as dependencies without copied engine code. @bloxwap/chart/sfx/haptic: independent upstream packages; optional integration only (chart through the separate `@bloxwap/hig/chart` adapter). @bloxwap/font: OFL-1.1, binaries stay in its pinned package. Brand SVG/geometry derives from Font docs, exact upstream commit in `evidence/upstream-inventory.json`; do not imply arbitrary trademark relicensing. Utility CheckIcon is original simple geometry. Full icons catalogs are excluded.

## Generated favicon and social preview

`npm run generate` derives unchanged SVG favicons and a 1200×630 SVG social preview from the approved mark. Source SHA256 and derivative paths are in `planning/brand-artifacts.json`; lint rejects stale outputs. The derived preview declares its lineage and omits the source credential metadata; unchanged source/favicons retain it. Hosts whose social crawlers require raster images must render a PNG from this same SVG instead of redrawing the mark. This preview uses a generic font rather than embedding the full font asset.


## Candidate platform support · 0.1.0
Source: docs/architecture/platform-matrix.md

# Candidate platform support · 0.1.0

| Area | DOM | RN | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Actions, surfaces, text, fields | Semantic DOM elements | Pressable/View/Text/TextInput | behavior tests, Vite/SSR/Metro |
| Native text scaling and script tracking | Browser zoom; no cap | `Text`/`Heading`/`NumberReadout` `maxFontSizeMultiplier` (prop or HIGProvider default); Korean/Chinese runs at companion spacing via `script` and `letterSpacingByScript` | native Jest (#67); iOS Simulator AX5: capped readout 48pt vs 86pt prose; Android emulator 200% (non-linear scaling stays under the 2x cap) (`evidence/native-sim/issue-67-71/`) |
| Native colour roles | CSS severity/data attributes | `Switch` `tone`, `Alert` `severity`/`tone` take token roles only; raw colours fall back. The Android Switch thumb uses the `text` token instead of the app theme accent | native Jest (#67); iOS Simulator and Android emulator captures (`evidence/native-sim/issue-67-71/`) |
| Native colour space | CSS sRGB with P3 in `@supports` | `HIGProvider colorSpace` `srgb` (default) or `display-p3`; every component paints from `useColors()`; iOS `display-p3` uses `nativeColors.iosDisplayP3`, Android and web stay sRGB; no raw colours | native Jest (#93: P3 values for action/warning/negative/info, direct-import guard); iOS Simulator capture as a Display P3 host (`evidence/native-sim/issue-93/`); physical display pending (#55) |
| Selection/range | Built-in input/select | OS Switch/community Slider, radio/check Pressables, Modal chooser; Android Slider adds `ACTION_SET_PROGRESS` through the autolinked `HIGAdjustableView` (plain View without native linking) | contract tests; Android emulator UiAutomation (#71): set-progress listed, 80 applied once, snapped/clamped, absent and rejected while disabled; iOS Simulator increment/decrement unchanged (`evidence/native-sim/issue-67-71/`) |
| Dialog/sheet/menu | Radix scoped primitives; optional Vaul GestureSheet with fixed snap points or opt-in dynamic content sizing | Modal and explicit close/back; optional Gorhom GestureSheet with the same sizing alternatives, rejected-close retry and accessibility escape | DOM nested focus/Escape plus real Chromium/WebKit sheet drag, scroll and snap checks; mocked native focus/back/detents plus separate packed Android/iOS gesture entry; physical gesture/screen-reader certification is not claimed |
| Tooltip/popover | Radix hover/focus/anchored | persistent HelpText/modal | no RN hover claim |
| Navigation/search | href/callback adapters | host route/back callbacks | tab/search/disclosure contracts |
| Financial lists/table | semantic table/list; optional per-place animated readout | FlatList labeled rows; optional Reanimated/Worklets per-place readout, static `data` remains engine-free | formatting and contract tests; mixed-bidi/native static fallbacks and physical-device/RTL observations remain limited |
| Chart | `@bloxwap/hig/chart`: lazy @bloxwap/chart canvas (required peer) | numeric/list summary only | typed theme; physical gesture evidence pending |
| Brand mark | individual SVG renderer/asset | optional react-native-svg | pinned geometry; device comparison pending |
| React Native versions | — | RN 0.81.5 / Expo 54 / React 19.1.0 and RN 0.83.10 / Expo 55 / React 19.2.0 and RN 0.88.1 / Expo 58 / React 19.3.0; peer ranges `react-native` `^0.81.5 \|\| ^0.83.10 \|\| ^0.88.0`, SDK-matched Expo, SVG, Slider, Reanimated and Worklets peers | CI packed Metro exports and native-ref typechecks for all three (`smoke:packed-native`, `--profile rn-0.83`, `--profile rn-0.88`); iOS Simulator and Android emulator gallery, interaction and GestureSheet runs on both with the same outcomes; differences tracked in #86–#89 (`evidence/native-sim/rn-0.83/`) |
| Fonts | pinned Sans/Mono asset URLs | hash-pinned static faces, typed manifest, explicit weight registration and host script fallback | Expo-web loading/byte/hash gates; no physical native-font certification |

SSR: client components retain use-client boundaries in emitted JS. Importing a button needs React/tokens/contracts only at runtime. CSS is explicitly imported. Native API never imports DOM, Web Audio or chart. Native target size remains comfortable even when host density is compact; Pro density is a DOM exception, not a reason to shrink phone targets.

Optional peer packages: none for chart, whose `@bloxwap/hig/chart` entry relies on the package's one required peer, `@bloxwap/chart` (#96); community Slider for native selection entry; react-native-svg for the native brand and avatar entries (the native status entry exports `Avatar` without the generated face and loads no SVG); `cuer` for the web and native `wallet-address` entries, plus react-native-svg on native, while the `wallet-address-core` entries load neither and take the host's own QR drawing (the web one draws HIG's `QRCode` when none is passed); react-native-svg alone for the native `qr-code` entry, and no peer for the web one. Vaul is isolated behind the web gesture-sheet entry. Gorhom is isolated behind the native gesture-sheet entry, and Gesture Handler behind the native gesture-sheet and toast entries; Reanimated and Worklets are isolated behind the native gesture-sheet, animated-number, toast and confetti entries. Base imports, including ordinary native `data` readouts, do not load them. No root barrel loads every component. DOM overlays are one scoped family entry and carry Radix MIT attribution; Radix peers are optional caret ranges and overlay-free web blocks have their own entries. ESM is supported; CommonJS consumer support is not claimed.

RN 0.88 compatibility is verified by independent packed TypeScript and Android/iOS Metro consumers. Existing simulator/emulator interaction reports cover RN 0.81 and 0.83 only; no RN 0.88 physical or simulator interaction result is inferred from a bundle export.


## CI runners
Source: docs/ci-runners.md

# CI runners

GitHub Actions jobs run on self-hosted Apple silicon Mac minis, except for the `publish` job in `publish.yml` and `linux-visual` in `quality.yml`:

```yaml
runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
```

The trusted-publishing job uses GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04`; Linux visual verification uses GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` with Chromium and `--with-deps`. All other jobs remain self-hosted and do not call `apt`, `sudo`, or Playwright `--with-deps`. Scratch directories use `$RUNNER_TEMP`. Jobs that run npm/Python/Playwright export `TMPDIR=$RUNNER_TEMP` through `GITHUB_ENV` (the `runner` context is not available in workflow or job `env`).

## Required on every Mac mini

- macOS on Apple silicon, with the Actions runner registered using the labels `self-hosted`, `macOS`, and `ARM64`
- Git
- Python 3.10+ with the standard-library `venv` module (`fonttools` 4.61.1 requires `>=3.10`). GitHub's `actions/setup-python` macOS builds mkdir `/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache` and fail on these minis (`Permission denied`). CI therefore installs relocatable CPython 3.12 into `$RUNNER_TEMP` with a pinned `uv` 0.13.1 binary (`scripts/ci-setup-python.sh`). The login-shell Python does not have to be 3.12. Cache misses create `$RUNNER_TEMP/hig-fonttools` and install `fonttools[woff]==4.61.1` and `brotli==1.2.1` there; they do not write to system site-packages
- Network access to npm, GitHub, and Playwright browser downloads
- Homebrew `gnu-tar` on **every** mini so `gtar` is on the runner service `PATH` or at `$(brew --prefix)/opt/gnu-tar/bin`. `actions/upload-pages-artifact` invokes `gtar` on macOS (`--hard-dereference` is a GNU option). Install with `brew install gnu-tar`. One machine having it is not enough.
- Disk for npm caches, Playwright browsers at `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright`, packed-consumer trees under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and generated font faces

Node 24.22.1 is installed per self-hosted job by `actions/setup-node`. It does not need to be the login-shell default. On the minis, `setup-node` must not set `cache: npm` (and must not rely on v5+ automatic npm caching): the minis already keep `~/.npm` on disk, and GitHub's cache store has saved 1.1–1.3 GB archives at about 1 MB/s, producing 27-minute `Post setup-node` tails. Quality jobs reuse generated native/OG font faces (~4 MB) from an on-disk cache on each mini (`scripts/ci-native-fonts.sh`, under `~/Library/Caches/bloxwap-hig/native-fonts`), not from `actions/cache`. The publication job uses no Actions caches and generates fonts every time with `bash scripts/ci-generate-fonts.sh`.

## Playwright

Mac mini jobs that need browsers run `npx playwright install chromium webkit` with no `--with-deps`. Browsers stay on disk at `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright` across jobs on a mini; do not save that folder with `actions/cache` (it stalls 11+ minutes because the directory is shared). Chromium and WebKit must launch headless as the runner user. Playwright Firefox is not installed or launched.

## Visual baselines

Catalog Button/Field/Input states and Slider focus captures live under `tests/visual-baselines/<process.platform>/` (`linux` or `darwin`). Geometry changes still fail; pixel changes still fail above 2% after a 24-channel-value antialias tolerance. Missing Darwin images fail closed: review the uploaded capture and commit it with `HIG_UPDATE_VISUALS=1`. Do not copy a Linux baseline or raise the thresholds to hide an OS difference.

## Not required for these workflows

The `native` job exports Android and iOS Metro bundles (`smoke:packed-native` for RN 0.81.5 / Expo 54 and RN 0.83.10 / Expo 55, and RN 0.88.1 / Expo 58). It does not boot simulators. Xcode, an iOS Simulator runtime, JDK 17, and the Android SDK are only for local `scripts/native-sim/` gallery runs, which these workflows do not execute.

## Jobs

### HIG candidate quality and dry-run artifacts (`quality.yml`)

| Job | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `paths-filter` | Same PR path filter as before; docs-only PRs skip the heavy jobs |
| `compiler` | Compiler selection, TypeScript fallback and emit parity |
| `quality (task)` | 14 independent lanes: static checks, web tests, native tests, ten packed-consumer checks, and release dry-run verification |
| `native (profile)` | Separate packed native Metro exports for RN 0.81 / Expo 54, RN 0.83 / Expo 55, and RN 0.88 / Expo 58 |
| `browser (gate)` | 18 separate suites covering Chromium, WebKit, components, Expo, docs, catalog and Next hydration; each starts only its required previews |
| `linux-visual` | Linux Chromium baseline comparison |
| `candidate` | Required aggregate check; waits for every matrix lane and fails if any lane fails or is unexpectedly skipped |

The matrices use `fail-fast: false` so failures do not cancel other diagnostic results. They have no `max-parallel` cap: GitHub schedules as many lanes as the available runners allow. Each lane has its own checkout, `$RUNNER_TEMP`, build outputs, tarballs and uniquely named failure artifacts. Browser preview ports are allocated dynamically. Package builds precede their consumers within each lane; release dry-run and artifact verification remain ordered. Local `run-browser-gates.mjs` runs all suites by default; `HIG_BROWSER_GATE` selects one, and invalid selectors fail closed.

More lanes only run simultaneously when the fleet has free runner capacity. Register each additional runner service with a distinct installation/work directory; do not share a checkout or temp directory. Heavy native exports and browser processes still compete for a mini's CPU and memory, so size the runner fleet accordingly. Workflow concurrency cancels superseded PR runs while keeping unrelated PRs independent. Publication and deployment retain their security, approval and artifact dependencies.

### Documentation (`docs.yml`)

| Job | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `build` | Static docs build and typecheck. GitHub Pages artifact only on `main` (same condition as deploy); pull requests still build and validate |
| `deploy` | GitHub Pages deploy from `main` |

### Registry publication (`publish.yml`)

The `publish` job runs on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04`, as required by [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/). It installs the pinned npm@11.6.1, checks out the release tag, downloads the prepared tarball, verifies its report digest and every package hash, then publishes with OIDC and `--provenance`. It does not rebuild packages or run consumer tests.

All heavy release work uses the self-hosted Macs. After the exact-tag quality prerequisite succeeds, three `validation` lanes (static/quality checks, web tests, and native tests) run alongside `prepare`, which builds and verifies the stable artifact. The security scan runs independently. `publish` waits for all of them and the `npm-release` environment approval. The prepared report's SHA-256 is passed as a job output and checked after download, before the existing source/version/package-set/tarball verification. Artifacts are named per run and attempt, so retries use their producing job's exact artifact.

After publication, five `registry` lanes run concurrently: web/SSR, Next hydration, and RN 0.81, 0.83 and 0.88. Every lane verifies registry tarball hashes, provenance and npm signatures before testing its consumer. They retain bounded registry-visibility retries, never suppress failures, and upload separate evidence. No matrix concurrency cap is set; runner availability limits scheduling. The release setup action installs npm in a unique `$RUNNER_TEMP` prefix, so concurrent runner services do not replace a shared npm executable.

A published GitHub release or a manual dispatch must use the existing release tag as its ref. The prerequisites still require configured `npm-release` reviewers and a successful quality run for the exact source commit. Only the hosted publication job has `id-token: write`; validation, preparation and registry jobs have read-only repository permissions. No token fallback or approval bypass is provided.

All eight `@bloxwap/hig-*` Trusted Publishers are configured for repository `bloxwap/hig`, workflow `publish.yml`, environment `npm-release`. The 0.1.2 publication records npm's GitHub Actions trusted-publisher identity for each package, separately from its signed provenance. No workflow step references the organization publishing token. The shared organization secret remains available to other repositories. Required environment reviewers and exact-source quality gates remain mandatory. See the [release policy](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/governance/release/) and `evidence/release/registry-0.1.2/` for verification.


## Actions & surfaces
Source: docs/components/actions-surfaces.md

# Actions & surfaces

Buttons, typography, and layout primitives for clear actions and related content.

Includes `Button`, `IconButton`, `Link`, `Text`, `Heading`, `Stack`, `Inline`, `Surface`, `Card`, `Separator`, `InstallCommand`, and `MarketingHero`.

Issue #13. Entry: `button / surface`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig/react/button` or `@bloxwap/hig/native/button` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Button`, `IconButton` | `children`, `intent`, `busy`, `busyLabel`, `disabled`, `fullWidth`, `suppressFeedback`, and forwarded ref. Web uses `onClick`; native uses `onPress`. A busy Button shows a spinner on the leading side of its label; a busy IconButton shows the spinner in place of its icon. The busy text (` · Working`) is not drawn: it is appended to the accessible name from HIGProvider `messages.busy` or `busyLabel`; `''` omits it while busy state stays exposed. Native: the label renders through HIG `Text` (HIGProvider or `maxFontSizeMultiplier` prop font-scale cap, registered family for the weight, per-script letter spacing), and a busy Button with text children sets its accessible name ([localization rule](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/localization/#built-in-component-strings)); an explicit `accessibilityLabel` wins. On web, HIGProvider `pressDecoration` draws a host element inside every Button (`kind: 'button'`) and IconButton (`'icon-button'`) without changing its layout, for example the native switch input iOS Safari needs for a haptic ([blocks](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/blocks/#shared-host-hooks)). A native IconButton is drawn at 44dp and reaches 48dp on every side through `hitSlop`; a host `hitSlop` wins. `intent` also takes the market-direction fills `up` (buy, long) and `down` (sell, short), on both platforms (0.8.0): the fill follows HIGProvider `marketColors` (web `--hig-up`/`--hig-down`, native `useColors().up`/`.down`), which default to the buy and sell colours, with the dark label `destructive` uses, so a host's Long/Short or confirm-close actions keep the market convention (red for up in KRX or A-share hosts) without drawing their own button. `intent='warning'` fills with the warning role (web `--hig-warning`, native `useColors().warning`) with the same dark label, for an action that goes ahead despite a caution, such as `ConfirmBlock confirmIntent='warning'`. Unavailable stays neutral like every intent. Type `ButtonIntent`. `href` (Button, web and native, 0.8.0) makes a filled pill a real link, described [below](#button-as-a-link). `glow` (Button, web and native, 0.8.0) draws a soft halo in the fill colour around a filled intent (`primary`, `destructive`, `up`, `down`, `warning`): two spread shadows at 45% and 20% of the fill (web `.hig-button[data-glow]`, the colour from `--hig-glow`; native `boxShadow`, which needs React Native's new architecture). Use it for the one hero action of a brand or marketing surface, such as a 404 page's Trade BTC; `secondary` and `ghost` ignore it, and an unavailable button has no halo. |
| `Link` | Platform link behavior; host applications own routing. |
| `Text`, `Heading` | Platform text props. `Text` takes `tone='muted'` (secondary text, such as a note under a group, in the muted role) and `size='caption'` (12/18 instead of the 16/24 body), on both platforms; a native `style` colour or size still wins. Native adds `maxFontSizeMultiplier` (font-scale cap for dense numeric readouts, also on `NumberReadout`; HIGProvider sets a default) and `script` (`latin`, `ko`, `zh`; detected from string children). Korean and Chinese runs use the companion face's own spacing (`scriptLetterSpacing`, 0em) instead of Latin tracking; HIGProvider `letterSpacingByScript` overrides it per script in em. |
| `Stack`, `Inline`, `Surface`, `Card` | Platform layout props. |
| `InstallCommand` | `command` and `onCopy`; accepts an asynchronous host clipboard adapter. The copy result is raised as a toast: on web when `Toaster` from `@bloxwap/hig/react/toast` is mounted, and inline otherwise. The block itself does not load Sonner. Native renders the command in the provider's `monoFontFamily` and keeps it left-to-right inside RTL roots; a copy failure leaves a manual-selection recovery message. Imported from the blocks entry (`@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks`, `@bloxwap/hig/native/blocks`). |
| `MarketingHero` | `title`, `description`, `href`, and `cta`: a heading, one sentence and a link for a landing section. Imported from the blocks entry (`@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks`, `@bloxwap/hig/native/blocks`). |

## When to use and examples

Actions that sit side by side are 8 units apart at every density: buttons in an Alert, tabs, Pagination, Filter capsules and the SwapPanelBlock action row. On web that is the `--hig-action-gap` variable (the `sm` space token); set it on a container to change it. Content inside `Stack` and `Inline` keeps the density gap (12 on touch, 8 compact), so put a row of buttons in a container that uses `--hig-action-gap`, not a bare `Inline`.

The primary and secondary call-to-action buttons that close a form sit a double step below the rest of it: 16 units (`--hig-action-offset`, twice the action gap), and 8 units from each other. TradeEntry, the SwapPanelBlock action row, and the buttons that end a Dialog or a default sheet follow this already. In a host form laid out with `Stack`, add `className='hig-form-action'` to each closing button on web, or a 4dp top margin on native, where the `Stack` gap is 12.

Use one primary review action. Do: busy protects host requests, shows the leading spinner and announces the translated busy label (`Working` in English). Don’t: use destructive red for every sell button.

### Button as a link

Give `Button` an `href` when the action goes somewhere instead of doing something, such as a pill that opens docs or a route, so it keeps the button's look and gets link behaviour (open in a new tab, copy link, the link role).

- **Web** renders `<a class="hig-button" href>` with the same `data-intent`, `data-full`, density, `glow`, busy spinner and busy text, and the same `onClick` and accepted feedback (a host `preventDefault()` cancels both the navigation and the feedback). `target` and `rel` pass through as given (browsers already treat `target="_blank"` as `noopener`; pass `rel` for `noreferrer`). Disabled or busy, the anchor drops its `href`, so it leaves the tab order like a disabled button, and keeps `role="link"` with `aria-disabled="true"` (and `aria-busy` while busy); a click does nothing. The forwarded ref then holds the `HTMLAnchorElement` (the ref type stays `HTMLButtonElement` so existing refs keep compiling). `IconButton` takes no `href`.
- **Native** sets `accessibilityRole="link"`. Without `onPress`, a press opens `href` through `Linking.openURL` and a failure goes to `onError`, as `Link` does; a host `onPress` (an Expo Router push or an in-app browser) replaces that navigation, so one press never opens both. Disabled or busy blocks both. On React Native Web the root renders the `href` and the press stops the anchor navigating on its own.

Label wrapping (web): a label breaks between words first. `.hig-button` uses `overflow-wrap: break-word`, so a word that is a little wider than the space beside a trailing icon in a narrow two-button row (`ExplainerBlock`, `ConfirmBlock` and `TargetBlock` action rows at 320px) runs into the button's own padding instead of splitting mid-word (“Get my disco/unt” before). A single word wider than the whole button still overflows it, so keep action labels, and their translations, short.

## States, interaction and accessibility

DOM semantic button/anchor, forwarded focus, target minimum width and height tied to density (web: 44px comfortable, 36px compact); RN target always at least 48. Multiline labels wrap at word boundaries; RN custom children render in a View with text nodes styled individually.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

RN external Link uses Linking; routes belong to host. Native fontFamily only after registration. Decorative SVG hidden; IconButton label is mandatory.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.

Native `Button contentMode="custom"` renders host Text/View children directly, preserving layouts with separate identity and trailing nodes. The root retains minimum target, disabled/busy, propagation, ref and accepted-feedback behavior. Hosts own visible busy content in this mode; `busyLabel` still controls the accessible busy suffix. Keep child content noninteractive and give icon-only actions an accessible label.

Native `Link` accepts a forwarded View ref, root Pressable props and `contentMode="custom"` for host label/icon nodes. Required `href` retains its destination. Without `onPress`, it opens through Linking and reports failures to `onError`; a supplied `onPress` replaces that navigation so host WebBrowser/route handlers run exactly once. Disabled links reject activation. The root always has link semantics.

The catalog browser gate measures controls at both densities, including their clickable wrapping labels for checkbox, radio and switch inputs. Only inline prose links matching `p .hig-link` are exempt from the target minimum (WCAG 2.5.8 inline-text exception); standalone and breadcrumb links retain the full target. Hidden controls are not targets.


## Blocks
Source: docs/components/blocks.md

# Blocks

Composed patterns for balances, markets, trade review, swapping, picking assets, and documentation.

Includes `SwapPanelBlock`, `FromPickerBlock`, `ToPickerBlock`, `AccountBlock`, `TokenActionBlock`, `ConfirmBlock`, `LanguageBlock`, `ManagePositionBlock`, `TradeHistoryListBlock`, `TradeHistoryDetailBlock`, `TargetBlock`, `PresetPickerBlock`, `ExplainerBlock`, `PositionBlock`, `AssetsBlock`, `ProfileBlock`, `RewardBlock`, `SoundHapticsBlock`, `SignalsBlock`, and `NotificationsBlock`, and the `ScreenHeader` they all share.

`MarketRow`, `TradeEntry`, `InstallCommand` and `MarketingHero` are still imported from the blocks entry, but they are single components, not whole screens, so they are documented with their families: `MarketRow` in Financial data, `TradeEntry` in Fields & inputs, and `InstallCommand` and `MarketingHero` in Actions & surfaces.

Issue #26. Entry: `blocks`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks` or `@bloxwap/hig/native/blocks` according to applicability below. On web, each block also has its own entry, for example `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/install-command`, `blocks/market-row` and `blocks/marketing-hero`. These need no Radix peer; `smoke:packed-boundaries` renders and bundles them with no Radix installed (#63). `blocks/swap-panel-block` needs none either. `blocks/trade-entry` and the aggregate `blocks` entry need `@radix-ui/react-dialog` for the confirm step. `blocks/swap-sheet` (not in the aggregate) needs `vaul`. Import `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

Blocks were called recipes through 0.5.x. The old import paths, `@bloxwap/hig/react/recipes`, `@bloxwap/hig/react/recipes/<name>` and `@bloxwap/hig/native/recipes`, still resolve to the same modules and are deprecated: move imports to `blocks`. The native one is also a real file, `native/dist/recipes.js`, that re-exports the blocks, so a Jest `moduleNameMapper` that maps `@bloxwap/hig/native/<entry>` to `native/dist/<entry>.js` resolves it. They stay for at least one minor release and 30 days and are removed in the next major release, as the deprecation policy in the release guide requires. Blocks added after 0.5.2, such as `AccountBlock` and `TokenActionBlock`, `LanguageBlock`, exist only under `blocks`.

## API and anatomy

All data and actions are supplied by the host application.

| Block | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `SwapPanelBlock` | Send, swap and bridge in one panel. `tokens` (and optional `fromTokens`, `chains`, `hotTokenIds`), the pair as `from` / `to` with `onFromChange` / `onToChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultFrom` / `defaultTo`, `onAmountChange` (From amount in token units), the host quote as `received`, `fee`, `fees` and `quoteLoading`, `slippage` / `onSlippageChange`, `wallet`, `receive`, and `onSubmit(action)`. Details below. |
| `AccountBlock` | An account at a glance: a header, the total with a deposit action, the pinned dollar balance, then every other holding by value. Details below. |
| `TokenActionBlock` | One token and what can be done with it: where it is held, the chains it sits on, and the actions as equal full-width buttons. Details below. |
| `ConfirmBlock` | The last look before a send: the amount as the headline, the destination address in full and the network as plain lines, a warning that the send cannot be taken back, then Cancel and Confirm side by side. Details below. |
| `TradeHistoryListBlock` | A history of closed trades: a header, then one row per trade with the asset, its side and leverage, and the net result over its age. Details below. |
| `TradeHistoryDetailBlock` | The full record of one closed trade: the asset, the net result as the headline figure, the trade's figures as rows, and the host's actions. Details below. |
| `LanguageBlock` | Choose the app's language: a header, a search field, and each language as a row with its flag and a check on the one in use. Details below. |
| `ManagePositionBlock` | One open position: margin against notional as a `BarMark`, the liquidation, mark and entry prices as a `BarPnl`, the host's actions as rows, and the position underneath. Details below. |
| `TargetBlock` | A take profit or a stop loss on one position: the target as the headline figure, an info button for how the order fills, the entry and trigger prices on one bar, the unit, quick choices and the confirming action. Details below. |
| `PresetPickerBlock` | Choose one value from quick choices, such as an order size or leverage: an optional header, the value as the headline figure, an optional row that opens the host's own entry, the choices as chips, then Cancel and the confirming action. Details below. |
| `ExplainerBlock` | How something works, or how to finish a task: an optional header, a lead paragraph, titled sections with an optional icon and tone, numbered steps, a closing note, then one or two actions. Details below. |
| `PositionBlock` | The position being opened or edited: a summary of what it costs and where it ends, an optional paper trading switch, and its settings as grouped rows. Details below. |
| `AssetsBlock` | Choose a market: a search field, category capsules, All / Positions / Trend views, then the markets in sections by category, each with its signal disc. Details below. |
| `ProfileBlock` | A person's profile as one screen: the avatar with a status dot, the name, then grouped rows for accounts, history, rewards and settings. Details below. |
| `RewardBlock` | A competition: a prize pool or sweepstakes promotion, a choice of standings, the viewer's own standing, and the ranked list. Details below. |
| `SoundHapticsBlock` | Sound, microphone, haptics and flash settings: one card per channel with a switch, and for a channel that is on its device, input meter and volume steps. Details below. |
| `SignalsBlock` | The signals the viewer receives, in groups with a heading, a small help pill and switches. Details below. |
| `NotificationsBlock` | The notifications the viewer receives: one card per kind with a switch, and a failure under its card. Details below. |
| `FromPickerBlock` | Where assets come from: a connected wallet row (disconnect optional) or Connect wallet with a Generate address switch, above a searchable token list. Details below. |
| `ToPickerBlock` | Where assets go: a destination address field with a scan button, on its own or above a searchable token list with or without the chain filter. Details below. |

Presentation mode uses a grid with logical numeric alignment and no block padding. The host can set matching column widths on each row through `style`/`className`, its compact height and the surrounding keyboard/option semantics. The number face inherits from that row. Slots render host content; keep decorative icons/indicators hidden from assistive technology, or give interactive controls their own names and deliberate keyboard behavior. Presentation rows accept no `onSelect` and emit no action feedback. Tiny prices keep the requested precision; unknown values remain —. Volume formatting and units stay host-owned. The optional `identity` slot belongs to presentation mode; action mode keeps its named HIG button. Hosts that use `toFixed` rounding should pass their already-rounded percent-point value plus explicit `changeOptions` to preserve binary rounding, trailing digits, signs and negative zero. Options use the same contract as `Percent`: the input is percent points, and the rendered style remains percent.

### SwapPanelBlock

`SwapPanelBlock` was called `SwapPanel` through 0.5.x. The old component name, its `SwapPanelProps` type and the import paths `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/swap-panel` and `@bloxwap/hig/react/recipes/swap-panel` still work and are deprecated; they are removed in the next major release. The swap pieces around it keep their names: `SwapSheet`, `SwapAmountCard`, `SwapPill`, `SwapKeypad`, `SwapToken` and the other `Swap…` types.

`SwapPanelBlock` is a From card and a To card joined by a flip control, with one action button that names itself from the pair: the same asset is **Send**, different assets on one chain is **Swap**, and different assets across chains is **Bridge** (`swapAction(from, to)` returns the same value). Until the pair and amount are valid the button is disabled and says what is missing: select a token, enter an amount, or insufficient balance.

```tsx
<SwapPanelBlock tokens={catalog} fromTokens={holdings} hotTokenIds={ranked}
  from={from} to={to} onFromChange={setFrom} onToChange={setTo}
  onAmountChange={setUnits} received={quote?.out} fee={quote?.feeUsd} fees={quote?.fees} quoteLoading={loading}
  slippage={slippage} onSlippageChange={setSlippage}
  wallet={{connected, address}} onConnect={connect} onDisconnect={disconnect}
  submitting={executing} onSubmit={action => execute(action, quote)}/>
```

One panel covers each flow with the same cards; the catalog page shows every one as an example state.

| Flow | From card | Bottom card | Props | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Swap | token | another token, same chain | the pair | `swap` |
| Bridge | token | a token on another chain | the pair | `bridge` |
| Send | token | recipient, still to be picked | `destination` with `pending` and `onPress` | `send` |
| Deposit to an account | account, dollars only | the account | `caption` on the token, `lockFrom`, `destination`, `denominationSwitch={false}` | `deposit` |
| Withdraw from an account | account | where it lands, with a limit note | as deposit, plus `note` | `withdraw` |
| Withdraw to another chain | account the user can change | pressable destination | `destination` with `onPress` | `withdraw-chain` |
| Stake | holding, token units | label and value rows | `details`, `denomination='token'` | `stake` |
| Unstake | position, token units | rows, with a warning | `details`, `note`, `noteTone='negative'` | `unstake` |
| Receive | QR code and address | hidden | `receive`, `receiving` | none |

Stake and unstake are one example each: the asset changes only the token data, not the layout.

- **Tokens.** A `SwapToken` is `{id, symbol, name, chain, chainId}` plus optional `icon`, `chainIcon`, `balance` (token units), `price` (USD per unit) and `keywords` (extra search text such as the contract address). `balance` enables Max, Test and the balance check; `price` enables the dollar and unit conversion and the estimate shown before `received` arrives.
- **Amount.** The From amount is typed in dollars or token units; the capsule under it switches denomination and converts the entry. Keys typed while focus is in the panel, a paste, and the keypad all drive it. `onAmountChange` always reports token units as canonical decimal text, preserving up to 100 fractional places (18 for dollar-to-token conversion when token precision is omitted). Estimates use floating point; transaction callbacks do not. Set `amount` only to resync the entry, for example to `'0'` after a submit. `keypad='auto'` shows the keypad for a coarse pointer on web and always on native; `captureKeyboard` (web) lets digits typed anywhere outside a text field drive the amount.
- **Pushed views.** The token pickers and settings are views pushed inside the panel's own bounds, replacing the cards, each with a Back control; Escape pops one level on web and choosing a token pops to the cards. `view` / `onViewChange` (`'main' | 'from' | 'to' | 'settings' | 'slippage' | 'fees'`) control the stack when the host needs to.
- **Pickers.** Pressing a card pushes its picker: search, chain filter chips, an optional Hot section from `hotTokenIds`, and the token list with arrow-key and Enter selection on web. The From picker shows the connected wallet with a disconnect control, or Connect wallet and the receive toggle; the To picker shows the recipient field when `onRecipientChange` is set, with a scan button when `onScanRecipient` is set. On web ⌘F / Ctrl+F and ⌘K / Ctrl+K open the From and To pickers while the panel is mounted; pass `shortcuts={false}` to leave the browser's own shortcuts alone.
- **Settings.** The menu button pushes the settings view: the default denomination, slippage (presets plus a custom percent) and the fee breakdown one level deeper, then any host rows passed as `settings`.
- **Receive view.** With `receive={{address, qr, onCopy}}` the From picker offers “Receive to an address”. The From card then shows the host's QR node beside the address in fixed-width rows with the leading and trailing characters emphasised, the To amount is hidden, and the action becomes “Send from your wallet” (calls `onConnect`). HIG ships no QR encoder or scanner: the host renders `qr` and implements `onScanRecipient`.
- **Fixed destination.** `destination={{title, subtitle, icon, address, detail, onPress}}` replaces the To token with a place the host already knows: a recipient wallet, a staking pool, a trading account. The To card becomes one compact row with no picker and no amount, the panel is one-way, the action is ready from the From side alone, and `onSubmit` receives `'send'`. `address` shows shortened with the wallet's colour disc; `onPress` makes the card a button with a trailing chevron, for example to change the recipient; `fee` shows on the card when the host passes it.
- **Accounts.** A token with a `caption` (for example `$22.72 available`, or the same as a live figure, `{value:22.72, options:{style:'currency', currency:'USD'}, suffix:' available'}`) is presented as an account: the name over the caption beside one disc, with Max only. A small chevron follows the name while the side can still be changed.
- **Pending destination.** `destination.pending` shows the destination as a placeholder; the action stays disabled and reads “Pick a destination” until the host supplies a real one.
- **Prices.** `entry` and `exit` draw one `BarPnl` without a card, scaled to the two prices: the stretch between them is filled in the result colour and the two prices read under it. This replaces an Entry row and an Exit row. `priceOptions` formats them; the default is US dollars. Leave either out and there is no bar.
- **Details.** `details=[{label, value, options, prefix, suffix}]` are the other figures, such as size, notional, time held, fees and funding. They are drawn three to a line as a small label over its value, in the order given. A number is formatted with `options` between `prefix` and `suffix` and updates place by place; a string is drawn as given, which suits a duration the host has already formatted.
- **Note.** `note` is a line under the cards for a limit or a delay; `noteTone='warning'` or `'negative'` makes it a tinted capsule.
- **Heading and controls.** `title` puts a heading above the cards and `onBack` a Back control beside it, for a panel that is its own screen or sheet. From 0.8.0 the heading is the shared `ScreenHeader` on both platforms (the title centred, 17/24 weight 600, in a 44 unit row with Back on its leading edge), like every other block, so a push from another block to a titled panel keeps Back and the title in place; it was a left-aligned 24px (web) or `Heading` (native) title. Native test IDs stay `swap-header` and `swap-back`, with `swap-title` added. `headingId` sets the heading's `id` (web) or `nativeID` (native). `controls={false}` leaves the action button alone at full width, and `actionIcon` puts a decoration before its text.
- **Locked sides.** `lockFrom` / `lockTo` keep that side's token fixed: its card looks the same but does not open the picker, has no shortcut, and reset leaves the token in place.
- **Action label.** `actionLabel` names the action once it is ready, in place of Send, Swap or Bridge: Stake, Deposit, Unstake. The host supplies the translated text. The prompts before it is ready (select a token, enter an amount, insufficient balance) do not change.
- **Host-held action.** `actionDisabled` holds the action for a reason only the host knows (below a minimum, no quote yet, a closed market), and `actionStatus` is what it then says. The panel's own prompts still come first. `actionIntent='destructive'` is for an action that cannot be undone, such as a burn.
- **Submission.** While `submitting` is true, operation-changing controls stop accepting edits. The host must still capture the exact amount, asset identities, destination, quote and expiry before awaiting execution, revalidate them in its transaction layer, and provide idempotency. An enabled button is not transaction authorization. Web global input belongs to one visible panel; set `active={false}` for a retained inactive screen.
- **Amount limits.** A token's `decimals` must be an integer from 0 to 100. It caps keypad, pasted and externally supplied token amounts; dollars stop at two places. `limitToBalance` rejects edits above any known balance, including zero, and clamps external resync to that balance. Without the cap, insufficient amounts remain visible but cannot submit. Unknown balances are distinct from zero.
- **Artwork.** A token's `icon` and `chainIcon` and a destination's `icon` take an image URL or the host's own element, which fills the disc.
- **Host content.** `banner` sits above the From card (a pending transfer) and `footer` under the action (recent activity).
- **Starting amount.** A mounted `amount` (token units) seeds the entry in the default denomination.
- **Fixed denomination.** `denominationSwitch={false}` removes the conversion capsule under each amount and the denomination setting, and keeps both amounts in `denomination` (dollars by default). Use it when the host only has one of the two, for example dollars with no token price.
- **One way.** `oneWay` is for flows that only run top to bottom, such as a deposit: the control between the cards becomes a decorative down arrow instead of the flip button, and the pair cannot be exchanged.
- **Live numbers (required).** Every number in the swap card that can change while the card is on screen updates through `AnimatedNumberReadout`: only the places that changed move, and the text is never swapped in one step. This covers the entered and received amounts, the conversion capsule, the From balance, the fee and slippage on the To card, an account caption, the destination detail, detail rows, the settings rows and fee breakdown, and the balances in the token pickers. The panel does this itself for everything it formats. For text the host writes, pass the figure as a number so the panel can do the same: `details=[{label:'Staked', value:11.0735, suffix:' HYPE'}]`, `caption={{value:234.68, options:{style:'currency', currency:'USD'}, suffix:' available'}}`, `destination.detail={{value:3.1, suffix:'% APR'}}`. A string is still accepted and is drawn as given; use it only for text that does not change, such as a tier name. A value that is loading or unknown shows `…` or `—` and does not roll in from zero. Reduced motion updates the same numbers without movement, and the accessible reading is always the final value. Host-drawn parts of the card follow the rule too: `SwapNumber` (web, from the swap panel entry) or `AnimatedNumberReadout` for a `SwapAmountCard` `meta` or `conversion`, and for custom settings rows. On native the swap panel and pickers entries therefore need the optional Reanimated and Worklets peers of the `animated-number` entry.
- **Ownership.** The panel never fetches a quote, reads a wallet or submits a transaction. `onSubmit` is called once per accepted press and not while `submitting`.
- **Submitting.** While `submitting`, the action shows its spinner, ignores presses and keeps its ready name (`actionLabel`, or Send, Swap or Bridge), or says `submittingLabel` (host text such as “Burning…”) when given, even if the host has already cleared the amount (`amount='0'`) or the balance has dropped: it never falls back to “Enter an amount” or “Insufficient …” mid-submit. Without `submittingLabel`, a held action (`actionDisabled`) still says its `actionStatus` (such as “Signing…”). The keypad, typed keys, Max and Test leave the amount as it is until `submitting` clears. A missing token or a pending destination still names itself first. Without `submitting` the action text is unchanged.

`SwapAmountCard`, from the same web entry, is the From card on its own for a host that enters one amount without a pair, such as a position size. It draws the asset (`name`, `symbol`, `icon` as a URL or a host-drawn node, optional `chainIcon` and `context` line), capsule `actions` such as Max (use `SwapPill`), a `meta` line such as the balance, and the entered `value` with `prefix`, `suffix`, `fractionDigits` and `trailingDot`. `conversion` puts a capsule under the amount, and `onSelect` with `selectLabel` makes the slot choose the asset. The host owns the entry and the keypad; `SwapKeypad` is exported beside it.

```tsx
<SwapAmountCard name="USD Coin" symbol="USDC" context="Hyperliquid" value={Number(entry)} prefix="$"
  fractionDigits={typedDecimals} trailingDot={entry.endsWith(".")} amountLabel="Size"
  actions={<SwapPill onClick={useMax}>Max</SwapPill>} meta="1,000 USDC" />
```

Native has the same two from `@bloxwap/hig/native/blocks` (and the native swap panel module): `SwapAmountCard` takes the same props (`name`, `symbol`, `icon` as a URL or element, `chainIcon`, `context`, `actions`, `meta`, `value`, `amountLabel`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `fractionDigits`, `trailingDot`, `maximumFractionDigits` default 8, `conversion`, `onSelect`, `selectLabel`, `style`) and draws the panel's From card: a string `context` or `meta` is drawn small and muted and a node as given, the `actions` stay their own targets on the trailing edge, and the amount is one element named by `amountLabel` whose value is the drawn text (`$1.50`, `12.` while a dot is typed). `testID` (default `swap-amount-card`) prefixes `-slot`, `-select`, `-name`, `-context`, `-actions`, `-meta`, `-amount` and `-conversion`. `SwapPill` is the capsule (32dp, a 44dp target): `children` as text drawn small and muted, or nodes as given; `onPress`; `disabled` dims it and reads as unavailable; other Pressable props such as `accessibilityLabel`, `testID` or `android_disableSound` reach it.

```tsx
<SwapAmountCard name="USD Coin" symbol="USDC" context="Hyperliquid" value={Number(entry)} prefix="$"
  fractionDigits={typedDecimals} trailingDot={entry.endsWith('.')} amountLabel="Size"
  actions={<SwapPill onPress={useMax}>Max</SwapPill>} meta="1,000 USDC"/>
```

`SwapSheet` presents the panel in a gesture sheet: `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/swap-sheet` on web (Vaul) and `@bloxwap/hig/native/swap-sheet` on native (the native `GestureSheet` backend). It takes every `SwapPanelBlock` prop plus `open`, `onOpenChange`, a required accessible `title` and, on web, an optional `trigger`. Views push inside that one sheet, which follows the height of the view on show. Escape and Back pop a pushed view first; from the cards, Escape, the scrim and a downward drag close the sheet, and a reopened sheet starts on the cards. The native `SwapSheet` needs the optional `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` peer and the host's sheet providers, exactly as `GestureSheet` does; on Android the hardware Back button pops a pushed view before it closes the sheet.

```tsx
<SwapSheet title='Swap' open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} trigger={<Button>Swap</Button>} tokens={catalog} onSubmit={execute}/>
```

### FromPickerBlock and ToPickerBlock

The two pickers are the swap panel's token views as standalone blocks, for a host that picks a source or a destination outside the panel: in its own sheet, a page, or a step of a flow. They carry no sheet or overlay of their own; place them in a `Dialog`, a `GestureSheet` or any container. `SwapPanelBlock` uses the same two blocks for its pushed views.

Both share one token list: `tokens` (a wallet's holdings, a whitelist or a whole catalog), `selected`, `onSelect`, optional `chains`, `hotTokenIds` and `loading`. The search and address fields are the standard rounded HIG inputs. `chainFilter={false}` leaves out the chain filter, for a single chain or a list that should not be narrowed by chain; it is also left out when the tokens are all on one chain.

```tsx
import {FromPickerBlock, ToPickerBlock} from '@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/pickers';

// Destination address only
<ToPickerBlock address={address} onAddressChange={setAddress} addressPlaceholder={shortWallet} onScan={openScanner}/>
// Address, then the asset, filtered by chain
<ToPickerBlock address={address} onAddressChange={setAddress} onScan={openScanner} tokens={catalog} selected={to} onSelect={setTo}/>
// The same without the chain filter
<ToPickerBlock tokens={catalog} chainFilter={false} selected={to} onSelect={setTo}/>

// No wallet yet: connect, or generate an address to send to
<FromPickerBlock wallet={{connected: false}} onConnect={connect} generateAddress={generating} onGenerateAddressChange={setGenerating} tokens={catalog} onSelect={setFrom}/>
// Connected: holdings, with sign-out
<FromPickerBlock wallet={{connected: true, address}} onDisconnect={disconnect} tokens={holdings} selected={from} onSelect={setFrom}/>
```

| Variant | Props |
| --- | --- |
| `ToPickerBlock`, address only | `address`, `onAddressChange`, optional `addressPlaceholder` and `onScan`; no `tokens` |
| `ToPickerBlock`, with chains | add `tokens` and `onSelect` |
| `ToPickerBlock`, without chains | add `chainFilter={false}` |
| `FromPickerBlock`, not connected | `wallet={{connected:false}}`, `onConnect`, and `generateAddress` / `onGenerateAddressChange` for the switch |
| `FromPickerBlock`, connected | `wallet={{connected:true, address}}`; `onDisconnect` shows the sign-out button, omit it where signing out does not belong |
| `FromPickerBlock`, whitelist | no `wallet`: the token list alone |

- **Generate address** is a switch, not an action: it reports the new value and the user goes on to pick a chain and an asset. The host then shows the address to send to, for example with `WalletAddress`, or `SwapPanelBlock`'s receive view.
- **Scanning** and **connecting** belong to the host: HIG ships no QR scanner and no wallet connection. `onScan` and `onConnect` only report the press.
- **Search** matches the token's name, symbol, chain and `keywords`, so put the contract address in `keywords` to make a pasted address find its token.
- **Keyboard** on web: with focus in the search field, the arrow keys move through the list and Enter selects.
- **No search.** `search={false}` leaves out the search field, for a list of two or three tokens such as a withdraw picker. On web no row is highlighted until the pointer moves over one, because there is no arrow-key cursor; each row is still a button in the tab order.
- **Balances.** A row draws a balance only when it is above zero; `zeroBalances` also draws a known zero, for a list of every asset the account can hold. A token's `unitsSuffix` follows its balance figure (`1.005 HYPE`), and its `detail` replaces the chain on the second line, for a list whose tokens are not told apart by chain; the search still matches the chain.
- **Input attributes.** `searchInputProps` and, on `ToPickerBlock`, `addressInputProps` reach the inputs: on web any `<input>` attribute, including `name`, `autoComplete`, `data-1p-ignore`, `data-lpignore`, `data-form-type`, a mono `className` and `onFocus` / `onBlur`; on native any `TextInput` prop, including `onFocus` / `onBlur`, `textContentType` and `style`. The value and its change handler stay the block's. A host `onKeyDown` on the web search runs first; the list's arrow keys and Enter then run unless it called `preventDefault()`. `searchRef` and `addressRef` give the host the input itself, for example to register it with a bottom sheet's keyboard handling or to focus it.
- **Visible labels.** `searchLabel` and `addressLabel` draw a visible label over the field (a `Field` label, 8 units above it on native and the field gap on web), which then names the field in place of the built-in hidden name. Without them the fields are named by the built-in “Search tokens” and “Recipient”, as before.
- **Selected row and row attributes (0.8.0).** The row of `selected` is marked `aria-current="true"` on web (native already read it as `accessibilityState.selected`), besides its drawn “Selected”. `tokenRowProps={token => props}` gives each token's row host attributes: on web `data-*`, `id`, `title` and `aria-describedby` (type `PickerRowProps`; HIG keeps the row's type, class, state and handlers), on native `testID` (replacing `swap-token-<id>`), `nativeID` and `accessibilityHint`.
- **Inside a host sheet (native).** The list is a bounded `FlatList`. `listComponent` renders the rows through the host's list instead, such as `BottomSheetFlatList` from `@gorhom/bottom-sheet`, so it scrolls inside the sheet and hands drags to it; the host's component receives HIG's bounded `style` and may override it. `SwapHostContext`, now exported from `@bloxwap/hig/native/pickers` and the `blocks` aggregate, does the same for every picker under it, as `SwapSheet` uses it; `listComponent` on the block wins.

### AccountBlock

`AccountBlock` shows one account: a header with Back on the leading edge, the title in the centre and an optional action on the trailing edge; under it the total on the leading edge and the deposit action on the trailing edge; then the holdings as `AssetBalanceRow` capsules 8 units apart. It is available from `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/account-block`, `@bloxwap/hig/native/account-block` and the `blocks` aggregates.

```tsx
<AccountBlock assets={holdings} onBack={goBack} onShowAddress={openAddress} onDeposit={openDeposit}
  onAssetSelect={asset => open(asset.id)}/>
```

- **Account address.** `onShowAddress` puts a QR button on the trailing edge of the header, above the deposit action. The host shows the address when it is pressed, for example in a `Dialog` or `Sheet` with `WalletAddress`; the card never holds the address. `headerAction` replaces the QR button with a host control.
- **Assets.** An `AccountAsset` is `{id, name, symbol}` plus optional `icon` (an image URL or a host element), `balance` (token units), `price` (USD per unit) and `value` (dollars). The value shown is `value`, or `balance × price` when both are known, or the unknown dash.
- **Pinned dollar balance.** The asset whose symbol is `pinnedSymbol` (default `USDC`) is always the first row and is always shown: when the account does not hold it, the row reads $0.00. It shows its dollar value alone, because its units are the same figure.
- **Order.** Every other asset follows by dollar value, largest first. Unknown values come last and ties sort by name. The host does not sort. `accountRows(assets, pinnedSymbol)` returns the same order for a host-drawn list.
- **Total.** `balance` is the total in dollars. Without it the card sums the asset values; any unknown or nonfinite constituent makes the total unknown. `null` reads as unknown.
- **Deposit.** `onDeposit` shows the primary action beside the total. `depositLabel` replaces the built-in text, for example with Add funds.
- **Header.** `title` replaces the built-in “Account”. `onBack` shows Back; `headerAction` is the trailing control. The title stays centred with either, both or neither. `stickyHeader` pins it (see [pinned headers](#pinned-headers); native also takes `stickyHeaderBackground` and `scrollComponent`), and `headingId` names its heading.
- **Rows.** `onAssetSelect` makes each row a button that reports its asset. Without it the rows are plain. `selectable: false` on an asset keeps that one row plain.
- **Units.** `units: false` on an asset draws no units line, for a ledger whose units are the same figure as its value. `unitsOptions` formats an asset's units (at most six fraction digits by default) and `unitsSuffix` follows them (` PAPER`). An asset whose value is unknown but whose `balance` is known shows its units as the headline figure, with no second line, in place of the unknown dash. `unknownValue: 'dash'` on the asset keeps the unknown dash over the units instead, for a value that is still loading, such as a price not yet read.
- **Tags.** An asset's `tag` is short muted host text under its figures (`AssetBalanceRow tag`), such as Perp, Spot or Staked, so two rows of the same symbol read apart without changing the symbol line.
- **Order.** `order: 'given'` keeps the rows after the pinned one in the order passed, for a ledger with a fixed order; the default `'value'` sorts them as above. A section's own `order` overrides the block's. `accountRows(assets, pinnedSymbol, {order, pinnedId})` and `accountSectionRows` take the same options.
- **Pin by id.** `pinnedId` pins the asset with that id, for a dollar ledger whose symbol is not unique (two USDC rows); without a match the `pinnedSymbol` match applies as before. A section's own `pinnedId` overrides the block's. A row pinned by symbol shows its value alone; a row pinned by id keeps its own `units` setting.
- **Sections.** `sections=[{id, title, total, assets}]` replaces the flat list with titled groups in the order given, 24 units apart, each a region named by its title with its rows 8 apart under a heading line that carries the group's `total` on the trailing edge (the sum of its asset values when left out; `null` reads as unknown). Within a group the pinned asset leads only when the group holds it (no $0.00 placeholder), then the rest by value. A group with no assets is not drawn. Without `balance` the block total is the sum of the totals of the groups that are drawn, so a group with no assets adds nothing even when it has a `total`; when any drawn group's total is `null`, the block total is unknown too. `onAssetSelect` then also receives the group: `onAssetSelect(asset, section)`. `accountSectionRows` and `accountSectionTotal` return the same order and total for a host-drawn list.

```tsx
<AccountBlock onDeposit={openDeposit} onAssetSelect={(asset, section) => open(section?.id, asset.id)} sections={[
  {id: 'exchange', title: t.exchange, assets: [{id: 'perp', name: t.perp, symbol: 'USDC', value: 500, units: false}]},
  {id: 'wallet', title: t.wallet, assets: walletAssets},
]}/>
```

- **Live numbers.** The total, every section total, every value and every units figure update through `AnimatedNumberReadout`, as in the swap card.
- **Ownership.** The card never reads a wallet, fetches a price or moves funds.

### TokenActionBlock

`TokenActionBlock` is the screen for one token: the same header as `AccountBlock` with the ticker as its title, two `BarMark` bars, then the actions. The bars are read-only, so they are drawn without a card (`surface={false}`) and sit directly on the screen, as in `ManagePositionBlock`. The first bar is titled with the token's `name`, shows the total holding in dollars on its trailing edge, and divides among `assets`, the places the token is held (Staked, Core, Paper). The second is the same bar titled Chains that shows how many chains hold a balance and divides among `chains`. It is available from `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/token-action-block`, `@bloxwap/hig/native/token-action-block` and the `blocks` aggregates.

```tsx
<TokenActionBlock symbol="HYPE" name="Hyperliquid" onBack={goBack}
  assets={[{label: 'Staked', value: 320}, {label: 'Core', value: 239}, {label: 'Paper', value: 200}]}
  chains={[{label: 'Base', value: 120}, {label: 'Hyperliquid', value: 639}]}
  actions={[{id: 'send', onSelect: send}, {id: 'receive', onSelect: receive},
            {id: 'stake', onSelect: stake}, {id: 'unstake', onSelect: unstake}]}/>
```

- **Bars.** `assets` and `chains` are `BarMark` elements: `{label, value}` plus optional `tone`, `color`, `detail` and `id`. Use one unit for both, usually dollars. `chainsTitle` replaces the built-in “Chains”. A `detail` can be a live figure (`{value, options, prefix, suffix}`), which moves place by place on both platforms, like the total.
- **Actions only.** Both bars are optional: leave out `chains` to draw the assets bar alone, `assets` to draw the chains bar alone, or both for a card of commands with no breakdown. `name` is needed only with `assets`; the ticker stands in without it.
- **Note.** `note` is a line under the actions, for example why some are missing on a view-only account; `noteTone='warning'` or `'negative'` makes it a tinted capsule, as in `SwapPanelBlock`. It sits 8 units under the actions, or 16 under the bars when there are no actions.
- **Total.** `value` is the holding in dollars. Without it the card sums the asset values; any unknown or nonfinite constituent makes the total unknown. `null` reads as unknown. It updates place by place.
- **Units headline.** For a token with no dollar value, `units` (token units) with `value` left out or `null` takes the total's place on the assets bar, followed by `unitsSuffix` (` BLOX`) and formatted with `unitsOptions` (at most six fraction digits by default). It updates place by place, and an unknown `units` (`null`) reads as the dash. With a dollar `value` the total is shown as before.
- **Chain count.** The chains bar shows the number of chains with a balance above zero.
- **Actions.** Each action is `{id, onSelect}` plus optional `label`, `disabled` and `intent`. The ids `send`, `receive`, `stake` and `unstake` take a built-in translated label; any other id needs `label`. They render in the order given, full width, 8 units apart and 16 below the bars. Leave out the actions a token does not support.
- **Intent.** Actions default to `secondary`, because the card offers equal choices. Set `intent: 'primary'` on at most one, or `'destructive'` for something like a burn.
- **Header.** `onBack` shows Back and `headerAction` is the trailing control, as in `AccountBlock`, with the same `stickyHeader` and `headingId`.
- **Ownership.** The card never reads a wallet or starts a flow. Each action only reports the press; the host opens its send, receive, stake or unstake screen, for example a `SwapPanelBlock`.

### ConfirmBlock

`ConfirmBlock` is the last look before a send, usually in a sheet after the amount and destination are chosen: the header, the amount with its ticker as the headline, the destination address and the network as plain lines, a warning, then Cancel and the confirming action side by side. It is available from `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/confirm-block`, `@bloxwap/hig/native/confirm-block` and the `blocks` aggregates.

```tsx
<ConfirmBlock amount={2.5} symbol="HYPE" address={destination} network="HyperEVM"
  busy={sending} onBack={goBack} onConfirm={send} onCancel={close}/>
```

- **Amount.** `amount` is in token units and is formatted with `amountOptions` (at most six fraction digits by default); `symbol` follows it, smaller and muted. `null` reads as unknown. `amountLabel` names the figure for assistive technology (“Amount: 2.5”, then the ticker); without it the figure is read alone.
- **Destination.** The details are information, not controls, so they are plain lines with no card or row container: a muted label on the leading edge and the value on the trailing edge. `address` is shown in full beside the built-in “To”, always as two rows of monospace split at the middle, left to right in every locale. The characters people compare are emphasised in the text colour, the first 4 (6 when the address starts with `0x`) and the last 4, and the rest is muted, as in `VerticalAddress`. Assistive technology reads the plain address. Never shorten it here. `network` is the value of the Network line. `details` adds lines under it, such as a fee: `{label, value}` plus `valueLabel` for a value that is not text. Native reads each line as one (“To, 0x…”). Values wrap by default; `oneLineDetails` keeps the Network line and each of `details` on one line, the label whole and the value truncated with an ellipsis (still read in full), while the address keeps its two rows. A value that is not text truncates the same way when it is inline text content (a `span` on web, a `Text` on native, where it is set inside the line's one-line text).
- **Warning.** The warning is on by default: the built-in heading “Double-check the address.” and a sentence that names the token and the network. `warningTitle` and `warning` replace them with host text; `warning={null}` draws none. It is a note, not an alert: it is there before the user acts, so nothing is announced on its own. Something that does need announcing, such as a fee that cannot be read or a send that failed, goes in `notice`: the host's node (usually an error `Alert`, which announces itself) drawn as given between the warning and the actions. Nothing by default.
- **Actions.** `onConfirm` reports the press on the confirming action, which is the primary button; `confirmLabel` replaces the built-in “Confirm Send”. `onCancel` shows Cancel on its leading side (`cancelLabel`), the two sharing the row equally as in `TargetBlock`; without it the confirming action takes the full width. `confirmDisabled` draws the confirming action unavailable, and `cancelDisabled` draws Cancel unavailable without `busy` (0.8.0). The two actions need not be Cancel and Confirm: a refusal that offers two ways forward, such as “Export account” beside “Withdraw first” with “Delete anyway” as the tertiary action, passes them as `cancelLabel` / `onCancel` and `confirmLabel` / `onConfirm`.
- **Busy.** While `busy`, the confirming action shows a spinner and ignores presses, and Back and Cancel are unavailable, so a send that is being signed cannot be left half way. `cancelWhileBusy` keeps Back, Cancel and the tertiary action available during the wait, for one the host can abandon, such as a wallet signature for turning on an experiment. `backWhileBusy` keeps only Back available, for an action that finishes whether or not the user stays, such as closing a position: the user may leave the pane, but Cancel and the tertiary action stay held, since they cannot stop it.
- **Header.** `title` replaces the built-in “Confirm Send”. `onBack` shows Back and `headerAction` is the trailing control, with the same `stickyHeader` and `headingId` as the other blocks. `backProps` passes attributes to Back as `ScreenHeader` takes them: web `<button>` attributes such as a `data-testid`, native Pressable props such as `{android_disableSound: true}` (0.8.0).
- **Test IDs per action (0.8.0).** `confirmTestID`, `cancelTestID` and `tertiaryAction.testID` set each action's `data-testid` on web; on native they replace `<testID>-confirm`, `<testID>-cancel` and `<testID>-tertiary` one by one, so a host keeps its own IDs (`delete-account-withdraw`, `delete-account-export`, `delete-account-anyway`) under one prefix.
- **Confirmations that are not sends.** Every send part is optional, so the block also draws the last look before signing out, deleting an account, closing positions or turning on an experiment. Leave out `amount` for no headline (an amount without `symbol` draws the figure alone), and `address` and `network` for no lines; without `address` there is no built-in warning (pass `warning` for one). `children` is what is being confirmed, drawn as given under the header and any send parts, in a column 12 apart: usually a muted `Text`, an `Alert` or a `ListGroup` of figures. `points` adds a bulleted list in the muted colour under it, such as what deleting an account loses. `confirmIntent='destructive'` fills the confirming action with the negative role, for an action that deletes or ends something; `confirmIntent='warning'` fills it with the warning role (the `Button` `warning` intent, dark label), for an action that goes ahead despite a caution, such as sending past a `warning`. `tertiaryAction={{label, onSelect, tone, disabled}}` adds a full-width ghost button 8 under Cancel and Confirm, such as “Delete anyway”; `tone='destructive'` draws its label in the negative colour, and it is unavailable while `busy`.

```tsx
<ConfirmBlock title="Delete account?" confirmLabel="Delete" confirmIntent="destructive"
  points={[keysErased, profileRemoved]} onCancel={close} onConfirm={remove}>
  <Text tone="muted">This cannot be undone.</Text>
</ConfirmBlock>
```

- **Native test IDs.** `testID` (default `confirm`) prefixes `-header`, `-back`, `-title`, `-amount`, `-symbol`, `-to`, `-network`, `-detail-<index>`, `-body`, `-point-<index>`, `-warning`, `-confirm`, `-cancel` and `-tertiary`.
- **Ownership.** The block never validates an address, reads a wallet or sends. The host checks the address before showing the block, and signs and sends on `onConfirm`.

### LanguageBlock

`LanguageBlock` is the screen for choosing the app's language: the same header as `AccountBlock`, a search field, then each language as a row. It is available from `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/language-block`, `@bloxwap/hig/native/language-block` and the `blocks` aggregates.

```tsx
<LanguageBlock value={locale} onSelect={language => setLocale(language.code)} onBack={goBack}
  languages={[
    {code: 'en', name: 'English', description: 'English', flag: '/flags/us.svg'},
    {code: 'fr', name: 'Français', description: 'French', flag: '/flags/fr.svg'},
  ]}/>
```

- **Languages.** A `LanguageOption` is `{code, name}` plus optional `description` and `flag`. `name` is the language in its own words and `description` is the reader's name for it, shown muted underneath. `flag` is round artwork: an image URL or a host element; without it the row shows the first two letters of the code. Rows keep the host's order.
- **Selection.** `value` is the `code` in use; its row shows a check on the trailing edge. `onSelect` reports the language pressed. The host applies it and navigates.
- **Search.** The field at the top filters by name, description and code, ignoring case and accents, so `francais` finds Français. No match shows the built-in “No results”. On web the arrow keys move through the matches from the field and Enter chooses the highlighted one, or the only one. `search={false}` leaves the field out for a short list. `filterLanguages(languages, query)` returns the same matches.
- **Header.** `title` defaults to the built-in “Language”. `onBack` shows Back and `headerAction` is the trailing control, as in `AccountBlock`, with the same `stickyHeader` and `headingId`. `description` is a muted line under the header.
- **Disabled.** `disabled` dims the rows, marks them unavailable and ignores presses (and Enter from the search field on web), for example while a change is being applied.
- **Accessibility.** The rows are a radio group named by the title; each row is a radio that reads the language's name and description, and carries its `code` as the language of its name.

### ManagePositionBlock

`ManagePositionBlock` is the screen for one open position. Under the shared header it draws a `BarMark` and a `BarPnl`, the host's actions as rows, and the position itself. The two bars are read-only, so they are drawn without a card (`surface={false}`) and sit directly on the screen; only the things a person can press look like surfaces. It is available from `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/manage-position-block`, `@bloxwap/hig/native/manage-position-block` and the `blocks` aggregates.

```tsx
<ManagePositionBlock labels={t.position} mode="Demo" side="long"
  entry={64700} mark={64696} liquidation={63082} margin={10} notional={399.98}
  actions={[{id: 'stop-loss', label: t.stopLoss, onSelect: openStopLoss},
            {id: 'take-profit', label: t.takeProfit, onSelect: openTakeProfit},
            {id: 'close', label: t.close, onSelect: openClose}]}
  position={{name: 'Bitcoin', icon: btc, leverage: 40, size: 0.006182, pnl: -0.0247, pnlPercent: -0.0025}}
  onBack={goBack}/>
```

- **Labels.** Every word in this block is a trading term, so the host supplies all of them through `labels`: `title`, `margin`, `notional`, `liquidation`, `mark`, `entry`, `long`, `short`, and one sentence that receives a formatted figure, `toLiquidation(percent)`. HIG ships no default text here, in keeping with the rule that built-in strings contain no glossary term.
- **Margin bar.** The first element is a `BarMark` titled with the margin mode from `mode` (Demo, Cross, Isolated), or the margin label without one, and reads the share left before liquidation on its trailing edge, for example 99.8% to liquidation. Its bar is the margin in the info role against the rest of the notional in the positive role, so a 40× position shows a one-fortieth sliver of margin. The legend names both with their dollar amounts.
- **Price bar.** The second element is a `BarPnl` (see the financial data chapter): one bar that places the liquidation, mark and entry prices, coloured by whether the position is in profit or loss, with the three prices under it in price order. It takes its three labels from `labels.liquidation`, `labels.mark` and `labels.entry`. `positionCorridor({side, entry, mark, liquidation})` still returns the share left before liquidation that the first element shows. In profit the bar and the mark price take the positive role and the first element reads 100% to liquidation; the catalog's `profit` example shows it.
- **Prices.** The three prices are drawn compact, with no extra zeros: `$64,700`, `$142.96`, `$0.4821`. `priceOptions` changes the format, for example to another currency.
- **Actions.** Each action is `{id, label, onSelect}` plus optional `disabled`. Together they are one `ListGroup`: rows with a chevron that share one rounded container, such as Stop Loss, Take Profit and Close. The host supplies the labels and opens its own flow.
- **Action values.** An action can take a trailing `value` before its chevron: host text, or a live figure `{value, options, prefix, suffix}` that updates place by place. `tone` colours it `positive`, `negative` or `muted` (the default is the muted value colour). Use it for a resting order on the row that manages it, such as a take profit set at $66,000. The row reads its label and value as one button.
- **Position.** `position={{name, icon, leverage, size, pnl, pnlPercent}}` draws the row under the actions: artwork, the name over an arrow for the side with the leverage and size, and profit and loss in dollars over its percent.
