- **Label tone.** `tone='destructive'` paints the label in the negative role, for a row such as Delete account; `tone='muted'` paints it muted, for a task that is done. The words still carry the meaning.
- **Choices.** `selected` turns a row into one choice of a list that selects and closes, such as a signing account or an avatar: `true` draws a check on the trailing edge in place of the chevron and marks the row (`aria-current` on web, `accessibilityState.selected` on native). With `selected` set, true or false, the row draws no chevron unless `disclosure` asks for one, so the unselected rows of the list stay bare.
- **Busy.** `busy` puts a spinner where the disclosure was, marks the row busy (`aria-busy`, `accessibilityState.busy`), adds HIGProvider `messages.busy` (or `busyLabel`; `''` omits it) to a selectable row's name as `Button` does, and ignores presses. The row is not dimmed and keeps its focus.
- **Disclosure.** `disclosure` picks the glyph of a row with `onSelect` or `href`: `chevron` (the default), `external` (an arrow pointing up and away, for something that opens outside the app; it mirrors in right-to-left layouts like the chevron) or `none`. The glyph is decorative, so a row that leaves the app says so in its label when that matters.
- **Switch rows.** `checked` (or `defaultChecked`) with `onCheckedChange`, and no `onSelect` or `href`, makes the whole row a switch: a press anywhere on it toggles the switch drawn on the trailing edge, the switch is named by `label`, and `disabled` or `busy` stop it. On web the switch input stays the one named control for keyboard and assistive technology, named by the row's visible label through `aria-labelledby`, so the name is drawn and read once (0.8.0: the switch's own label no longer carries a second, visually hidden copy, which screen readers read as text after the switch); the host's press decoration covers the row as one `'switch'` layer. On native the row is one 48dp switch element. A static row with a `Switch` in `trailing` still works as before.
- **Numbers in a value.** A number readout in `value` (`Usd`, `NumberReadout`, `AnimatedNumberReadout`) is drawn in the row's interface face with tabular digits, not the mono face, so it matches the row's text values (web: `.hig-list-row-value .hig-number` inherits the face; native readouts already use the provider face unless the host passes a mono `style`).
- **Ref and pass-through.** The ref reaches the row's element (the button, link or `div` on web; the Pressable or View on native). On web every other attribute, such as `data-*` and `aria-*`, reaches that element. On native the row takes the other Pressable props, such as `android_disableSound`, `hitSlop`, `onLongPress` and `accessibilityHint`, beside `testID`.
- **Disabled.** `disabled` dims the row and blocks `onSelect`, `href` and the switch.
- **Group heading.** `title` may be host text or an element, such as a live count. `titleAccessory` puts host content after it, such as `2/3` or an aggregate figure: it is read with the heading while the group stays named by the title alone (inside the `<h3>` on web; on native the title and accessory are one header element named by both). `action={{label, onSelect, disabled}}` draws a text action, such as Cancel all, on the trailing edge of the heading; it is a button named by its label, 44 units tall on web without growing the heading and at least 48dp each way on native through `minWidth` and `hitSlop`, outside the header element, and takes the `'button'` press decoration on web. `intro` holds host content between the heading and the rows, such as a note or a field; a group with `intro` and no rows draws no row container.
- **Anatomy.** Rows are 56 units high with 20 units of inline padding. The group has a 20-unit radius; the first and last rows take its corners. A group without a `title` is the container alone. Stack groups 24 units apart: that gap is what separates one group from the next, where rows inside a group are 2 apart.
- **Accessibility.** With a `title` the group is a region named by it, and its rows are a list. A selectable row is one button named by its label, description and value. The chevron, check, spinner, external arrow and `leading` are decorative; selected and busy are exposed as states. A static native row with `selected` or `busy` is one element named by its label and value so the state is read, unless it has `trailing` content, which stays its own target (the state is then not announced on the row). A busy linked row on web stays the same `<a>` (`aria-disabled`, not navigating), so focus stays on it.

## When to use and examples

Do: expose current location and keep deep-link ownership with host. Don’t: replace native back with a browser history dependency.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Tabs use selected states and one active panel; DOM Arrow/Home/End keys, RTL-aware arrow mapping. Only the selected tab is in the Tab order. The active DOM panel is a tab stop only when its first content is not focusable. When the panel starts with a focusable element, such as the `InstallCommand` `pre`, that element is the single stop after the tab list. Panels that start with text keep `tabIndex=0` so their content stays reachable. Server and hydration markup render every panel with `tabIndex=0`; on the client a layout effect corrects the shown panel before paint, in the same commit that shows it, so a panel that starts with a focusable element is never an extra stop after a tab switch. Accordion uses details/summary on DOM and expanded Pressable on RN. Search results are visible action lists; keyboard shortcuts belong to host.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Breadcrumb is DOM-specific; native host routes plus BackButton are supported alternatives. No fuzzy-search engine, command palette shortcut hijacking or native hardware-keyboard certification.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Overlays
Source: docs/components/overlays.md

# Overlays

Dialogs, sheets, menus, and contextual help with explicit dismissal and focus behavior.

Includes `Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `Sheet`, and `Menu`. `Popover` and `Tooltip` are web-only; native help uses persistent `HelpText`.

Issue #16. Entry: `overlay`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig/react/overlay` or `@bloxwap/hig/native/overlay` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | Controlled `open` and `onOpenChange`, plus `title`, `description`, and `children`. The web `trigger` is one element that accepts a ref. `closeLabel` overrides the Close button (`Sheet`, web `Popover`, native `Menu` and `GestureSheet` too); web `AlertDialog` takes `cancelLabel`. Defaults come from HIGProvider [`messages`](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/localization/#built-in-component-strings). |
| Web host composition | `title` remains required; `titleHidden` keeps its accessible name when the host renders a visible heading in the card. `description` is optional; `descriptionHidden` keeps supplied supporting text available to assistive technology. `contentRef` reaches the actual modal element. `contentProps` accepts layout classes/styles, DOM attributes and Radix focus/Escape/outside events; HIG retains ownership of the dialog id, role, naming associations, locale, direction, children and mounting behavior. Owned props and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` are filtered at runtime for JavaScript callers too; the caller's object is left unchanged. |
| Web close control | Omit `closeButton` for the current translated action, pass a ref-capable button element for a custom control, or pass `null` when the host supplies its own explicit dismissal action. Custom controls are composed with Radix Close; disabled buttons and `event.preventDefault()` retain their normal behavior. `closeLabel`/`cancelLabel` label only the default action. |
| Optional web `GestureSheet` | A separate Vaul modal root owns real drag, optional fixed snap points, scroll handoff and focus scope. The Dialog title/description, trigger, close control and `contentRef` contracts apply. For fixed detents, `backendProps` retains typed Vaul flags and snap-point options. For opt-in content sizing, use top-level `enableDynamicSizing` with optional `maxDynamicContentSize` and omit Vaul snap props. `contentProps` retains host layout, DOM data attributes, focus/Escape/outside events and pointer capture events. `handleProps`/`handleRef` customize the actual backend handle; `handle={false}` omits it. `overlayProps` observes outside-pointer actions or retains host overlay styling. `labelledBy` (0.8.0) names the sheet by a heading inside it, such as a block's `headingId`: the sheet takes `aria-labelledby` with that id, and its own `title` stays for the backend but is visually hidden and hidden from assistive technology, so the sheet's name is read once. |
| Native focus targets | `initialFocusRef` and `returnFocusRef` accept live focus targets. Initial focus defaults to the title; the host supplies the trigger ref (Menu and Select pass their own trigger). |
| `Menu` | `label` and items with `label`, optional `disabled`, and `onSelect`. |
| Web `Popover` | `label` is the text of the built-in trigger, a secondary Button, and `children` the content, followed by a Close button (`closeLabel`). 0.8.0, all optional with unchanged defaults: `open` / `onOpenChange` control it (or `defaultOpen` with its own state); `trigger` is the host's own trigger, one element that accepts a ref and spreads its props, such as an `IconButton` or a badge `<button>`, and `label` then names the popover (`aria-label` on its content); `openOnHover` also opens it while a mouse rests on the trigger, without moving focus, and closes it 150ms after the pointer leaves both the trigger and the popover, unless a click on the trigger pinned it open (the click that follows a hover does not toggle it shut; Escape, a press outside or a second trigger click closes a pinned one; touch and pen keep press to open); `hideClose` leaves out the Close button, for information the user dismisses with Escape, a press outside or the trigger; `testID` is the content's `data-testid`; `tone` (`info`, `positive`, `warning` or `negative`, type `PopoverTone`) tints the surface from that token role, a 12% wash over the popover fill, a 40% stroke and a soft 24px glow, as `data-tone` on the content (the role's colour is `--hig-popover-tone`, which the host may set in `style` for a colour outside the roles, such as a gold badge's tint); `className` adds classes after `hig-popover` and `style` adds inline style after the theme's variables, for a host surface treatment. Type `PopoverProps`. |
| Optional native `GestureSheet` | `contentMode='default'` scrolls the title, optional description, children and Close action. `contentMode='custom'` provides an unpadded content container; fixed mode is full-height while dynamic mode reports intrinsic content height. The host owns custom header, back/close actions, safe-area content padding and scrolling. `title` remains required as the accessible name. Pass `titleRef` attached to the caller's accessible heading to focus it on open; without it, the sheet focuses its visually hidden title. `labelledBy` (0.8.0) takes the `nativeID` of a heading inside the sheet, such as a block's `headingId`, and sets `accessibilityLabelledBy` on the sheet's content (Android; iOS keeps `title`). |

Native `Dialog` and its aliases support `contentMode='custom'`: host content/actions, required `title`, one HIG Modal owning Back, accessibility escape and focus. `titleRef` targets the host heading (otherwise hidden); `initialFocusRef` overrides it, `returnFocusRef` targets the trigger. Rejected close retains focus.

`stageComponent` accepts `GestureHandlerRootView`; `stageStyle`/`stageTestID` configure it. `backdrop` supplies the scrim/action; `contentStyle`/`testID` configure the surface. Preserve accessible descendants and close policy; never nest Modals.

`animationType` defaults to `none`; reduced motion forces `none`. Animated iOS focus return waits for [iOS-only `onDismiss`](https://reactnative.dev/docs/modal#ondismiss); Android restores next frame. Keep mounted with `open={false}` through dismissal. Reopen/unmount cancels restoration.

A web card can keep its own visible heading and close geometry without replacing the modal's focus scope:

```tsx
<Dialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={(next) => {
    if (!next && pending) return;
    setOpen(next);
  }}
  title={t('reviewTitle')}
  titleHidden
  description={t('reviewDescription')}
  descriptionHidden
  contentRef={panelRef}
  contentProps={{ className: 'host-review-card', style: { maxWidth: 420 } }}
  closeButton={<button type='button' disabled={pending} aria-label={t('close')}>×</button>}
>
  <h2>{t('reviewTitle')}</h2>
  {reviewContent}
</Dialog>
```

Here `t`, `panelRef`, the card content and pending state belong to the host. The visible heading remains a real heading; the hidden Radix title supplies the modal's accessible name. An omitted description removes its ARIA association instead of referencing a missing element. `contentProps.onOpenAutoFocus` and `onCloseAutoFocus` can prevent the default focus choice; the host then supplies the intended focus target. Other content events retain Radix cancellation semantics. Controlled `onOpenChange` can reject a pending wallet close without unmounting the dialog or moving focus back to the trigger. `AlertDialog` continues to prevent outside-pointer dismissal even when a host observes that event.

These web composition props apply to `Dialog`, `AlertDialog` and the static `Sheet` alias. They do not add drag gestures, detents or product keyboard heuristics to the static sheet.

For a native card stack, import `GestureSheet` from `@bloxwap/hig/native/gesture-sheet` and render the caller's cards directly:

```tsx
const titleRef = useRef<Text>(null);

<GestureSheet
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title={card.title}
  titleRef={titleRef}
  contentMode='custom'
  snapPoints={card.snapPoints}
  returnFocusRef={triggerRef}
>
  <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
    <Heading ref={titleRef}>{card.title}</Heading>
    {card.content}
    <Button onPress={() => setOpen(false)}>Done</Button>
  </View>
</GestureSheet>
```

Here `Text` and `View` are React Native types/components, and the host supplies the card state and its own accessible back/close labels. Custom content can use its own Gorhom scrollable or list without an outer scroll view. `snapPoints` may change while open: the current detent index is retained, or clamped to the highest remaining index if its detent was removed. Detent changes keep the sheet mounted and do not repeat open focus. Keep at least one sorted snap point; `initialIndex` applies to the next presentation. Focus return, Android Back, reduced-motion and dismissible backdrop behavior apply in both content modes.

For content-sized native cards, set `enableDynamicSizing` and omit `snapPoints`. This chooses one backend-measured detent rather than adding a competing fixed point. In custom mode HIG uses Gorhom's `BottomSheetView` to report intrinsic layout; it keeps a plain full-height `View` in fixed mode so nested scrollable registration stays with the caller. Choose the sizing mode for the presentation and avoid `flex: 1` or a full-height constraint on content that should determine its own height. Bound a long card's own scroll view. Default anatomy continues to use the backend scroll view. Mixed headers/footers and nested registered Gorhom scrollables compete for the backend's content-height measurement: their scroll content can replace the whole card height. Use host-measured fixed snap points for that composition. A content-sized card can instead bound a plain React Native `ScrollView` and set `enableContentPanningGesture={false}`, retaining the handle gesture and its own scroll gesture. This follows [Gorhom dynamic sizing](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/dynamic-sizing).

```tsx
<GestureSheet
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title='Size and leverage'
  contentMode='custom'
  enableDynamicSizing
  maxDynamicContentSize={availableHeight}
>
  <View>{contentSizedCard}</View>
</GestureSheet>
```

`maxDynamicContentSize` is an optional finite positive ceiling in native points; the backend container height is the default. The dynamic detent uses index `0`. Content growth, shrinkage and ceiling changes keep the presentation and card state, and height updates do not repeat open focus. Reduced motion applies HIG's no-animation backend policy; compositions that cannot safely report intrinsic height use the fixed-size alternative described above. A fixed sheet still requires a nonempty `snapPoints` list. `enableContentPanningGesture` passes through to the backend, allowing hosts with an independently scrolling list to disable content panning without changing their close/Back actions.

Close, Android Back and iOS accessibility escape use the same controlled close request. If the host rejects the request and controlled `open` remains true, HIG retries presentation after host state settles, retaining the card and its state instead of leaving a backend-dismissed but logically open sheet. Rejected closes and interrupted reopenings do not return focus or call `onDismiss`; hosts may use that settled callback to clear retained state only after an accepted close. `onHardwareBackPress` can consume Android Back (`true`) or defer to the host's nested-card dispatcher (`false`); omitting it keeps the default dismissal behavior. Accessibility escape is a platform contract, not a physical VoiceOver certification.

`topInset` and `bottomInset` default to safe-area values; use `0` for an intentional flush edge. `handleComponent` (including `null` for an overlay handle), `handleStyle`, `handleIndicatorStyle`, `backgroundComponent` and `backgroundStyle` retain host geometry and decoration. Sheet content is raised by default, so wells, list rows and quiet fills step up one shade against HIG's `overlay` fill; a host whose background paints the page `background` passes `raised={false}` so those fills match the page. The backend measures the rendered handle. Use `useColors()` in custom backgrounds. `modalRef` exposes the optional backend's imperative motion methods; hosts must keep controlled `open` in sync with `present()`/`dismiss()`. Focus return and settled `onDismiss` remain controlled by the HIG wrapper. `animateOnMount`, `animationConfigs` and `backdropComponent` retain host entry motion and backdrop styling; the reduced-motion mapping still applies. A custom backdrop must honor the host dismissal policy.

Keyboard policies are typed backend options: `keyboardBehavior`, `keyboardBlurBehavior` and `android_keyboardInputMode`. Defaults remain HIG's `interactive`, `restore` and `adjustResize`. A host retaining an existing Gorhom policy can explicitly pass `none` for blur and `adjustPan` on Android. See [Gorhom keyboard handling](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/keyboard-handling).

For a screen-level drawer that must prepare and retain its native children while closed, choose `presentation='inline'`. HIG uses the public persistent `BottomSheet` backend; the default remains `presentation='modal'` with `BottomSheetModal`. Inline content stays mounted at index `-1`, hidden from accessibility and touch, and registers no Back listener while closed. Opening and reopening keep child/controller/list state. Rejected closes restore the last open detent; accepted closes return focus and call `onDismiss` once after settling. Use `sheetRef` for the inline backend's actual `expand`, `close` and `snapToIndex` methods; `modalRef` is only available in modal mode and exposes `present`/`dismiss`. Imperative calls must keep controlled `open` in sync. `onChange` observes backend index/position/type after HIG updates its index, focus and close request; it cannot replace those handlers. This lets a host change its animation policy after the opening detent settles. `containerStyle` retains sibling overlay order. Hosts own screen-level backdrop/container layering for inline presentation. No modal portal provider is required for inline sheets.

## Optional web gesture backend

Install `vaul ^1.1.2` and import `GestureSheet` from `@bloxwap/hig/react/gesture-sheet`. Core `overlay`, Button and overlay-free blocks do not import or install Vaul. The backend supplies its own motion CSS when loaded; HIG's explicitly imported component CSS supplies scoped surface, text, geometry and reduced-motion rules. See the official [Vaul anatomy and API](https://vaul.emilkowal.ski/api) and the verified [1.1.2 source](https://github.com/emilkowalski/vaul/blob/v1.1.2/src/index.tsx).

```tsx
import {GestureSheet} from '@bloxwap/hig/react/gesture-sheet';

<GestureSheet
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={(next) => { if (next || !pending) setOpen(next); }}
  title={t('markets')}
  titleHidden
  contentMode='custom'
  contentRef={panelRef}
  contentProps={{ className: 'host-market-card', style: { bottom: viewportBottom, maxHeight: availableHeight } }}
  backendProps={{ handleOnly: false, repositionInputs: false, shouldScaleBackground: true, dismissible: !pending }}
  handleProps={{ style: { width: 100 }, preventCycle: true }}
  closeButton={null}
>
  <h2>{t('markets')}</h2>
  {hostHeaderAndScrollableContent}
</GestureSheet>
```

`contentMode='default'` provides padded, scrolling anatomy. `custom` leaves padding and scrolling with the host. The required accessible title remains available when hidden; render a real visible heading when the host card needs one. `closeButton={null}` means the host must retain an explicit accessible close/Back action. `handleOnly=true` requires the actual handle for dragging. Handle styles, classes and capture events are customizable; HIG filters replacements for the backend's handle pointer/click handlers, hidden state and reserved `data-vaul-*` attributes. Frozen caller prop objects remain unchanged.

Backend defaults remain Vaul's: `handleOnly=false`, `repositionInputs=true`, `shouldScaleBackground=false`, `dismissible=true` and `autoFocus=false`. Retain existing host flags explicitly. With `autoFocus=false`, hosts may use `contentProps.onOpenAutoFocus` to focus their heading/search control without requesting a software keyboard automatically. `shouldScaleBackground=true` requires the host's `[data-vaul-drawer-wrapper]` around the page. Physical `backendProps.direction` is independent of the provider's text direction. Fixed snap points retain Vaul's viewport geometry. The modal root stays controlled and modal; there is no second nested HIG Dialog root.

For content-sized sheets, set top-level `enableDynamicSizing` and omit `backendProps.snapPoints`, `snapPoint`, `activeSnapPoint`, `setActiveSnapPoint`, `fadeFromIndex`, and `snapToSequentialPoint`. Dynamic sizing and those Vaul snap props are mutually exclusive; fixed snapping remains the other explicit mode. `maxDynamicContentSize` is an optional finite positive content-height ceiling in CSS pixels; the viewport ceiling still applies. Content growth and shrinkage update the open sheet smoothly without remounting its children or repeating open focus. Reduced motion applies the new size without height animation, and unavailable measurement or animation capabilities use a static final size. Dynamic height applies to top/bottom sheets; other physical directions retain their static layout. The controlled dynamic example in the catalog uses real React and React Native content expansion/collapse.

The host can reject `onOpenChange(false)` while pending; HIG restores Vaul's last resting motion styles after a rejected drag without remounting card state. Use `dismissible=false` as well when pending should prevent dismissal attempts altogether. Backend `onAnimationEnd` is observed only when its reported state still matches controlled `open`, so rejected closes and stale opposite-state callbacks cannot clear retained card state. Programmatic state changes keep the backend's callback behavior. Reduced motion removes the sheet/overlay animation and transition; drag and fixed snap selection still work. Viewport constraints, editable-input blur policy, safe-area padding and product-specific keyboard accessory reserves stay in the host.

`scripts/gesture-sheet-browser-smoke.mjs` exercises the real Vaul backend in Chromium and WebKit: drag/scroll handoff, handle-only drag, controlled veto with retained input identity, nondismissible state, snap expansion, dynamic growth/shrink and capped scrolling, rapid resize interruption, focus/node identity, focus trap/Escape/return, viewport resizing, host styles/refs and reduced motion. Evidence in `evidence/web-gesture-sheet/` records the exact source baseline and dirty state. Desktop viewport resizing does not certify physical mobile software-keyboard behavior; that remains a host/device observation.

### Views that swap (`GestureSheetView`)

A sheet that walks through several views, such as choose, review and done, wraps them in `GestureSheetView` from the same entry and names the current one with `viewKey`:

```tsx
<GestureSheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Buy Bitcoin" titleHidden closeButton={null} enableDynamicSizing>
  <GestureSheetView viewKey={step}>
    {step === 'fees' ? <Fees/> : step === 'review' ? <Review/> : <Choose/>}
  </GestureSheetView>
</GestureSheet>
```

When `viewKey` changes, the old view fades and shrinks slightly out of the way without holding its space, the new view fades in at its own size, and the content-sized sheet moves to the new height at the same time. All three share one curve, `cubic-bezier(.26,.08,.25,1)`, with no spring and no overshoot: the old view and the height take 270ms and the new view 220ms, the values of Vaul's Dynamic Drawer. Going deeper and going back look the same, as in Vaul: there is no push or pop direction. The first view appears with the sheet. The outgoing view is inert and hidden from assistive technology while it leaves. Under reduced motion, and where the browser cannot animate, the views swap at once. Give every view its own way out, since `closeButton={null}` removes the built-in Close. The native preview engine has no view component: its content is swapped by the host and the sheet moves to the new height.

## Native sheet engine (preview)

`@bloxwap/hig/native/gesture-sheet-next` is HIG's own sheet for iOS and Android, written to replace the `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` backend behind `@bloxwap/hig/native/gesture-sheet`. It needs `react-native-reanimated`, `react-native-gesture-handler` and `react-native-safe-area-context`, and no sheet library. It is a preview: its arithmetic and lifecycle are tested, but it has not yet been measured on devices, so it sits beside the existing entry until it has.

```tsx
import {GestureSheet, GestureSheetHost, GestureSheetScrollView} from '@bloxwap/hig/native/gesture-sheet-next';

<GestureSheetHost>{/* once, around the screen */}
  <App/>
  <GestureSheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Markets" contentMode="custom" enableDynamicSizing>
    <GestureSheetScrollView>{rows}</GestureSheetScrollView>
  </GestureSheet>
</GestureSheetHost>
```

- **Why it stays smooth.** While the sheet moves, only its `translateY` and the backdrop's opacity change, both on the UI thread. Nothing is laid out per frame, whatever the content weighs. Opening, closing, a new detent set and content that changed height all become one spring. The surface is rasterised on Android (`renderToHardwareTextureAndroid`).
- **Sizing.** `snapPoints` are points or a percentage of the room under `topInset`, sorted for you, with `initialIndex` counted from the lowest. Fixed content is laid out once at the tallest detent, so at a lower detent its lower part is off screen, as in Vaul. `enableDynamicSizing` gives one detent as tall as the content, up to `maxDynamicContentSize`; when the content changes height the content is laid out at once and the sheet moves to the new height in 270ms.
- **Drag.** The whole sheet drags. A slow release takes the nearest detent, or closes past half way below the lowest; a flick moves one detent in its direction, or closes from the lowest. Above the top detent the sheet resists. A drag can be caught mid-motion.
- **Views that swap.** The engine animates the height only. A host that swaps its content gets the sheet moving to the new height in 270ms on the web sheet's curve; the content itself changes at once. A cross-fade and a push and pop by depth were built and measured on a Seeker, and dropped a frame per swap with a 12ms median frame at 120Hz, so they were removed.
- **Scrolling content.** Use `GestureSheetScrollView`: at the top detent it scrolls, a pull down from the top of the content moves the sheet, and below the top detent the drag moves the sheet. Bounce and overscroll are off.
- **Presentation.** `modal` (default) draws in the nearest `GestureSheetHost` and is mounted from opening until its closing motion ends; without a host it draws in place. `inline` draws where it is rendered and keeps its children mounted while closed.
- **Dismissal.** Drag, a backdrop press, Android Back, the accessibility escape and the default Close ask through `onOpenChange(false)`; a host that keeps `open` gets the sheet back at its detent. `dismissible={false}` blocks all of them. `onDismiss` fires once after an accepted dismissal has finished moving; `onChange(index)` fires when the sheet settles on a detent.
- **Keyboard.** iOS lifts the sheet over the keyboard. Android resizes the window, which the sheet reads as new room.
- **Differences from `native/gesture-sheet`.** No backend-typed props: `modalRef`, `sheetRef`, `handleComponent`, `backgroundComponent`, `backdropComponent`, `animationConfigs`, `containerStyle`, `keyboardBehavior` and `enableContentPanningGesture` are gone. `handle`, `backgroundStyle`, `backdropOpacity` and `testID` take their place. Modal sheets need `GestureSheetHost` in place of `BottomSheetModalProvider`. The sheet draws no shadow.

## When to use and examples

Do: repeat the order amount and give an explicit cancel action. Don’t: hide essential terms in hover help or execute confirm on open.

## States, interaction and accessibility

DOM Radix focus scopes restore trigger focus, trap modal focus, handle Escape and scroll locks. AlertDialog blocks outside-click dismissal. Menus use roving keyboard focus. Native Modal owns back and keyboard avoidance with scrollable content. Native overlays follow the host orientation: React Native's iOS Modal defaults `supportedOrientations` to portrait, so HIG passes every orientation and opening a Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, Menu or Select never rotates a landscape host back to portrait (observed on the iOS Simulator, `evidence/native-sim/ios/orientation/`). Hosts still decide which orientations the app supports.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Basic Sheet uses static Modal layout. The separate optional `@bloxwap/hig/native/gesture-sheet` entry provides GestureSheet with sorted snapPoints, initialIndex, dismissible, safe-area/keyboard configuration, reduced-motion mapping, native back, scoped listener cleanup and controlled dismissal deduplication. Rejected controlled closes re-present after host state settles. See `fixtures/native/gesture-sheet.tsx` and `index-gesture.js` for the real separate consumer; packed smoke compiles both Android/iOS entry points. Hosts provide GestureHandlerRootView, SafeAreaProvider and BottomSheetModalProvider. Required optional peers are Gorhom 5.2.14, Reanimated 4.1.1, Worklets 0.5.1 and Gesture Handler 2.28.0, pinned to Expo 54 bundledNativeModules rather than the newer monorepo native runtime. Backend configuration follows [Gorhom usage](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/modal/usage) and [props](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/props). Mocked wiring and Metro compilation are not gesture-detent or TalkBack certification. With TalkBack on the Android emulator, opening Dialog/AlertDialog/Sheet/Menu moves accessibility focus to the heading and Back closes the overlay; without a `returnFocusRef` TalkBack falls back to the first screen element, so hosts should pass the trigger. VoiceOver does not run in the iOS Simulator, so VoiceOver focus restoration remains a physical-device observation (`evidence/native-sim/`). Native help is persistent text; no hover tooltip or anchored popover claim.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/gesture-sheet.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/gesture-sheet-dynamic.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Real Chromium/WebKit cases cover fixed detents and dynamic growth/shrink; `evidence/web-gesture-sheet/` records the exact inputs. RN 0.88 iOS Simulator checks in `evidence/native-number-flow/ios-inline/` verify short→tall→restored geometry in normal and reduced motion, plus retained inline state and rejected/accepted dismissal. Physical hardware, VoiceOver/TalkBack speech, software-keyboard behavior and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Selection controls
Source: docs/components/selection.md

# Selection controls

Controls for choosing options, changing preferences, and adjusting values.

Includes `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `SegmentedControl`, `Filter`, `PresetGroup`, `Select`, and `Slider`. See the navigation guide for `Tabs`.

Issue #15. Entry: `selection`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig/react/selection` or `@bloxwap/hig/native/selection` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

Slider requires finite ordered bounds and a positive finite step. Displayed values and callbacks are clamped to the range. Choice keys must be unique. Controlled components retain their ownership for their mounted lifetime; remount to change ownership.

## API and anatomy

| Control | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Checkbox and switch | `checked`, `defaultChecked`, and `onCheckedChange`. Native `Switch` also takes `tone`, a token role (`action` default, `positive`, `negative`, `warning`, `info`, `buy`, `sell`) for the on track; raw colours are not accepted and fall back to `action`. On Android the thumb uses the `text` token, so the app theme accent never shows. `Switch` takes `hideLabel` on both platforms: the track is drawn alone and `label` still names the switch, for a switch whose row already shows its name (on native a `Switch` in a `ListRow` `trailing` would otherwise print its label twice). Native `Switch` takes `testID`. For a row the whole of which toggles, use a `ListRow` with `checked` and `onCheckedChange` ([navigation](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/navigation/#listgroup-and-listrow)). |
| Choice controls | `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange`. Options have `value`, `label`, and optional `disabled`. Native options also accept `description` (a second line) and `lang` (the label's BCP-47 language). |
| `Filter` | One row of filter capsules that scrolls sideways: `label` (accessible name, not drawn), `options` of `{value, label, icon?, disabled?}`, and `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`. Single choice with radio semantics. Each capsule leads with a circle showing the option's `icon` image or an empty ring; the chosen capsule inverts and a check draws into its circle. Use an empty-string option for “All”. Native `scrollComponent` replaces React Native's `ScrollView` with the host's (it receives the same props), such as a sheet library's scroll view that keeps sideways drags from the sheet on Android. `bleed` (0.8.0, web pixels or native units, default 0) runs the row out past its container by that much on each side and rests the first and last capsule that far in, so in a padded container the capsules are cut by the container's edge rather than by its padding: pass the container's side padding. On web it sets `--hig-filter-bleed`, which an ancestor can set instead. |
| `PresetGroup` (0.8.0) | Quick choices as chips in an equal-width grid that fills its container's width, such as order sizes ($10 … $1,000, Max) or leverage steps (1x … 40x): `options` of `{value, label, disabled?, testID?}` (`value` a string or a number), `value` (`null` selects none) or `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `columns` (chips per row; defaults to every option in one row, and fewer columns wrap the chips onto rows that keep the column width), `selectedIntent` (fill of the selected chip, `primary` by default), `disabled`, `label` (the group's accessible name, not drawn) and `testID`. Each chip is a HIG `Button` in the interface (sans) face, `secondary` at rest and `selectedIntent` when selected, and is dimmed when its option is `disabled`; a press on the selected or a dimmed chip does nothing. Web: a `role="group"` of toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`, each at least 44px tall at either density, an option's `testID` as its `data-testid`. Native: Buttons that read `accessibilityState.selected`, 44dp tall with a 48dp touch target, an option's `testID` (or `<testID>-<value>`) as its test ID. Each chip is named by its option's `label` (`accessibilityLabel`), and its label text is one line that shrinks to fit its column, down to 75% of its size, instead of wrapping (`numberOfLines={1}`, `adjustsFontSizeToFit`, `minimumFontScale={0.75}`), in Button's label colours; the label text takes the test ID `<chip testID>-label` (`<option testID>-label`, or `<testID>-<value>-label`) (0.8.0). The target is hit slop, 2dp above and below and 4dp (half the 8dp gap) to each side, so neighbouring chips' targets meet without overlapping and a chip squeezed under 48dp wide still takes its whole column pitch; Android's Fabric renderer counts a child's hit slop in its parent's overflow inset, so slop past the row's frame is reachable there unless a clipping ancestor (`overflow: 'hidden'`, a scroll view's edge) cuts it. React Native has no named group (VoiceOver never reads a container that is not an element), so native reads `label` as each chip's hint, after its label and state. A new choice plays the provider's `selection` feedback once the value lands, like `SegmentedControl`; `suppressFeedback` keeps it off for a host that plays its own cue. `TargetBlock` draws its presets with it. |
| `SegmentedControl` | Equal-width segments with a shared selection pill on web and native. Accepted selection changes slide the pill using the base motion token (260ms); repeated or rejected changes do not move it. Initial placement and reduced motion are immediate. No additional animation peer is required. `hideLabel` keeps `label` as the group's accessible name without drawing it (web: a visually hidden legend), for a control a heading or row already names. Native takes `testID`, and each segment takes `<testID>-<value>` (0.8.0), such as `trade-share-mode-video`, for end-to-end tests. Web takes the same `testID` as the fieldset's `data-testid`, and each segment's radio takes `<testID>-<value>` as its `data-testid` (0.8.0). On both platforms an option's own `testID` (`{value, label, testID}`, type `SegmentedControlOption`) replaces `<testID>-<value>` for that segment, also without a group `testID` (0.8.0). Native `segmentProps` are Pressable props for every segment, such as `{android_disableSound: true}` for a host that plays its own sound; HIG keeps its own name, role, state, target and press (0.8.0). On web each segment takes HIGProvider `pressDecoration` with `kind: 'segment'`, aimed at its radio, so a host's layer selects the segment once ([blocks](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/blocks/#shared-host-hooks)). |
| `Select` | A custom styled combobox/listbox on web. Arrow keys, Home/End, typeahead, Enter/Space, Escape and Tab support keyboard selection; disabled options cannot be selected. The popup escapes clipped containers while inheriting HIG theme and density. |
| `Slider` | `min`, `max`, `step`, and `value`; a visible `label` is required. Web uses the product slider’s white 20 × 14px oval thumb and 6px track. Native keeps the community backend’s platform thumb shape with HIG colors. The DOM keyboard focus ring is drawn inside the 48px range box, so it never paints over the label or the next control at comfortable or compact density. Native increment/decrement actions use HIGProvider `messages.increase`/`messages.decrease`. |

## When to use and examples

Do: control selection from accepted host state. Don’t: emit a success cue on every render or repeated slider value.

Native language pickers can keep the native name and a translated description in one radio row:

```tsx
<HIGProvider locale='en-US' fontFamiliesByScript={{
  latin: {400: 'BloxwapSansRegular'},
  ko: {400: 'BloxwapSansKRRegular'},
  zh: {400: 'BloxwapSansSCRegular'},
}}>
  <RadioGroup label='Language' value={language} onValueChange={setLanguage} options={[
    {value: 'ko', label: '한국어', description: 'Korean', lang: 'ko-KR'},
    {value: 'zh', label: '简体中文', description: 'Chinese', lang: 'zh-Hans'},
  ]}/>
</HIGProvider>
```

Register each face before passing its name. `Text` chooses `fontFamiliesByScript` by the label's glyphs, independently of the app locale; `lang` supplies `accessibilityLanguage` and resolves shared CJK punctuation. Descriptions use the app language. A script map selects the requested static weight, or its nearest registered weight; the existing `fontFamilies`/`fontFamily` remain the fallback. Explicit text `script` and style `fontFamily` override detection and registered family selection respectively. Native radios expose the label, supporting description as an accessibility hint, checked/disabled state and the explicit `activate` accessibility action; disabled rows reject both touch and accessibility activation. Per-option language is passed to React Native's `accessibilityLanguage`; pronunciation support depends on the platform and installed voices.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Checkboxes, radio controls and sliders retain native HTML keyboard semantics. Web Select renders HIG options in a custom popup; focus stays on its labeled combobox, which announces the active option. Escape dismisses without changing selection, and Tab dismisses while moving focus onward. RN Switch renders the OS track inside one labeled 48dp switch row (the row is the accessibility element and touch target); checkbox/radio use labeled Pressables with checked state. RN slider uses the optional community backend for the visual track and touch drag; a plain 48dp adjustable View owns the label, value and increment/decrement actions (5% steps) on iOS and Android because the backend's iOS Fabric view ignores accessibility increments and its Android SeekBar node measures 18dp. On Android the wrapper is the package's autolinked `HIGAdjustableView`, which also lists `ACTION_SET_PROGRESS` for Voice Access and Switch Access: a requested value snaps to `step`, clamps to `min`/`max`, updates the control once and is rejected while disabled. React Native's own `accessibilityActions` cannot express set-progress (custom names get synthetic ids and the progress argument is dropped). Without native linking (Expo Go) the wrapper is a plain View and set-progress is absent. The backend's native track height (18dp Android, 40pt iOS) still bounds direct touch drag; hosts needing a larger drag area should pad around the control. Select opens labeled native Modal choices and returns focus to its trigger.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Filter uses the same single-choice radio semantics: on web the arrow keys move the selection inside one tab stop, and the check, colour and image transitions stop under reduced motion. Use it to narrow a list by one facet when the options do not fit equal-width segments; the row scrolls instead of wrapping.

PresetGroup chips are toggle buttons, not radios: each is its own tab stop, Enter or Space takes it, and the selected one reads pressed (web) or selected (native). Use it for a handful of fixed amounts the user taps to fill a value, where the choices wrap into a grid and some may be unavailable now; use `SegmentedControl` for a short set of modes, and `Filter` to narrow a list.

SegmentedControl uses single-choice radio semantics on both platforms. Use it for a short set of related choices; use `RadioGroup` when options need longer descriptions. Web retains native radio keyboard behavior and a visible focus ring. The control is 44 units high on touch density (36 compact): a dark track with a lighter selected pill. Native segments extend their touch target to 48dp with vertical hit slop (6dp each side, 10dp at compact density, where segments are 28dp; 0.8.0: compact segments reached only 40dp before) and keep wrapping labels, per-option language and accessibility activation. The decorative pill is hidden from accessibility and does not intercept taps. Its position follows RTL direction and available width; native layout changes snap into place, and rapid selections interrupt the current animation. `HIGProvider reducedMotion` and the OS motion preference disable movement. A controlled pill follows the accepted `value`, including programmatic changes. An absent value has no pill.

Slider accessibility increment/decrement, set-progress and disabled rejection are verified on the iOS Simulator and Android emulator (`evidence/native-sim/`); tactile drag feel and haptic rate remain physical-device work; the slider backend is an optional native peer. Earlier native SegmentedControl gallery captures show the previous radio-list rendering and do not validate the new animation on physical devices.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/select.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/segmented-control.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/preset-group.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/preset-group.test.cjs`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, `tests/native/segmented-control.test.cjs`, `tests/native/language-options.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. `node scripts/select-browser-smoke.mjs` verifies the custom dropdown in Chromium/WebKit at mobile and desktop sizes, including RTL, clipped containers, keyboard selection and modal focus. `node scripts/segmented-control-browser-smoke.mjs` checks real animation frames, interruption, RTL, responsive alignment and reduced motion in Chromium/WebKit for React DOM and React Native Web; it does not certify iOS/Android rendering. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.

`SwitchRow` from `@bloxwap/hig/native/switch` (also `selection`) wraps an existing host row in one switch target. It takes the same required `label`, `checked` / `defaultChecked`, `disabled` and `onCheckedChange` contract as `Switch`, plus required noninteractive `children` and root Pressable props. Keep the visible label, description and track noninteractive: the root owns activation and hides the content from accessibility to avoid duplicate targets. Put the description in `accessibilityHint`. Root `style` supports pressed callbacks; `accessibilityState` preserves `busy` while HIG owns checked/disabled state. Disable the row explicitly during pending requests; busy alone is descriptive. The Expo web row supports Space, Enter and pointer activation. Tree shaking an ESM import of ordinary `Switch` removes this optional anatomy.


## Status & feedback
Source: docs/components/status.md

# Status & feedback

Visible progress, notifications, and recoverable states that keep people informed.

Includes `Badge`, `Alert`, `Callout`, `Toast`, `Toaster` with `toast()`, `Progress`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState`, `Avatar`, `StatusIndicator`, and `Confetti`.

Issue #18. Entry: `status`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig/react/status` or `@bloxwap/hig/native/status` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import. `Confetti` has its own entries, `@bloxwap/hig/react/confetti` and `@bloxwap/hig/native/confetti`; see [Confetti](#confetti).

Progress normalizes its value and maximum consistently for drawing and accessibility. Confetti is bounded to 500 particles per burst and eight simultaneous bursts per renderer (4,000 active particles); at most eight pre-mount requests wait. Overflow requests resolve immediately without drawing.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Badge` | Quiet label with an explicit `tone` (`neutral`, `positive`, `negative`, `warning`, or `info`; type `BadgeTone`) on both platforms (native since 0.8.0): the label in that token role over a 15% wash of it (web `.hig-badge[data-tone]`, native the role colour with a `26` alpha byte). Web adds standard span props and a forwarded span ref; native takes `testID`. The neutral default retains its appearance. `dot` (web and native, 0.8.0) draws a 6px status dot in the label colour on the leading edge (web `span.hig-badge-dot`, native a 6dp `View`), hidden from assistive technology, for a live or status pill such as “Off the tape”. Tone uses provider token roles and never infers meaning from text or a number's sign. Badge adds no live region; the host owns announcements. |
| `Alert` | `title`, `severity`, and an optional recovery `action`. Severity tints the fill and colours the title from a token role on web and native, with no stroke or glow: the surface mixed with 10% of the tone, at the Surface radius. `default` → neutral (6% of `text`, title in `text`), info → `info`, success → `positive`, warning → `warning`, error → `negative`. On native, `tone` swaps in another token role for an approved product accent, never a raw colour. `announce` (default `true`) speaks the alert when it appears or its words change: web gives it `role='status'` (`'alert'` for `error`), Android a live region, and iOS an explicit announcement. Pass `announce={false}` for an alert that is part of the screen from the start, such as a standing warning. On native a string or number child is drawn in a HIG `Text`, so a plain sentence needs no wrapper. |
| `Callout` | Same API as `Alert`, for static guidance. It adds the documentation severities `note` (`info` role) and `tip` (`positive` role), so SDK docs do not need their own callout colours. Pass `announce={false}` for callouts present at page load. `title` accepts a ReactNode, such as text with a `<code>` span; on web it renders inside `<strong>` and should stay inline. On native it renders inside the `Heading`, so pass a string or inline `Text`; its visible text is announced. |
| `Toast` | `notices` with stable `id`, `message`, `severity`, and optional `action`; `onDismiss` handles dismissal. Each notice is one capsule row with no stroke: a severity symbol on the leading edge, the message, the optional action, and a close symbol on the trailing edge. Native notices also accept `description` and `closable` (default true when `onDismiss` is supplied). Native `maxHeight` bounds a scrolling viewport; it defaults to 60% of the window height and accepts dp or a parent percentage. `dismissLabel` overrides the Dismiss wording inside the close button's accessible name; the button draws a symbol, not text. The capsule itself is `ToastNotice` on both platforms. For transient notices use `Toaster` and `toast()`, below. |
| `Toaster`, `toast()` | The transient host, from `@bloxwap/hig/react/toast` and `@bloxwap/hig/native/toast`: mount `Toaster` once, then call `toast(message, options)` from anywhere. Same names, options and stack on both platforms; see [Transient toasts](#transient-toasts-toaster-and-toast). |
| `Progress` | `label`, `value`, and `max`. Native draws the label with a ` value/max` suffix (`…` while indeterminate); `hideValue` leaves the suffix out for a host that shows the figure itself, and the value is still read. |
| `Spinner` | `label` (defaults to HIGProvider `messages.loading`) beside a spinning ring: web a `role='status'` span drawing `label…`; native one accessible element named by `label` (native also takes `testID`). `hideLabel` draws the ring alone for a tight spot, such as a row or a button-sized slot, while the label stays the accessible name (web: a visually hidden `label…` inside the status; native: the element keeps `accessibilityLabel` and draws no text). Type `SpinnerProps`. |
| `EmptyState` | `title`, optional `description`, optional `action`, and decorative `illustration`. A centred stack: symbol, title, description, action. `illustration` replaces the default symbol; `null` omits it. |
| `Avatar` | `name`, an optional image (`src` on web, `source` on native) and, when the host asks for it, a face generated from a `seed`. `variant`, `size`, `colors`, `faceColor`, `square` and `decorative` are the same on web and native. Its own entries are `@bloxwap/hig/react/avatar` and `@bloxwap/hig/native/avatar`. See [Avatar](#avatar). |

Native `EmptyState` keeps the default `Surface`, `Heading` and body-text anatomy, centred. Its `description` is optional; omitted or empty text leaves no blank description node. Decorative `illustration` content replaces the default symbol above the heading (`null` omits it); HIG hides the whole illustration subtree from VoiceOver/TalkBack navigation while keeping the heading and action accessible. The host controls the illustration's dimensions and spacing. Root `ViewProps`, including `style`, `testID` and layout events, pass to the Surface. `titleStyle` and `descriptionStyle` reach the actual text nodes; `maxFontSizeMultiplier` caps both, or inherits the provider policy when omitted. Text keeps the provider palette and heading semantics unless the host explicitly styles it.

```tsx
<EmptyState
  title={t('noMarkets')}
  illustration={<BrandMark width={64} height={64} />}
  style={{ flex: 1, alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center', backgroundColor: 'transparent', padding: 0, gap: 12 }}
  titleStyle={{ fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 28, textAlign: 'center' }}
  maxFontSizeMultiplier={2}
  action={<Button onPress={clearFilters}>{t('browseAll')}</Button>}
/>
```

The mark and clear-filter action remain host-owned. `tests/native/empty-state.test.cjs` verifies default anatomy, omitted descriptions, decorative accessibility metadata, real text/root props and accepted action delivery; these wiring checks are not physical-device accessibility certification.

### Avatar

A person or an account as a 40-unit disc. It shows the first of these that it has:

1. The image, when one is given and it loads.
2. A generated face, when the host asks for one.
3. The first two letters of `name` on the well fill.

The generated face is the "beam" face of [Boring Avatars](https://boringavatars.com): a backdrop, a tilted shape, two eyes and a mouth, all decided by a hash of the seed. The same seed and the same colours draw the same face on web and native, on every device, with nothing stored. It is off until the host asks for it, with `variant='beam'` or by passing a `seed`. An `Avatar` with neither looks as it always did.

Import `Avatar` from `@bloxwap/hig/react/avatar` or `@bloxwap/hig/native/avatar`. The native entry draws the face with `react-native-svg`, an optional peer that this entry needs. The status entries keep exporting `Avatar` for the imports that predate these: `@bloxwap/hig/react/status` exports the same component, and `@bloxwap/hig/native/status` exports it without the generated face (no `seed`, `variant`, `colors` or `faceColor`), so that entry still loads no SVG peer.

| Prop | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Required. The accessible name, the letters of the initials, and the seed when `seed` is left out. |
| `src` (web), `source` (native) | An image to show instead: a URL on web, a React Native image source on native. A photo that is not square is cropped to fill the box. If it fails to load, or it names no image (an empty `src`; on native `{uri: undefined}`, an empty address or an empty list), the face or the initials show in its place. |
| `seed` | What the face is drawn from, such as a wallet address. Passing it selects the generated face. It is case-sensitive, so pass an address in one casing everywhere. |
| `variant` | `'initials'` or `'beam'`: what shows without an image. Defaults to `'initials'`, or to `'beam'` when `seed` is given. |
| `size` | Width and height, in CSS pixels on web and dp on native. Defaults to 40. With `size`, the initials are drawn at 40% of it. A size that is not a finite number of zero or more (`NaN`, a negative, `Infinity`) is ignored. |
| `colors` | The palette of the face. Defaults to the `action`, `info`, `negative` and `warning` token roles, in that order (exported as `avatarColorRoles`). |
| `faceColor` | One colour for the eyes and mouth of every face. Left out, each face takes the `background` role on a bright colour and the `text` role on a deep one. |
| `square` | A square with no rounded corners instead of a disc, for a host that clips the avatar to its own shape. |
| `decorative` | Hides the avatar from assistive technology, for an avatar beside the name it stands for. |

```tsx
// A wallet: the address draws the face and the short address names it.
<Avatar name={shortAddress(address)} seed={address} size={20} />
// Beside the visible name, so it is not read twice.
<Avatar name={trader.name} seed={trader.address} decorative />
// A photo when there is one; the face when there is none or it fails to load.
<Avatar name={name} seed={address} src={photoUrl} size={64} />   // native: source={{ uri: photoUrl }}
```

**Colour.** The default palette is token roles, so it is Display P3 wherever HIG is. Web paints the `--hig-action`, `--hig-info`, `--hig-negative` and `--hig-warning` variables, which the tokens stylesheet defines in Display P3 where the browser supports it. Native paints the provider's colour table: the Display P3 table on an iOS host with `HIGProvider colorSpace='display-p3'`, and sRGB everywhere else. `colors` replaces the palette with the host's own: any CSS colour on web, `color(display-p3 …)` included, and any React Native colour on native, where a hex value is painted in the host's colour space like every other HIG colour. A seed picks its colours by position, so the number of colours and their order are part of a face. Change the palette and the same people get other colours; the shapes stay. For a signed-out placeholder, pass one fixed seed and a grey palette.

**Moving from boring-avatars.** For the same seed and the same `colors`, the shapes and the colour of each shape are those of boring-avatars 2.0.4 with `variant="beam"`, so people keep their faces. `<Avatar name={address} variant="beam" size={20} colors={palette} />` becomes `<Avatar name={label} seed={address} size={20} colors={palette} />`: boring-avatars' `name` is HIG's `seed`. These differ:

- The eyes and mouth are black or white in boring-avatars. HIG draws the `background` or the `text` role in their place, chosen by the same brightness rule, and `faceColor` sets one ink for every face.
- boring-avatars reads only six-digit hex colours when it chooses that ink and draws white for anything else. HIG also reads short hex, `rgb()` and `color()`, and draws the dark ink on a colour it cannot read, such as a CSS variable.
- The disc is the box's own rounding, not an SVG mask, so the drawing has no mask and no element id. `square` gives the unrounded square.
- `size` is a number. Only the beam face is drawn; the other boring-avatars variants are not.

The arithmetic is in `@bloxwap/hig/contracts/avatar`, with no React in it: `beamAvatar(seed, colors, inks?)` returns the colours, the two transforms, the mouth path and the eye positions in a 36-unit square, and `beamHash`, `beamInk`, `beamSize` and `beamEye` are exported beside it. The same entry holds what both renderers share outside the face: `avatarColorRoles` (the default palette roles), `avatarSide` (which sizes are drawn) and `avatarInitials` (the letters, never half of a character such as an emoji). A host that draws the same face somewhere else, such as on a canvas or in a share image, calls it directly.

## Transient toasts: `Toaster` and `toast()`

One API raises a notice that leaves by itself, on web and on native. Mount `Toaster` once; call `toast()` from anywhere, in or out of a component. Both draw the `ToastNotice` capsule and stack it the way [Sonner](https://sonner.emilkowal.ski/) does: the newest in front, three visible, the older ones collapsed behind it.

```tsx
// Web: Sonner is the engine (optional peer `sonner ^2.0.0`).
import {Toaster, toast, dismissToast} from '@bloxwap/hig/react/toast';

<HIGProvider>
  <App/>
  <Toaster position="top-center"/>
</HIGProvider>
```

```tsx
// Native: HIG's own host on Reanimated and Gesture Handler. Mount it last, so it draws over the screens.
import {Toaster, toast, dismissToast} from '@bloxwap/hig/native/toast';

<GestureHandlerRootView style={{flex: 1}}>
  <SafeAreaProvider>
    <HIGProvider>
      <App/>
      <Toaster position="top-center"/>
    </HIGProvider>
  </SafeAreaProvider>
</GestureHandlerRootView>
```

```tsx
// Either platform.
toast('Address copied');
toast.success('Withdrawal sent', {description: 'It arrives in about a minute.'});
toast.error('Transfer failed', {
  id: 'transfer',                 // raising 'transfer' again replaces this notice where it stands
  duration: Infinity,             // stays until dismissed
  action: <Button intent="ghost" onPress={retry}>Retry</Button>, // onClick on web
  onDismiss: () => log('closed by the person or by dismissToast'),
});
dismissToast('transfer');         // or dismissToast() for every notice
```

| `toast(message, options)` | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `severity` | `info` (default), `success`, `warning` or `error`. Picks the symbol and its token role. `toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.warning` and `toast.info` set it. |
| `description` | A second line under the message, in regular weight. With one the capsule keeps a 22-point corner radius instead of a full pill. |
| `action` | A control drawn before the close control, such as a `Button`. It does not dismiss by itself; call `dismissToast(id)` in its handler. |
| `duration` | Milliseconds before the notice leaves; the Toaster's `duration` (4000) when omitted. `Infinity` keeps it. Only a positive number is a time: zero, a negative number or `NaN` takes the default, and a time longer than a timer can count (2^31 − 1 ms, about 24 days) keeps the notice instead of ending it at once. |
| `id` | Raising a notice with the id of one that is showing replaces it in place and starts its time over. `toast()` returns the id. An empty string is not an id: the notice gets the next number. |
| `dismissName` | Accessible name of the close control. Defaults to the provider's `dismissNotice` wording around the message, so it is translated. |
| `onDismiss`, `onAutoClose` | Called once: `onDismiss` when the close control, a swipe or `dismissToast` ends the notice, `onAutoClose` when its time runs out. |

| `Toaster` prop | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `position` | `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center` (default) or `bottom-right`. Notices enter from that edge and leave towards it. `left` and `right` are the physical sides on both platforms, as in Sonner: under right-to-left the capsule's content mirrors and the stack stays where it is. To mirror the stack, choose the position by direction. |
| `expand` | Lists the visible notices one after another instead of collapsing them behind the front. Default `false`. |
| `visibleToasts`, `gap`, `duration` | 3 notices, 14 points, 4000ms. At least one notice is always shown. |
| `offset` | Distance from the screen edges, added to the safe-area inset: one number for every edge, or `{top, right, bottom, left}` with the other edges keeping the default (24 points; 16 under a 600-point window). `left` and `right` are physical, like `position`. `offset` places the stack at every window width on both platforms; on web, Sonner's `mobileOffset` replaces it under 600px when it is given. The app's top placement is `offset={{top: nativeMetrics.safeArea.toastOffset}}`; see [safe area](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/safe-area/). |
| `swipeDirections` | `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`. Default: towards the edges the stack sits against, so `bottom-center` swipes down and `top-right` up or right. |

Try all six placements in the [Toaster examples](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/components/toaster/). The `center` positions are the top-middle and bottom-middle placements. Select a position, then choose **Show a notice**. The copied example sets that position on the single mounted host.

The web `Toaster` also takes every other Sonner prop. The native one takes the props above and `testID`.

### How the native host moves

- **Nothing is laid out per frame.** A notice is rendered when it is raised, replaced or dismissed, and never while it moves. Raising or replacing one commits the host once and draws that notice's capsule alone; the screens beside the host do not render. Entering, leaving, restacking and the swipe change only `transform` and `opacity`, in Reanimated worklets on the UI thread. Each notice reads its place from one shared stack, so an arrival, a departure or a notice that changed height moves every notice in the same frame. With no notice showing the host renders nothing and runs no timer.
- **Stack.** 400ms on the CSS `ease` curve, Sonner's values. A new notice joins the stack once it has been measured, then slides in from its own height while the others make room. Behind the front of a collapsed stack each notice is 5% smaller, one gap further out and drawn at the front's height with its content hidden, so only its edge shows. One notice past the visible ones stays mounted and transparent, so the notice that is pushed out fades where it is.
- **Leaving.** 200ms on `ease-out`: the front goes back out by its own height while it fades, and the others close the gap in the same frame. A notice dismissed while it waits behind the drawn ones has nothing on screen to take away: it leaves the store at once and no view is mounted for it.
- **Swipe.** The notice follows the finger 1:1 towards an allowed edge and resists the other way, never passing 20 points. A release 45 points out, or faster than 500 points per second that way, dismisses: the notice goes on by its own size and fades, in 200ms or less so it leaves at the finger's speed. Anything else, and any swipe the system takes away before the finger lifts, returns on a critically damped spring that carries the release velocity. The swipe is recognised after 8 points, so a press on the action or the close control stays a press.
- **Time.** A finger on any notice holds every notice's time at once, and after 200ms expands the stack until it lifts, so a tap or a quick swipe does not stir the stack. The time also stops while the app is not in front. A notice behind the visible ones does not count down until it is shown. Only a notice that can be touched holds the time, so one that is pushed out of reach under the finger lets it run again.
- **Reduced motion.** Nothing slides or scales: notices take their place at once and fade over 150ms, and a swipe out fades where it was released. The provider's `reducedMotion` decides, which follows the OS setting by default.
- **Limits.** The store keeps 16 notices; past that the oldest timed ones are dropped, without `onDismiss` or `onAutoClose`. The last `Toaster` mounted draws. The host is an ordinary view, so a React Native `Modal` (the native `Dialog`, `Sheet`, `Menu` and `Select`) draws above it; a bottom stack does not move for the keyboard.

### Where the platforms differ

| | Web (Sonner) | Native |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expanding a collapsed stack | Pointer over the stack, or a tap | A finger resting on a notice for 200ms; always expanded while a screen reader runs |
| Time of a notice behind the visible ones | Runs | Waits until it is shown |
| Fast swipe | Distance over the time since the pointer went down, above 0.11px/ms | Release velocity above 500 points/s, so a hold before the flick still dismisses |
| Reduced motion | Cuts to the end state | Fades over 150ms |
| Announcement | Sonner's polite live region for every severity | One announcement per burst: an error if there is one, otherwise the newest notice, the one in front. On iOS an error interrupts and anything else queues. Android's announcement cannot interrupt |
| `offset` as a string | CSS, passed to Sonner | Not accepted |
| Store limit | None | 16 notices |
| `toast.loading`, `toast.promise` | Not wrapped; raise a persistent notice and replace it by `id` | Same |

Severity colours come from the provider on both platforms: `--hig-info`, `--hig-positive`, `--hig-warning` and `--hig-negative` on web, which are Display P3 where the browser supports it, and the `useColors()` roles on native, which are the Display P3 table on an iOS host with `colorSpace="display-p3"`.

The host emits no sound or haptic. Play the outcome's feedback where the notice is raised.

## Confetti

A burst of confetti for a result worth celebrating, such as a winning close. It is HIG's own on both platforms, with no third-party confetti package, and has its own entries: `@bloxwap/hig/react/confetti` and `@bloxwap/hig/native/confetti`. Both export the same two things: `confetti(options)`, which fires one burst and returns a promise that resolves when it has finished, and `Confetti`, the host mounted once. The options are those of [canvas-confetti](https://www.kirilv.com/canvas-confetti/), so a call written for it maps over.

```tsx
import {Confetti, confetti} from '@bloxwap/hig/react/confetti'; // native: '@bloxwap/hig/native/confetti'

// Once, inside HIGProvider. On native this is the layer the pieces fly in: mount it last in the screen root.
<Confetti />

// From an event handler or an effect.
await confetti({particleCount: 100, spread: 70, origin: {y: 0.7}});

// Or declaratively: fires when `trigger` is truthy, on mount and on each change to another truthy value.
<Confetti trigger={winCount} options={{particleCount: 100, spread: 70, origin: {y: 0.7}}} />
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `particleCount` | `50` | How many pieces the burst launches. |
| `angle` | `90` | Launch direction in degrees: 90 is straight up, 0 towards the right edge, 180 towards the left. |
| `spread` | `45` | How far, in degrees, pieces may stray from `angle` in total. |
| `startVelocity` | `45` | Launch speed in pixels per tick. Each piece starts between half and one and a half times this. |
| `decay` | `0.9` | The share of its launch speed a piece keeps each tick, from 0 to 1; above 1 a piece gains speed. |
| `gravity` | `1` | Pull downwards: 1 falls at full speed, 0 floats, a negative value rises. |
| `drift` | `0` | Sideways push in pixels per tick; positive is towards the right edge. |
| `ticks` | `200` | How long the burst lasts, in ticks of 1/60 s (200 is about 3.3 seconds). Pieces fade out over it. |
| `origin` | `{x: 0.5, y: 0.5}` | Where the burst starts, as a share of the viewport (web) or of the `Confetti` layer (native). |
| `colors` | token roles | Colours dealt to the pieces in turn. See Colour below. |
| `shapes` | `['square', 'circle']` | Shapes picked at random for each piece: `'square'`, `'circle'` or `'star'`. |
| `scalar` | `1` | Scales every piece; below 0 reads as 0. |
| `flat` | `false` | Pieces neither tumble nor wobble. |
| `disableForReducedMotion` | `true` | Draws nothing when reduced motion is on. |
| `zIndex` | `100` | Web only: stacking order of the canvas, read from the burst that creates it. |

`Confetti` takes `trigger` and `options` (one burst, or an array fired together); native adds `style` and `testID` for the layer. `confetti.reset()` stops every burst at once and resolves their promises. `mirrorConfetti(options)` returns the same burst seen in a mirror.

A number that is not finite reads as the default, and `startVelocity`, `gravity`, `drift`, `scalar` and `ticks` are kept within a million either way, so no input places a piece at infinity. Nothing caps `particleCount`.

Several calls in a row make one celebration. A fireworks call written for canvas-confetti maps over call for call:

```tsx
const base = {origin: {y: 0.7}};
confetti({...base, particleCount: 50, spread: 26, startVelocity: 55});
confetti({...base, particleCount: 40, spread: 60});
confetti({...base, particleCount: 70, spread: 100, decay: 0.91, scalar: 0.8});
confetti({...base, particleCount: 20, spread: 120, startVelocity: 25, decay: 0.92, scalar: 1.2});
confetti({...base, particleCount: 20, spread: 120, startVelocity: 45});
```

### Confetti colour

Without `colors`, pieces take the provider's `action`, `info`, `down`, `warning` and `up` roles in turn, so a custom `primaryColor` or `marketColors` shows in the burst. On web these are read from the `--hig-*` variables at the host, which hold `color(display-p3 …)` values where the browser supports them, and the canvas itself is a Display P3 canvas on a screen that can show it; elsewhere both fall back to sRGB. On native they come from `useColors()`: the Display P3 table on an iOS host that paints P3 (`HIGProvider colorSpace='display-p3'`), sRGB otherwise, as for every native component.

A colour passed in `colors` is painted as given. On web that is any CSS colour: a hex colour is sRGB and stays inside sRGB on a P3 screen, so pass `color(display-p3 …)` for a colour outside it. On native it is any React Native colour, read in the host's colour space.

### Confetti motion and performance

The flight is one set of pure functions in `@bloxwap/hig/contracts/confetti`, used by both platforms. It restates canvas-confetti's frame-by-frame update as a function of time, so a piece is where canvas-confetti puts it at every whole tick, and a burst takes the same time on a 60 Hz and a 120 Hz display and after a dropped frame.

- Web: every burst shares one full-viewport canvas and one `requestAnimationFrame` loop. The canvas is created by the first burst, sized for the device pixel ratio, takes no pointer events, and is removed when the last piece has gone. Each piece is one small path, as in canvas-confetti; the opacity is set once a burst and the fill colour once for each of its colours, with no colour string built per piece. React renders nothing while a burst flies.
- Native: React renders once when a burst starts and once when it ends. In between one Reanimated clock per burst runs on the UI thread, and each piece, a plain view, reads its transform and opacity from it. Nothing is laid out per frame. A burst of about 100 pieces is the intended size; larger bursts mount one view a piece. A star is that one moving view holding five triangles that never change, so it mounts six views.

### Confetti accessibility and direction

Confetti is decoration. The canvas (`aria-hidden`) and the native layer are hidden from assistive technology and take no pointer events or touches; show and announce the result itself with the content it belongs to. Under reduced motion (`HIGProvider reducedMotion`, else the system setting) a call draws nothing and resolves at once, unless it passes `disableForReducedMotion: false`. canvas-confetti defaults the other way.

`HIGProvider` learns the system setting just after it mounts: in an effect on web, from an asynchronous question on native. A burst asked for in that moment, by a `trigger` that is truthy when `Confetti` mounts or by `confetti()` in a mount effect, is therefore held by the host until the provider can answer, and is then drawn or dropped like any other. On web the wait is one render and happens only where the system asks for reduced motion; on native it is the one question `Confetti` asks the system when it mounts. A held burst resolves without being drawn if the host unmounts or `confetti.reset()` is called first.

Confetti is physical: `origin.x` 0 is the left edge and a positive `drift` goes right in both text directions, on both platforms. For a cannon that should fire from the leading edge, pass the options through `mirrorConfetti` when the direction is right-to-left. No text is drawn, so large text does not apply.

### Confetti platform differences

- Web needs no host: without a mounted `Confetti`, `confetti()` reads colours from the document root and reduced motion from the system. Native needs one: without it a call resolves and draws nothing.
- The web canvas covers the viewport and sits in the document body. The native layer fills the parent of `Confetti`, and `origin` is a share of that layer.
- Web draws canvas-confetti's shapes exactly: a square is a slanted, fluttering parallelogram. React Native cannot slant a view on Android, so native draws the rectangle with the same centre, area and long and short axes; circles are exact. A `'star'` is the same ten-point star on both: web fills its outline, and native, which has no paths without an SVG package, covers exactly that outline with five triangles made of view borders.
- Before the native layer has been laid out, `origin` is a share of the window.
- A burst left running when its web host unmounts finishes; on native it stops with the layer and its promise resolves.
- The native entry needs the Reanimated and Worklets peers. The web entry needs no peer and no stylesheet.
- Not supported: canvas-confetti's `useWorker`, `confetti.create`, `shapeFromPath` and `shapeFromText`.
