`npm run lint` runs `scripts/check-built-in-strings.mjs`, and so does `tests/built-in-strings.test.ts`. The check fails when a component under `packages/{react,native}/src` adds a user-visible or accessible literal. That covers JSX text, a visible or accessibility attribute (`aria-label`, `accessibilityLabel`, `title`, `label`, `description`, …), a label-like default prop and a `set…()` status string. To add copy, add a key to `HIGMessages`, read it with `useMessages()`, and add a row to the table above. The test checks that every key is in this table with its English default.

## Validation

See `tests/tokens.test.ts`, `tests/data.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/glossary.test.ts`, `tests/built-in-strings.test.ts`, `tests/messages.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/messages.test.cjs`, `docs/foundations/localization.json` and the data chapter. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink.

The native Button shows a leading spinner while busy and draws no busy text. On iOS its accessible name remains `Action · Working`. Android speaks the action name and its localized busy state once.


## Native runtime differences
Source: docs/foundations/native-runtime-differences.md

# Native runtime differences

Follow-ups #86–#89 and #92–#94 distinguish implementation checks from physical-device certification in #55. The supported packed consumers remain React Native 0.81.5 / Expo 54 and React Native 0.83.10 / Expo 55. Historical simulator/emulator captures remain in `evidence/native-sim/`; their results are not overwritten by software tests.

## Android locale direction

RN 0.83's `I18nManager.isRTL` can report false for an Arabic app locale. The regression is [upstream #54938](https://github.com/react/react-native/issues/54938), introduced by [#53417](https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/53417) and fixed by [#57635](https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/57635), with older-Android handling in [#58723](https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/58723).

HIG defaults direction to `I18nManager.isRTL`. Hosts that support RTL pass `direction={localeDirection(getLocales()[0])}`, using `localeDirection` from `@bloxwap/hig/native/provider` and their localization adapter (for example Expo Localization). This handles an Arabic per-app locale even when RN's OS diagnostic still reports false. Hosts that disallow RTL leave direction unset. Formatting locale remains independent, with `en-US` as the default. The Android `os-arabic` harness asserts the explicit host direction. Historical local fallback measurements predate the merged public API.

## Slider action labels

RN 0.83 exposes an empty accessibility action label when the host omits it. HIG supplies `messages.increase` and `messages.decrease` for both actions, with English Increase/Decrease defaults and host translation overrides. Disabled adjustments remain rejected. Automated labels and state checks do not establish what a person hears through TalkBack; physical reference flows remain in #55.

## iOS Dynamic Type audit

The historical RN 0.81.5 / Expo 54 run recorded 68 TextInput Dynamic Type heuristic findings. The RN 0.83.10 / Expo 55 run recorded none, while the large-text captures and text-field counts matched. The note in `evidence/native-sim/native-sim.json` applies to RN 0.81.5 only.

Source comparison of the release tags establishes that `RCTUITextField.mm` is byte-identical and the Fabric text-input view has no new UIFontMetrics/scaling behavior. The font utility changed to honor default font handlers in [React Native #53755](https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/53755). That refactor has not been isolated as the cause of the audit change. We therefore do not claim a UIFontMetrics fix or a physical accessibility pass. Root-cause attribution for #88 and device VoiceOver/largest-size checks remain open.

## Audio completion diagnostics

Expo Audio 1.1's Android playback status derives `didJustFinish` from the player's ended state. Both the playback-state listener and status polling can report that state. The SDK 54 captures show two completion callbacks after one recorded `play:tick`; SDK 55 shows one. A completion callback is not an extra play.

Only the gallery recorder listens to `playbackStatusUpdate`. The HIG adapter dispatches preloaded players without waiting for or replaying completion events. `tests/native-verification.test.ts` injects two completion callbacks and asserts exactly one backend `play()` call while preserving both raw diagnostic events. No runtime completion de-duplication is needed unless the adapter later depends on completion. Dispatch timing and audible latency remain distinct; speaker, silent-mode and interruption observations remain in #55.

## Native text and color follow-ups

Native Button uses HIG Text for both its label and localized busy suffix, preserving font registration, script spacing and scale caps. Its busy accessible name includes the visible label, with explicit host labels taking precedence. Mixed ReactNode status titles concatenate visible text without inserting extra spaces.

`HIGProvider colorSpace='display-p3'` selects the canonical P3 table on iOS. Android and web resolve to sRGB. Native controls and host-drawn views read the resolved table through `useColors()`; nested providers inherit the selected space. These are channel-selection and semantic tests, not comparisons of physical displays.


## Foundation and platform rules
Source: docs/foundations/platform.md

# Foundation and platform rules

Nested HIGProvider instances inherit omitted environment, feedback and native font settings. Explicit false values, including reducedMotion, override their parent.

## Color (#6)

Dark is the only audited mode. Source values retain the commit-pinned monorepo authored OKLCH and brand channels; see [source reconciliation](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/source-reconciliation/). Use surface/text/action/focus/buy/sell/warning roles, never infer intent from a hue. Web emits sRGB then P3 in `@supports`. RN uses explicit hex values from HIG's own tables, selected once per app by `HIGProvider colorSpace` (#93); see the native colour space table below. Android and third-party images use sRGB. `evidence/contrast.json` records all 33 approved normal-text pairings. Faint text is restricted to background/surface: faint on nested fails normal-text AA, so use muted on nested instead. Border is decorative; meaningful control edges/focus must use tested text or focus tones. **Do** use onAction on green fills; **don't** put white body text on green.

### Primary brand colour

Set `primaryColor` on `HIGProvider` to apply another brand's accent. For example,
Tap Trade TV can use a red primary colour:

```tsx
import {HIGProvider} from '@bloxwap/hig/react/provider';
// Native: import {HIGProvider} from '@bloxwap/hig/native/provider';

<HIGProvider primaryColor='#ff0000'>
  <App />
</HIGProvider>
```

The red above is an example; supply the brand's exact hex. Both providers accept
opaque sRGB `#RGB` or `#RRGGBB` values. Other formats, including transparent
colours and CSS variables, throw a descriptive error. Omit the prop at the root
to retain the existing Bloxwap green and wide-gamut defaults. Nested providers
inherit the primary colour unless they supply another one. Separate roots can
use different brands; changing or removing the prop updates mounted components.

The override sets `action` and `focus`, plus `onAction` to black or white for the
higher text contrast (at least 4.5:1 on the primary fill). Buttons, links,
selection controls, progress indicators, action tones, and chart crosshair
labels follow the accent. Success/error/warning/info and buy/sell roles keep
their existing meanings and colours. Destructive buttons keep their dark label
on the negative fill. The approved Bloxwap mark retains its original colours;
another brand supplies its own logo.

Web applies scoped CSS variables on the provider wrapper and on HIG portalled
overlays, including Dialog, GestureSheet, Menu, Popover, and Tooltip. Import the
normal token and component CSS. `useThemeStyle()` from the web provider entry
returns the primary variables for a host-owned portal's root. Both platforms
export `useColors()` for host-drawn content (web returns sRGB values for canvas).
Native converts the sRGB input when an iOS provider selects `display-p3`; Android
and react-native-web keep sRGB input channels. A nested provider can change colour
space while inheriting the brand accent.

The [default palette contrast report](https://github.com/bloxwap/hig/blob/main/evidence/contrast.json) covers the
default theme. Custom accents also need review against the surfaces where they
appear, particularly link text and focus rings; automatic label selection only
guarantees contrast on the primary fill. Choose an accent with enough contrast
for the dark surfaces your product uses.

Tokens-only hosts can call `resolvePrimaryColor` from `@bloxwap/hig/tokens` and
apply the resulting `action`, `focus`, and `onAction` roles to a scoped element.
Keep these three roles together so primary labels remain readable.

### Market direction colours

Native colour tables carry two market-direction roles: `up` (rising, long, gain) and
`down` (falling, short, loss). They default to `buy` and `sell`. A host whose market
convention differs, such as KRX or A-share red-for-up, sets
`<HIGProvider marketColors={{up:'#ff3b30',down:'#0a84ff'}}>` from
`@bloxwap/hig/native/provider`. Either role can be omitted to keep its default, and
an empty or non-string value is ignored. Nested providers inherit the override, as with
`primaryColor`. The values are used as given, in the provider's colour space (Display P3
channels on an iOS P3 host). `buy`, `sell`, `positive` and `negative` never change:
`positive`/`negative` mean success and error, not market direction. Readouts paint
direction with `tone="up"` or `tone="down"`.

Web takes the same `marketColors={{up, down}}` on `HIGProvider` from
`@bloxwap/hig/react/provider`, as CSS colours. The provider sets `--hig-up` and
`--hig-down` on its wrapper, and CSS reads them as `var(--hig-up,var(--hig-buy))` and
`var(--hig-down,var(--hig-sell))`, so without an override nothing changes. Nested
providers inherit them through the cascade; `useThemeStyle()` returns them for a host
portal outside the provider. `TradeHistoryListBlock` and `TradeHistoryDetailBlock` paint
the side, the leverage and the result with these roles on both platforms, and `BarPnl` (with the
blocks that draw it) fills the stretch between entry and mark and colours the mark price with `up`
in profit and `down` at a loss. The liquidation tick stays `negative`, because it is a danger, not a direction.

### Native colour space

React Native reads a hex colour's channels in the app's default colour space. That is sRGB unless the iOS host overrides `defaultColorSpace()` in its React Native factory delegate to return Display P3. If it does, `#ff479c` is read as P3 channels and paints a more saturated pink than the token. Set `colorSpace` on the root `HIGProvider` to match the host. Every HIG native component (Text, Surface, Separator, Button, Link, Field, Switch, Slider, Alert, Badge, Spinner, Skeleton, Dialog and GestureSheet) then paints from that table through `useColors()`, with the primary brand override applied if present. The Bloxwap mark uses `useBrandColors()` to retain its approved colours in the same colour space. Hosts choose a table and can configure the primary accent through `primaryColor`. Nested providers inherit both settings, and a test fails if a component imports `nativeSrgb` or paints a raw hex value.

| `HIGProvider colorSpace` | iOS | Android | react-native-web |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `srgb` (default) | `nativeSrgb` | `nativeSrgb` | `nativeSrgb` |
| `display-p3` | `nativeDisplayP3` (= `nativeColors.iosDisplayP3`) | `nativeSrgb` (HIG publishes no Android P3 table) | `nativeSrgb` |

| Role | `nativeSrgb` | `iosDisplayP3` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| action / positive / buy / focus | `#00ff3f` | `#00ff3d` |
| warning | `#fffb38` | `#fffa2e` |
| negative / sell | `#ff479c` | `#ff3d9e` |
| info | `#35b5ff` | `#2eb8ff` |

Neutral roles (background, surface, nested, text, muted, faint, border, onAction) have the same hex in both tables. Use `useColors()` to read the resolved table for host-drawn views next to HIG components. Evidence is native Jest (#93) and iOS Simulator captures of the gallery built as a Display P3 host (`evidence/native-sim/issue-93/`). Those captures predate the pink/neon-yellow tone adoption: in them, `display-p3` paints warning and negative as exactly the then-current sRGB tokens (`#f5b300`, `#ff5c5c`), while `srgb` on the same host paints them oversaturated (`#ffaf00`, `#ff4a54`); the mechanism is unchanged. Action and info are wider than sRGB, so the screenshot clips them. Physical display comparison is tracked in #55.

## Typography (#7)

Pin @bloxwap/font 0.1.4. Vite: import `@bloxwap/font/css`, which loads unicode-range subsets (latin, cyrillic, greek, other) so a page fetches only the scripts it renders; Next: upstream Sans/Mono loaders own loading and script fallback. Sans for prose/controls; Mono for code and tabular readouts; Pixel for a short nonessential accent. Body 16/24, label 14/20, caption 12/18, title 24/30, display 48/52 are candidate role mappings based on SDK scale. Web CSS exposes the roles as `--hig-type-<role>-size`, `-line-height`, `-weight` and a `--hig-type-<role>` font shorthand, and the families as `--hig-font-sans`/`--hig-font-mono`. Those resolve the `@bloxwap/font` Next loader variables first and fall back to the literal `'Bloxwap Sans'`/`'Bloxwap Mono'` families, so HIG controls render the loaded face in both Next and plain `@font-face` hosts. Web rem uses 16px root; RN sizes are explicit dp and allow font scaling. Do not disable Dynamic Type or fixed-height clip translated labels. Run the pinned native font generator and register its static TTF faces from `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts`; its typed manifest records weight/family/source hashes. Web hosts never install that package. Published WOFF2/Next loaders are not directly native assets. **Do** wait for registration before applying a custom native family; **don't** invent a family string and claim the font rendered. Arabic/Hebrew/CJK companions are owned upstream; load required scripts, test mixed-script punctuation and RTL. Large-text and device font evidence is pending.

## Geometry and layout (#8)

Spaces 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/48; radius 6/8/10/14 and pill (`--hig-radius-sm`…`--hig-radius-xl`, `--hig-radius-pill`). Comfortable control/target 48 and gap 12; compact 36 and gap 8, reserved for pointer/keyboard dense layouts. CSS exposes each mode as `--hig-density-<mode>-<control|target|gap>`, and `--hig-density-control`, `--hig-density-target` and `--hig-density-gap` follow the nearest `[data-hig-density]`, which the React provider sets. Painted icons can be 16/20/24 while targets stay 48 on touch. Never expand adjacent invisible hit areas so they overlap. Use logical inline spacing, wrapping labels, safe-area insets, keyboard avoidance and a scrollable native sheet; preserve portrait/tablet rotation without locking orientation. Pro tables may scroll with column headers; app amount entry reflows. Elevation uses nested fills rather than unverified shadows. Layer order: document, sticky nav, contextual popover, modal, notification. Browser top layer handles modal stacking; native Modal remains platform-owned.

### Form spacing

Neutral fills step up from whatever they sit on, one shade at a time, so nothing on a screen jumps to the lightest grey. On the page (`background`), a well is `surface` and a raised fill is `nested`. Inside a Surface, Dialog or sheet, a well is `nested` and a raised fill is `border`. Wells are inputs, the segmented track, Badge and Avatar. Raised fills are what sits on a well (the selected segment, a pressed capsule) and every thin track or rule: the Switch off track, the Slider and Progress tracks, the Spinner ring, Skeleton and Separator. Web reads these from `--hig-fill` and `--hig-fill-raised`; native reads `useFills()`. A host-drawn control uses the same pair instead of a fixed role.

An unavailable button is neutral: a well fill with `muted` text (`faint` and no fill for ghost), whatever its intent, so a dimmed accent never reads as a second call to action. A busy button keeps its intent colour at 70% under its spinner.

Controls inside a card or sheet sit 8 units apart in both directions: a toggle above a field, rows of presets, two buttons side by side, capsules in a filter row. The action row at the bottom of a card or sheet, the primary action with its secondary beside it, sits 16 units below the content above it, so the decision reads as separate from the form. The two actions themselves stay 8 apart.

Buttons, segmented controls and single-line text inputs share one height on web: 44 units on touch density, 36 compact. Rows in a list are capsules 8 units apart. A row that leads with a round avatar pads it equally on every side, so the capsule end is concentric with the avatar: a 40 unit avatar with 8 units of padding gives a 56 unit row with a 28 unit end radius. Every pane of a sheet shows its title in the header. A switch in a row sits flush with the row's trailing edge, in line with the content above and below it, and level with the first line of its label: when the label or its description wraps, the switch stays at the top and does not drift to the middle.

## Motion and gestures (#9)

Fast 180ms, base 260ms, slow 320ms; web easing `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)`. CSS exposes `--hig-motion-duration-<fast|base|slow>` and `--hig-motion-easing-standard`. The durations become 0ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and inside `[data-hig-motion='reduced']`, which the React provider sets when the host or OS asks for reduced motion. Press response ends on release/cancel; action executes on accepted activation, never press-in. Drag/scroll cancellation clears visual and feedback state. Interrupt transitions from current state instead of queuing. Reduced motion uses immediate state changes, static skeletons and unanimated numeric readouts. Outcome messages remain explicit. **Do** animate deliberate disclosure once; **don't** replay an entrance, highlight or sound for every live-data update. A number that updates in place is the one exception: it moves only its changed places through `AnimatedNumberReadout`, and in the swap card this is required for every number that can change while the card is shown (amounts, conversions, balances, fees, slippage and detail figures; see the SwapPanelBlock live numbers rule). Native segmented selection uses an interruptible core Animated transform with the same timing and easing; physical-device animation feel remains unverified. Motion preference is independent from sound/haptics.

## Accessibility and localization (#10)

Baseline: [WCAG 2.2 AA, Recommendation 12 December 2024](https://www.w3.org/TR/2024/REC-WCAG22-20241212/). Normal text 4.5:1; large text and meaningful non-text UI 3:1. The [contrast report nonText section](https://github.com/bloxwap/hig/blob/main/evidence/contrast.json) checks focus, faint, negative and action against background, surface and nested at 3:1. Decorative border is excluded; it must not be the sole meaningful state indicator. Touch baseline 48 logical units exceeds the web minimum. Provide visible focus, semantic labels/descriptions, logical keyboard order and non-drag alternatives. Native roles/state/value map to VoiceOver/TalkBack. No tooltip-only critical text. Restore trigger focus on modal dismissal; Escape/native back closes topmost cancellable overlay. Host owns safe-area, locale, parsing, route and keyboard adapters. Device insets come from the device at runtime; the `safeArea` tokens are only the offsets added on top of them (see [safe area](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/safe-area/)). Intl display is not money arithmetic. Vocabulary is locked in the [trading glossary](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/glossary/) (`docs/foundations/glossary.json`) before any locale translation. Number, currency, date, leverage, percent and RTL formatting is in the [localization guide](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/localization/).

Component review checklist: keyboard completion; labeled controls/errors; busy/disabled; focus restoration; narrow viewport; 200% text; long translations; Arabic/Hebrew RTL; mixed scripts; reduced motion; sound off; haptics off; unknown/stale/error values; VoiceOver/TalkBack on physical devices. Automated results and physical observations must be separate. Exception requires owner, affected surface, reason, alternative and expiry. No observed device evidence means pending, never pass.

## Brand and icons (#11)

Approved mark is copied verbatim from the pinned Font docs SVG, including embedded provenance. Import `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/mark.svg` on web; both web and RN geometry renderers are available from their brand entries. `npm run generate` reads the SVG's geometry and fills into `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/brand` (`brandMark`, with sRGB and Display P3 fills), and both renderers draw from it, so the mark needs no palette exception and does not follow `primaryColor` or a token change. Keep aspect ratio and clear space of one quarter mark width. Decorative marks/icons are hidden from accessibility; icon-only actions require an explicit accessible name and 48-unit target. Use currentColor for utility icons, never tint the approved brand mark arbitrarily. Directional arrows mirror in RTL; brand, check and financial direction do not. Icons repository contains a large catalog; do not import it wholesale. Only reviewed single glyphs belong in runtime exports. Favicon/OG derivatives have source provenance and drift checks. Physical device visual comparison remains unperformed.

Font-loading note: `@bloxwap/font/css` references all supported families/scripts, which may increase deployed asset bytes even with on-demand browser loading. The Latin web fixture instead uses two explicit @font-face rules with package asset URLs (Sans and Mono). Add only the scripts/italics used by each consumer. Do not assume a Latin-only fixture certifies mixed-script rendering.


## Native text in multiple scripts

Register each required companion face with the host font loader, then pass its registration name through `HIGProvider fontFamiliesByScript`, for example `{latin: {400: 'BloxwapSansRegular'}, ko: {400: 'BloxwapSansKRRegular', 600: 'BloxwapSansKRSemiBold'}, zh: {400: 'BloxwapSansSCRegular'}}`. The provider's `fontFamilies` remains the fallback. Nested providers inherit the script map when it is omitted.

HIG Text detects Hangul or Han in each run even when the provider locale is English. Shared CJK punctuation follows the run's `accessibilityLanguage`, then the provider locale; `script` can select a face explicitly. If a script map has fewer weights, Text chooses its nearest registered weight. Explicit `style.fontFamily` wins. Hosts load these optional faces themselves; declaring a map does not load a font. Native RadioGroup options accept `lang` for the spoken label and `description` for its translated second line.


## Principles and content
Source: docs/foundations/principles.md

# Principles and content

Issues #2, #3. Rules are candidate guidance anchored to SDK source and the public marketing surface; the pinned monorepo audit and live-origin snapshots are in `evidence/issue-1-18/`. Do not represent example trading actions as live product behavior.

## Clear action hierarchy

Offer one primary action per decision. In an amount-entry block, **do** label the next step “Review order” and show the asset and amount before host submission; **don't** say “Go” or execute a trade when a field receives focus. Secondary actions navigate or cancel. Destructive intent means irreversible removal/cancellation; buy/sell colors mean market direction and never imply safety. Bind pending state to the host request, block duplicate activation, retain a progress label. Disabled means unavailable; busy means an action is running. Give the reason nearby.

## Touch before density

Use comfortable 48-unit controls for mobile trade forms. **Do** stack amount, available balance, validation and primary action at narrow widths; **don't** squeeze a desktop order panel into a phone. Pro can use compact 36-unit controls with keyboard focus and separated targets. SDK code windows scroll horizontally; surrounding prose reflows. Marketing CTA and SDK install controls retain explicit labels, as observed in `bloxwap.com` and `font/apps/docs/app/global.css`.

## State tells the truth

Resting, hover, focus, pressed, selected, busy, disabled, empty, error, success, offline and stale are distinct states. **Do** retain the last value with a timestamp and “Data unavailable — retry”; **don't** display unknown as zero, silently imply a completed order, or announce every price tick. Errors name the failed action and recovery. Confirmations repeat host-provided consequences and offer cancel before commit. Essential information remains visible and accessible with feedback muted.

## Content and precision

Use sentence case and concrete verbs (“Copy install command”). **Do** display currency, precision and units supplied by the host; **don't** use a rounded display number as transaction input. Keep raw decimal strings in business logic. A percent component expects percent points, not an implicit ratio. Use localized display with explicit parsing policy; do not strip unfamiliar separators and submit a changed amount. Code uses Mono, body Sans, Pixel only as a decorative brand accent.

## Composition and progressive disclosure

Show common actions first, advanced options on deliberate disclosure. **Do** give a native sheet a visible close action and let Android back dismiss; **don't** rely on hover tooltips on touch. Navigation remains host-owned: HIG does not choose routes, wallets, order types, or trading outcomes. Use status/callout for persistent critical errors; toast only for nonessential acknowledgements.

## Concrete source and pattern references

The preceding rules map to Bloxwap-owned examples, without treating host demo outcomes as submitted trades:

- Clear action hierarchy: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/ui-native/src/components/button.tsx), [HIG pattern](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/actions-surfaces/). Source primary/secondary/destructive variants, busy activation policy and semibold labels.
- Touch before density: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/tokens/src/spacing.ts), [HIG pattern](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/blocks/). Source spacing aliases and 16-unit root; marketing CTA before-capture is before-bloxwap.com.png.
- State tells the truth: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/ui-native/src/components/toast.tsx), [HIG pattern](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/status/). Source notification severity and persistent readable outcomes; HIG preserves undismissed bursts.
- Content and precision: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/ui-native/src/components/number-format.ts), [HIG pattern](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/fields/). Source display formatting stays separate from raw amount input and host arithmetic.
- Composition and progressive disclosure: [pinned Bloxwap source](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/blob/d47cef4c40363184bdfda8d8c263ead108ef9ff6/packages/ui-native/src/components/sheet.tsx), [HIG pattern](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/overlays/). Source back/dismissal and safe-area behavior; basic HIG Modal alternative has an explicit close action.


## Safe area
Source: docs/foundations/safe-area.md

# Safe area

Device insets come from the device at runtime (`useSafeAreaInsets()`, `SafeAreaView`, or `env(safe-area-inset-*)` on the web). The `safeArea` tokens are only the offsets added on top of those insets. They do not include, replace, or approximate the inset values themselves. Do not put raw device inset values in `packages/hig/tokens/source.json`.

The tokens record the offsets the native mobile app uses today. They are not a single standardized gutter. Compose them with the live insets:

```ts
import {nativeMetrics} from '@bloxwap/hig/tokens';
import {useSafeAreaInsets} from 'react-native-safe-area-context';

const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
const toastTop = insets.top + nativeMetrics.safeArea.toastOffset;
```

```css
padding-top: calc(env(safe-area-inset-top) + var(--hig-safe-area-toastOffset));
```

`toastOffset` is 44 + 16, to match the website's Sonner toaster: the website adds `env(safe-area-inset-top) + 44px` on top of Sonner's 16px `--mobile-offset-top`, so toast cards land at safe-area + 60.

## Trade screens stay full-bleed

Trade screens stay full-bleed. Their chrome adds the insets itself: the top bar, tap controls, toasts, share overlay, and chart axis reserves all compose `insets.*` with a `safeArea` offset. Do not wrap a trade screen in `SafeAreaView`, and do not also pad the chart canvas by the same insets.

```ts
const {safeArea} = nativeMetrics;

// Trade chrome gutters (8).
const paddingTop = insets.top + safeArea.chromeGutter;
const paddingLeft = insets.left + safeArea.chromeGutter;
const paddingRight = insets.right + safeArea.chromeGutter;
const paddingBottom = insets.bottom + safeArea.chromeGutter;

// Chart axis chrome reserved by the trade screen (8 + 48 pill; 80 + 8 tap controls).
const axisTop = insets.top + safeArea.axisChromeTop;
const axisBottom = insets.bottom + safeArea.axisChromeBottom;

// Sheet card content (16), when the sheet does not already apply insets.
const sheetPaddingBottom = insets.bottom + safeArea.sheetContentGutter;
```

## `SafeAreaView` for non-trade screens

Use `SafeAreaView` on non-trade screens such as settings, 404, bootstrap, and fullscreen modals. A trade route-gate may apply left and right safe-area edges only, so a blocked trade view is not full-bleed into the system insets.

`fullscreenMin` (20) comes from the QR scanner's fullscreen modal chrome: `Math.max(insets.top|bottom, 20)` and `insets.left|right + 20`. It is not the settings screen, which uses a Tailwind `px-5` gutter.

## Side gutters

The app currently uses side gutters of 8, 16, and 20 in different places. Document and keep that as-is; do not collapse them to one token.

- `chromeGutter` (8): trade top bar and tap controls (`paddingLeft` / `paddingRight` / `paddingTop` or `paddingBottom` of `insets.* + 8`).
- `sheetContentGutter` (16): sheet card and similar content padding, and the trade share overlay (`insets.* + 16`).
- `fullscreenMin` (20): the QR scanner's fullscreen modal chrome (`Math.max(insets.top|bottom, 20)` and `insets.left|right + 20`). Not the settings screen's Tailwind `px-5` gutter.

## Fixture and store-capture exceptions

Fixture and store-capture exceptions stay in the app. Snapshot and fixture builds may zero chrome insets so layout is stable; store-capture builds keep the device insets. Do not encode those exceptions in HIG tokens.

## Do not pad `GestureSheet` twice

`GestureSheet` already applies safe-area insets to its content padding (`tokens.space.xl` plus the bottom inset). Do not add `sheetContentGutter` or another inset on top of that default padding, or the sheet will be padded twice. Pass an explicit inset only when you intend to replace the default, including `0` for a flush edge.

## Source references

These values come from the private `bloxwap/monorepo` native app. Paths, not public links:

- `apps/mobile/src/components/tap-controls.tsx` — trade chrome gutter of 8; fixture and store-capture inset exceptions.
- `packages/ui-native/src/components/toast.tsx` — `TOAST_TOP_OFFSET = 44 + 16`.
- `apps/mobile/src/profile/lib/sheet-card-padding.ts` — sheet content gutter of 16.
- `apps/mobile/src/components/live-chart.tsx` — `AXIS_CHROME_TOP` 56 and `AXIS_CHROME_BOTTOM` 88; fixture and store-capture exceptions.
- `apps/mobile/app/trade/[asset].tsx` — full-bleed trade screen whose chrome adds insets itself; chrome gutter 8, share overlay gutter 16, toast offset, and the same fixture exceptions.
- `apps/mobile/src/components/qr-scanner.tsx` — fullscreen modal chrome: `Math.max(insets.top|bottom, 20)` and `insets.left|right + 20` (`fullscreenMin`).


## Pinned source reconciliation
Source: docs/foundations/source-reconciliation.md

# Pinned source reconciliation

Issues #2, #6–#9, #11–#18. See `evidence/issue-1-18/monorepo-sha.txt` for the exact monorepo commit and `monorepo-source-fetch.json` for all 129 audited paths. This supersedes the earlier 404 source-access limitation; it does not turn old unperformed product/device checks into passes.

The audit covers tokens, shared web/native primitives, plain-ui and app/Pro-owned controls. `monorepo-audit.json` records byte-identical duplicate groups, source bytes, repository asset totals and explicit source component dispositions. The existing catalog/platform matrix defines the HIG destination families. The authenticated organization inventory now includes monorepo, .github-private, taptradetv and tapsiren; their complete observed trees and explicit applicability decisions are recorded in new-repositories.json and planning/adoption.json. Joe Blau accepted the recorded source and applicability decisions on 2026-10-27; see evidence/adoption/owner-approval-2026-10-27.md. Confetti, signal strength, animated number backends and overlay layering internals stay optional host integrations; they are not silently added to base imports. Migration owners remain the owning product teams; HIG cannot claim their source forks have been deleted.

## Tokens and platform units

`packages/hig/tokens/upstream-palette.json` preserves the complete authored semantic OKLCH palette and brand sRGB/P3 channels. `sourceColors` exports web strings plus converted Android sRGB and iOS Display-P3 channel values; generated CSS exposes authored `--hig-source-*` variables. The HIG surface, nested, text and muted roles now retain their corresponding authored OKLCH values and tested sRGB fallback. Brand green and blue preserve upstream P3 channels. HIG focus green, market sell red, warning gold, opaque border and faint text are intentional intent/accessibility mappings rather than mislabeled exact source copies; direction remains distinct from destructive intent.

Native views default to sRGB and use `nativeColors.android`/`ios`. A host that explicitly configures RN iOS default color space as Display-P3 sets `HIGProvider colorSpace='display-p3'`, so HIG components paint `nativeColors.iosDisplayP3` (also exported alone as `nativeDisplayP3`). It reads `useColors()` for its own views and converts third-party sRGB assets (#93). Never send CSS functions to native views or use P3 channel hex in an sRGB host. These are mathematical conversion checks, not physical wide-gamut display certification.

Source `spacing.ts` and `type.ts` explicitly set both rem roots to 16; native spacing md=12 and base type=16 match HIG. Radius 6/8/10/14 and motion 180/260/320 ms also match. HIG caption line-height 18, title 30 and display 52 intentionally provide readable role leading versus the stock utility steps. Comfortable 48-unit native targets and compact 36-pixel desktop targets remain distinct; compact native buttons still retain 48-unit hit targets. Source native sheets use optional Gorhom/Reanimated gesture backends, 320 ms card transitions and separate 500 ms opening motion. HIG's basic Sheet stays a static, scrollable Modal alternative. The isolated gesture-sheet entry now supplies an optional Gorhom adapter with detents, cancellation delegation, native back, safe-area/keyboard configuration, reduced-motion mapping and focus requests. Its mocked lifecycle and real Metro imports are software-verified; actual worklet, pan interruption and assistive-technology behavior still require a booted native target.

## Native font generation and registration

Install `fonttools[woff]==4.61.1` and `brotli==1.2.1`, then run `npm run generate:fonts` before native consumer commands. `scripts/generate-native-fonts.py` derives static faces exclusively from the installed `@bloxwap/font@0.1.4` variable WOFF2 files, verifying all four input hashes before writing. Those four sources are byte-identical to 0.1.1 and 0.1.2, so the derived faces, their SHA-256 and their 0.1.1 unique IDs are unchanged. It adapts the monorepo's generator and preserves its naming/weight metadata. The generated manifest contains input/output SHA256, PostScript names, Expo registration keys, weights, scripts and byte counts; OFL attribution ships beside the faces. Generated TTF files are build outputs, not per-repository committed binary copies. Local tarballs include them through `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts/fonts/*` (moved out of the web tokens package in #64); consumers register only needed faces.

The Expo fixture registers Sans Regular/SemiBold and Mono Regular through `expo-font`, waits for loading, exposes failure visibly and passes explicit 400/600 family keys to the native provider. Text, headings and buttons select registered static weight families, avoiding an invalid variable family name or synthesized weight. Expo web uses feedback.web.ts browser adapters; Android/iOS retain the native backend. Korean/Simplified Chinese Regular/SemiBold faces can be registered by host locale policy; other scripts use an explicit host/system fallback. Pixel remains a scoped web accent, not a native body-font requirement. Font registration in Expo web and Metro builds does not certify native rasterization, native Dynamic Type, or multilingual physical-device layout.

## Observation boundaries

Headless browser synthetic composition checks preserve raw negative/decimal locale strings without formatting or precision loss; real on-screen IME composition is a separate device check. Browser 200% root text, narrow width and RTL checks exercise DOM reflow, not OS text scaling. Jest inspects RN roles, states and handlers with native modules mocked; Expo web exercises RN web rendering; neither is TalkBack. Android emulator installation, startup and any observed OS semantics are reported separately in `evidence/issue-1-18/`. Physical iOS/Android, tactile output and real VoiceOver/TalkBack observations remain unperformed on this Linux VM.

The root build compiles every `packages/hig` entry after the entries it imports through `@bloxwap/hig/<entry>` (`scripts/build-order.mjs` derives the order and fails on cycles or a missing `tsconfig.json`), so clean builds cannot rely on stale dist output. The expanded browser flow runs in Chromium/Firefox/WebKit under 320-pixel width, translated RTL tabs and 200% root text. It checks required validation, synthetic composition/raw precision, keyboard range/radio/menu/search, nested focus restoration, persistence/retry and zero automated axe WCAG findings. The Expo-web gallery separately checks registered faces, Modal picker, labels and range keyboard values. The native Slider web backend needs explicit ARIA min/max/now and keyboard actions; native OS builds retain adjustable role/state/value semantics. Checkbox/radio/tab web aliases likewise preserve native-renderer state in RN web. None of these observations is labeled as TalkBack. Quality gates verify every generated native face hash and cap the three selected fixture faces at 1.4 MB; optional CJK/other weight faces are available but are not imported by the default fixture.
