## Contribution, ownership and admission
Source: docs/governance/contributing.md

# Contribution, ownership and admission

Issue #36. This chapter sets out how HIG stays the one maintained design system for Bloxwap. It covers who owns what, how changes are reviewed, how components enter and leave the catalog, which platforms are supported, and how a product can justify an exception. Release, semver and deprecation rules are in the release chapter. Setting up and upgrading a repository is covered in the new-repository chapter.

## Canonical ownership

| Area | Canonical owner | Others may |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic tokens (colour roles, space, radius, type, motion, density), native colour spaces, contrast pairs | `bloxwap/hig` → `@bloxwap/hig/tokens` | Map roles to host variables with `var()`. They may not redefine literal values. |
| Component contracts, DOM and React Native renderers, blocks, the semantic feedback contract | `bloxwap/hig` → `@bloxwap/hig/contracts`, `-react`, `-native`, `-feedback` | Compose components and override layout in context. They may not fork a primitive's paint or geometry. |
| Font sources, families and web loaders | `bloxwap/font` → `@bloxwap/font` | HIG generates pinned native faces from Font releases. Consumers install fonts and never commit binaries. |
| Sound recipes and the Web Audio engine | `bloxwap/sfx` | HIG owns the cue mapping and preferences, and exports approved WAV cues for native. |
| Haptic presets and the web engine | `bloxwap/haptic` | HIG owns the RN adapter and the capability matrix. |
| Chart engine | `bloxwap/chart` | HIG owns chart theming and the accessible non-canvas alternative. |
| Product business logic, routing and data | The owning product repository | HIG components never import wallet, network or trading code. |
| Brand marks | `bloxwap/hig` brand component (pinned from the Font SVG) | Use the component. Its fills and geometry are generated from the approved SVG into `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/brand` (`brandMark`), the mark's canonical source; import that for a host-drawn mark, never the hexes. |

The organization adoption matrix (`planning/adoption.json`) records the owner, applicability, HIG version, merged PRs, status and dated exceptions for each repository and product surface.

## Contribution and review criteria

Every HIG pull request must:

1. **Link its issue** (`Part of #N` or `Closes #N`) and state its intent, the states it affects and its platform mapping.
2. **Change source and generated artifacts together**, then run `npm ci && npm run check` (build, lint, generation drift, typecheck, web and native tests). Also run the smokes relevant to the change: `smoke:ssr`, `smoke:packed`, `smoke:packed-native`, `smoke:packed-boundaries`, `smoke:packed-examples`, `examples:check` and `quality`.
3. **Cover behaviour on both renderers**, or record the platform decision and its supported alternative. Include accessible names, roles and states, keyboard and focus, native back, large text and RTL, and muted operation (sound and haptics off) without losing essential feedback.
4. **Label evidence precisely**: automated, browser, iOS Simulator, Android emulator or physical device. A mock, simulator or emulator never proves physical sound, haptics, VoiceOver or display output.
5. **List the checks that were not run**, upstream gaps, rollout and rollback. Breaking changes follow the release chapter.
6. **Pass the scoped anti-drift check** (`node scripts/drift.mjs`, run by `npm run quality` and tests). New exceptions follow the exception policy below.

A maintainer reviews against the same list. A PR that only updates screenshots or baselines must say why the visual change is intended.

## Component admission

A component or block enters the catalog only when all of the following hold:

- It is used repeatedly in at least two Bloxwap surfaces, or one product surface plus an SDK docs site, and the inventory (`planning/catalog.json`) cites that usage.
- It has a minimal API that composes existing primitives, with no wallet, network or trading dependencies and no unrelated imports. The per-entry export and boundary smokes enforce this.
- It has a React DOM renderer and either a React Native renderer or a documented native alternative, and the platform matrix is updated.
- It has a complete state matrix: focus, pressed, busy/disabled, error, empty, long text, large text, reduced motion, and feedback disabled where relevant. It also has catalog examples that typecheck in the packed consumers.
- It is documented: a usage chapter, an API reference, accessibility notes and a migration note for each fork it replaces.

## Component removal

1. Inventory every consumer with org-wide code search and the adoption matrix.
2. Deprecate the component in a minor release. Name the replacement, provide a codemod or checklist, and keep the export working for at least one minor release and 30 days.
3. Open removal PRs in each consuming repository, or record dated exceptions for them.
4. Remove the component in the next major release and record the change in the changelog and the matrix.

## Platform support policy

| Platform | Supported (tested in CI or recorded evidence) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React DOM | React 19.2; Vite, SSR and Next 16.4 (webpack) packed consumers; Chromium, Firefox and WebKit | Other bundler or Next versions need checks in the host |
| React Native | RN 0.81.5 with Expo 54 and React 19.1.0; RN 0.83.10 with Expo 55 and React 19.2.0 (#68); Metro; packed Android/iOS exports in CI for both; iOS Simulator (iOS 26.5) and Android emulator (API 35) gallery runs for both | RN 0.82 and 0.84+ are not supported. On RN 0.83 Android a per-app RTL locale does not reach `I18nManager.isRTL`, so RTL hosts pass `direction={localeDirection(getLocales()[0])}` ([localization](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/localization/#native-direction-from-the-host-locale), #86). Physical devices are pending (#55) |
| Tokens only | Plain CSS, Tailwind through host config, typed tokens | No React, RN or audio peers |
| Feedback | Web: `@bloxwap/sfx` and `@bloxwap/haptic`. Native: Expo audio and haptics adapters | Essential outcomes must never depend on sound or haptics |

Support only changes in a minor or major release. Each change updates `docs/architecture/platform-matrix.md`, the packed smokes and this table together.

## Justified product exceptions

A product may differ from HIG only through a recorded exception. Silent forks are not allowed.

- **Scope:** an exact path or folder prefix, and a single anti-drift rule (`obsolete-import`, `copied-palette`, `copied-token-definition`, `copied-primitive-css` or `copied-font-binary`).
- **Required fields:** `owner` (an accountable role or person), `reason` (the user or product need, or the rollback dependency) and `expires` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, at most 180 days ahead).
- **Where:** HIG's own exceptions go in `planning/drift-exceptions.json`. An adopting repository keeps its exceptions in its own `hig-drift.json`. The adoption matrix links to them.
- **Review:** the check fails on expired exceptions and on exceptions without an owner or reason, and warns about unused ones. Renewing an exception needs a new reason and owner approval. Repeated exceptions for the same need are a signal to propose a HIG change through the admission criteria.

Intentional density differences, such as compact Pro versus the comfortable touch app, are HIG density modes. They are not exceptions.

## Scoped anti-drift checks

`scripts/drift.mjs` has no dependencies and checks only files tracked in git under the configured `paths`. Paths listed under `canonical` are exempt from the copy rules.

| Rule | Fails when |
| --- | --- |
| `obsolete-import` | Code imports a retired fork (`@workspace/tokens`, `@workspace/ui`, `@workspace/ui-native`, plus repository-specific `obsoleteImports`) or a copied `vendor/hig/` or `styles/hig/` folder |
| `copied-palette` | Code outside a canonical owner hard-codes the Bloxwap brand hexes owned by `@bloxwap/hig/tokens`. The approved mark's fills are owned by `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/brand`, generated from the pinned SVG |
| `copied-token-definition` | A stylesheet assigns a literal value to a `--hig-*` token. Remapping one role to another with `var()` is allowed |
| `copied-primitive-css` | A bare `.hig-*` selector sets the primitive's paint or geometry (background, border, radius or min-height). Contextual layout overrides are allowed |
| `copied-font-binary` | A `.ttf`, `.otf` or `.woff*` file is committed outside a canonical font owner |

Generation drift (stale tokens, brand or glossary outputs) is checked separately by `scripts/check-drift.mjs` in `npm run lint`.


## New repository setup and upgrades
Source: docs/governance/new-repository.md

# New repository setup and upgrades

Issue #36. These steps adopt HIG in a new or existing Bloxwap repository without copying component folders, palettes, fonts or feedback engines. The five SDK docs sites followed this path: bloxwap/hyperliquid#180, bloxwap/chart#53, bloxwap/font#11, bloxwap/sfx#50 and bloxwap/haptic#26.

## 1. Pick applicability

Add or update the repository's row in `planning/adoption.json` (a PR to bloxwap/hig) with one of these applicability values:

| Applicability | Install | Never add |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product runtime UI (web) | `@bloxwap/hig/tokens`, `-contracts`, `-react`; `@bloxwap/font`; `-chart` with `@bloxwap/chart` only for `PriceChart` (#96) | Copied component folders or token CSS |
| Product runtime UI (React Native) | `@bloxwap/hig/tokens`, `-contracts`, `-native`, `-native-fonts`; optional `-feedback` plus Expo peers | DOM renderer imports, font binaries outside the manifest |
| Docs or marketing site | `@bloxwap/hig/tokens`, `-react` (CSS and the controls in use); `@bloxwap/font`; `-og-fonts` as a build-time dev dependency for OG cards only | A local `.btn` layer, a palette copy, `vendor/hig`, `-native-fonts` for OG cards |
| Brand or content only | Nothing at runtime; follow the principles, content and brand chapters | React, RN or audio dependencies |
| No UI | Nothing; README and content conventions only | Any HIG runtime dependency |

## 2. Install versioned packages

Install the required packages at the same exact published version. For a web consumer:

```sh
npm install --save-exact @bloxwap/hig-contracts@0.1.2 @bloxwap/hig-tokens@0.1.2 @bloxwap/hig-react@0.1.2
```

Native consumers install `@bloxwap/hig-native` and `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts` instead of the DOM renderer; add feedback only where needed and satisfy the supported profile's peers. Keep all HIG dependencies and overrides aligned. Commit the lockfile and record the release, source commit and exact registry integrity values in the owning evidence manifest.

Building candidates requires `npm run generate:fonts` with Python packages `fonttools[woff]==4.61.1` and `brotli==1.2.1`. Registry consumers use the packaged fonts without generating them.

For unpublished changes only, follow the [release dry-run procedure](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/governance/release/) and consume its exact packed candidate archives. Never copy `packages/*/src`, `dist` folders, token CSS, palettes, fonts or feedback engines. Replace candidate `file:` dependencies with registry versions and remove obsolete archives when adopting a published release. Retain provenance manifests and historical validation records.

Then follow the installation chapter for your platform: import `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/css` and `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` once (add `@bloxwap/hig/react/css/base` first only when HIG owns the whole page), use per-component imports, load fonts through `@bloxwap/font`, and on native register fonts from the HIG font manifest.

## 3. Add the scoped drift check to CI

Create `hig-drift.json` in the repository root:

```json
{
  "paths": ["apps/docs/app", "apps/docs/components", "apps/docs/lib", "apps/docs/styles"],
  "canonical": [],
  "obsoleteImports": [],
  "exceptions": []
}
```

Run the check from a pinned HIG checkout. The script uses only Node built-ins and needs no install:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with: {repository: bloxwap/hig, ref: <source commit of the installed release>, path: .hig}
- run: node .hig/scripts/drift.mjs --root . --config hig-drift.json
```

- **Scope:** only paths you have migrated. Widen `paths` as more surfaces move.
- **`canonical`:** use it only for assets the repository owns. For example, `bloxwap/font` owns its web font files.
- **Exceptions:** record any other exception with an owner, a reason and an expiry no more than 180 days ahead, following the contribution chapter's exception policy.

First run against current `main` heads on 2026-10-15, scanning `apps/docs` (automated, local):

- hyperliquid and haptic pass.
- sfx flags the brand-mark fill in `lib/og-card.tsx`. That needs an exception like HIG's own brand marks.
- chart flagged `styles/hig-roles.generated.css` (#66). [chart#56](https://github.com/bloxwap/chart/pull/56) deleted it.
- font flags its own font binaries, which belong under `canonical`.
- agent-cli flagged `vendor/hig/tokens.css`, its import, and committed TTFs (#58). [agent-cli#47](https://github.com/bloxwap/agent-cli/pull/47) removed them, and its drift check now passes with no exceptions.

## 4. Validate and record

- Build the site or app and run the repository's lint, typecheck, test and browser checks, plus keyboard, 390px mobile, large text and RTL checks.
- Measure CSS, JS and font bytes and the dependency count before and after.
- Link the merged PR, the HIG version and any dated exceptions in the matrix row.
- Label evidence as automated, browser, iOS Simulator, Android emulator or physical device.

## Upgrading HIG

1. Read the release changelog (or the dry-run changelog for an unpublished candidate), together with the semver section of the release chapter.
2. Upgrade tokens, contracts, renderer and feedback together. Never mix release versions or candidate commits. Verify the registry integrity values or candidate archive hashes.
3. Update the drift checkout `ref` to the same commit and run the check. Remove exceptions whose need has gone.
4. Re-run the validation in step 4 and update the matrix row's `higVersion` and PR links.
5. Roll back by reverting the upgrade PR, which restores the previous exact versions and lockfile. Product pilots also keep their host feature flag (for example `NEXT_PUBLIC_HIG_PILOT=0`).


## Quality, budgets and evidence
Source: docs/governance/quality.md

# Quality, budgets and evidence

Issues #31–#32. `npm run check` executes DOM and native suites with test counts. Native module mocks demonstrate roles/state/callback/lifecycle contracts; real packed Expo/Metro consumers demonstrate platform resolution. Neither is physical output or assistive-technology certification.

Gates inspect actual generated package exports, platform imports, tokens/cue hashes, scoped anti-drift exceptions, packed consumer installs, every copyable example, SSR/hydration/StrictMode, docs static route/base paths, visual/browser states and measured gzip/assets. Negative tests deliberately introduce invalid exports, stale token output, budget regression, cross-platform imports and copied/obsolete tokens to prove failure paths.

Budgets are regression limits from the initial candidate measurements, not claims of production savings:

| Metric | Measured initial | Limit | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Individual DOM Button gzip (React external) | 706 B | 920 B | ~20% API/behavior fix headroom, overlay/audio/chart excluded; raised from 850 B for `href` and `glow` (903 B) |
| Individual Input gzip | 426 B | 440 B | Includes Field ownership validation and merged accessible descriptions; 55 B above the previous 371 B build. |
| Native Switch gzip (React/RN external) | 2,668 B | 2,750 B | Includes fixed controlled ownership and the transition diagnostic. Verifies no Slider/SVG/overlay/feedback imports. |
| Platform-neutral feedback contract gzip | 962 B | 1,200 B | ~25% headroom without device engines |
| Docs JS gzip, all lazy chunks | 204,877 B | 240,000 B | ~17% headroom; includes chart/code examples, not initial-load-only |
| Docs CSS | 124,111 B (with resizable drawer and per-place number motion); 139,812 B with SwapPanelBlock, Filter and the review-pass styles; 150,567 B with BarMark, AssetBalanceRow and AccountBlock ; 167,406 B with the blocks added after 0.5.2 (account, token action, manage position, target, position, language, reward and trade history) | 185,000 B | Tight headroom against the current Next CSS output; the gesture example remains lazy-loaded and Vaul injects its own runtime CSS rather than adding a second bundled stylesheet Raised for SwapPanelBlock, Filter and WalletAddress, with about 10 KB of headroom for further components. |
| Sans + Mono assets | 592,796 B | 600,000 B | Pins two approved faces; new script/face requires explicit review |
| Native fixture faces from `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts` (Sans 400/600, Mono 400) | 1,278,880 B | 1,400,000 B | Only the three registered faces; optional CJK and other weights stay unloaded. Every generated face hash is checked |
| Font binaries in web/shared tarballs (tokens, contracts, react, feedback, native) | 0 files | 0 files | Native faces ship only in `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts` (#64); `release:dry-run` fails otherwise and records `packedSizes` |
| Native four-cue WAV assets | 103,618 B | 110,000 B | ~6% headroom; no full engine/catalog assets |

The actual build report is `evidence/quality-report.json`. The committed copy, the release report and the browser acceptance files were copied from a Linux CI run (`evidence/ci-refresh.json`, #98), not regenerated locally. GitHub Actions now runs on self-hosted macOS ARM64 Mac minis; see [CI runners](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/ci-runners/). Failed quality and browser jobs upload fresh copies for review; green runs skip the upload. Bundles use explicit external React/RN peers, so figures measure HIG runtime contribution, not total installed/Metro app size. Production app/Pro/native before/after deltas require owning-repository builds and reviewed baselines; do not invent a percentage improvement. Export/dependency graph reports and packed tests enforce separation, while owning migrations must measure complete apps with equal data/toolchain.

Exceptions require path/rule, owner, reason and expiry. Approved brand geometry is exempt from literal-palette detection until review; unrelated primitive/palette copies fail. New repositories should run scoped gates on migrated surfaces and keep dated residuals rather than blanket exemptions.

Physical release review remains pending: iPhone Safari, Android Chrome, native iOS and Android, VoiceOver/TalkBack, large text/RTL, color/font fidelity, actual SFX/haptic output/latency/settings/interruption/background behavior. Coordinate upstream haptic#9. Release artifacts cannot change those “pending” rows into passes.

## Versioned visual regressions

The catalog browser gate captures and runs axe on every shipped state. Button, Field and Input additionally compare eight versioned mobile/reduced-motion screenshots in `tests/visual-baselines/<process.platform>/` (`linux` or `darwin`), and Slider compares two keyboard-focused captures (comfortable and compact density). Geometry changes fail; pixel changes above 2% fail after a 24-channel-value antialias tolerance on every OS. `tests/visual.test.ts` deliberately changes geometry and pixels to prove the gate fails. Baselines record current candidate rendering on that OS, not approved product parity or native-device fidelity. Do not reuse another OS image or raise the thresholds to hide a runner difference. Review an intentional change using CI captures, then run `HIG_UPDATE_VISUALS=1 node scripts/catalog-browser-smoke.mjs` against the production docs preview and commit the reviewed baseline images for that platform.

The required `candidate` check includes `browser` on macOS and `linux-visual` on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`. The Linux job installs only Playwright Chromium and runs `HIG_VISUAL_ONLY=1 node scripts/run-browser-gates.mjs`, which starts only the production docs preview and compares the representative catalog captures against `linux/`. It never enables baseline updates. `npm test` checks every platform directory against the shared capture names and catalog states, including both Slider focus densities; missing or extra images fail.

For Linux regeneration, push the intended CSS change and download the `hig-linux-visual-<commit SHA>` artifact from that revision's quality workflow (available on passing and failing runs). Review `artifacts/visual/` and the failure summary in `evidence/visual-actuals/`. Copy only the filenames already listed in `tests/visual-baselines/linux/` from the artifact's `artifacts/visual/` directory into that baseline directory (when adding a capture, include its new filename on both platforms). Commit the reviewed images and require the next Ubuntu comparison to pass. This uses the same locked Playwright version, Ubuntu runner, fonts and production build as verification, avoiding local Linux rendering differences. Never copy macOS captures into Linux or update baselines automatically during verification.


## Release candidates, semver and rollback
Source: docs/governance/release.md

# Release candidates, semver and rollback

Issue #32. The local release automation is **dry-run only**. It never invokes npm publication, GitHub release or git tag creation. Unsupported flags fail before artifact creation. The dry run does not request or use npm credentials; registry publication is confined to the maintainer-controlled workflow described below.

```sh
npm ci
npm run check
npm run examples:check
npm run quality
npm run generate:fonts   # Python with fonttools[woff]==4.61.1 and brotli==1.2.1
npm run smoke:packed
npm run smoke:packed-og
npm run smoke:packed-native
npm run smoke:packed-next
npm run smoke:packed-css
npm run smoke:packed-boundaries
npm run smoke:packed-chart-workspace
npm run release:dry-run -- --channel candidate
npm run release:dry-run -- --channel stable-simulation
```

Candidate mode stages `<version>-candidate.sha<commit>` package metadata and matching internal dependency versions. Stable-simulation stages the coordinated source version. Runtime contract/docs source version and source commit are recorded explicitly; neither source files nor git refs are version-mutated by the dry run. Each dry run rebuilds packages and docs before staging so ignored output cannot retain an older API. Both produce local tarballs, checked export/types/CSS/assets/files/dependency manifests, hashes, changelog, copied docs artifact and provenance report. `npm pack --ignore-scripts` packs already validated outputs, never publishes. Physical claims remain pending in every report.

The release dry run, `npm run quality`, `smoke:packed-native` and `smoke:packed-og` first check that the generated TTF faces exist and match their manifests (#98). If any face is missing or stale, they stop before building anything. The message names `npm run generate:fonts` and its Python pins and lists the affected files, instead of failing with a raw `ENOENT`. `packedSizes` in the report records the `@bloxwap/hig` tarball size and, for the `tokens` (no fonts), `native-fonts` and `og-fonts` entries, their file count, unpacked bytes, gzip-9 bytes and font-file count. The dry run fails if a font binary sits outside `native-fonts/fonts/` or `og-fonts/fonts/`, or if the `og-fonts` entry reaches 1,000,000 B compressed (#99). `smoke:packed-og` builds the documented `app/og/route.tsx` handler with Turbopack (the Next 16 default) and with `--webpack`. It serves each build with `next start`, and also as moved standalone output. Every face's SHA-256 has to match, so a loader that bundles only one face fails here.

The chart adapter ships as the `@bloxwap/hig/chart` entry (#96). The dry run fails unless `@bloxwap/hig` declares `@bloxwap/chart` as a required peer and never as an optional peer or dependency. The result is recorded in `chartAdapter` in the report. `npm run quality` applies the same rule to the source manifest and checks that no built `dist` file outside `chart/` imports `@bloxwap/chart`. `smoke:packed-boundaries` checks that the packed manifest has no `./react/chart` entry, that a React button bundle pulls no `@bloxwap/chart` code, and that `PriceChart` renders on the server with its required peer installed. `smoke:packed-chart-workspace` builds a host shaped like bloxwap/chart: an npm workspace whose `packages/chart` provides `@bloxwap/chart` 0.4.0, plus `apps/docs`, which depends on it and on the packed `@bloxwap/hig` through a `file:` spec. The smoke deletes `package-lock.json` and `node_modules` and installs with `legacy-peer-deps=false` and `strict-peer-deps=true`. It then asserts four things. The lockfile keeps `packages/chart` and the `node_modules/@bloxwap/chart` link. `npm ls` is clean. Node and esbuild resolve `@bloxwap/chart` (including the `@bloxwap/hig/chart` entry's lazy `@bloxwap/chart/react`) from the app into the workspace. The host's `HIGProvider` messages reach `PriceChart`. It repeats the checks after `npm ci` and requires a second `npm install` to leave the lockfile byte-identical. Every scenario runs twice: once with the ambient npm (in CI, the npm bundled with Node 24.22.1) and once with the npm pinned in `packageManager` (11.6.1, the version chart reported), which is installed into a scratch prefix. A control run repacks `@bloxwap/hig` with the old optional peer and records in `evidence/packed-chart-workspace-smoke.json` whether each npm still drops the workspace.

CI checks out PR source, installs locked peers, executes web/native/SSR/Metro/example/visual/accessibility/budget gates and uploads review artifacts. A provenance record identifies source commit, package/contract/docs versions and hashes; it is not an npm registry provenance attestation or a release. Artifact inspection checks exports, licenses, optional peers and only approved assets. No example app implementation is included in runtime packages.

Publication gates are tracked in `planning/release-blockers.json`. The owner
explicitly authorized the first coordinated npm publication, including the
customizable primary-colour provider, on 2026-10-23; see
[the release authorization](https://github.com/bloxwap/hig/blob/main/evidence/release/owner-authorization-2026-10-23.md)
and [PR #141](https://github.com/bloxwap/hig/pull/141).

Releases 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 used an organization token. Release 0.1.2 uses npm trusted publishing; subsequent workflow executions have no token fallback. Released SFX/Haptic 0.2.0 backends satisfy their setup gates. Physical-device and native-font acceptance use the
existing dated owner attestation from PR #131. Source-parity and named adoption decisions are accepted in #57. Owning-product
rollout and six non-English glossary entries retain scoped exceptions through
2027-01-15; real wallet acceptance and rollback retirement remain open in #110.
These exceptions do not turn unobserved product or physical checks into passes.
The immutable-tag, package-set, tarball-hash and CI checks still apply.

Semver:

- **Major:** breaking changes to token meaning or appearance, typography scale, layout, accessibility or action behaviour, or semantic feedback mapping.
- **Minor:** compatible additions.
- **Patch:** verified fixes.

Deprecation names the alternative, a migration codemod or checklist, and the owning consumers from `planning/adoption.json`. A deprecated export keeps working for at least one minor release and 30 days, and is removed only in the next major release after consumer PRs are merged or have dated exceptions (see the contribution chapter). Keep code/examples/API/citations at the same source commit; separate package prerelease identifiers are explicit in artifact metadata.

Rollback for an owning pilot: keep the previous package artifacts and lockfile, disable the host feature flag, restore prior renderer/backend imports and rebuild. Keep saved feedback/business data backward-compatible; never erase prior choices. Remove old assets only after production and physical-device proof. A future published rollback would require separate release authorization and package provenance; this task performs none.

## Maintainer-controlled registry publication (#56)

The local dry-run command remains unable to publish, create tags, or create releases. In the separate `publish.yml` workflow, the GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` `publish` job is the explicit exception to the self-hosted runner policy; `prerequisites` runs on the minis. Publishing a GitHub release with a `v*` tag triggers it; maintainers can also dispatch it manually with the existing tag as both the workflow ref and input, for example `gh workflow run publish.yml --ref v0.1.2 -f tag=v0.1.2`. It validates the tag and checks out `refs/tags/<tag>` so every gate runs against that tag commit. Before publication, `prerequisites` fails unless the `npm-release` environment has required reviewers and `quality.yml` succeeded for this exact tag commit. Manual dispatch rejects a branch ref because the OIDC provenance source must identify the release tag, then resolves that tag SHA. The `publish` job needs the unchanged self-hosted `security` release scan, these prerequisites, all validation lanes and artifact preparation, waits for `npm-release` environment approval, and verifies that the checked-out tag still matches the approved SHA. Checkout does not persist credentials.

The workflow re-runs the build, lint, type, web/native test and quality gates in parallel self-hosted validation lanes. A separate self-hosted preparation job rebuilds the stable-simulation artifact and runs `node scripts/verify-release.mjs`. The hosted publication job waits for every validation lane, preparation and security, then verifies the downloaded report digest, source and tarball hashes again before publishing. The tag, source commit and coordinated version must match; the release must contain exactly the `@bloxwap/hig` package and its tarball hash must match. Every gate in `planning/release-blockers.json` must be `cleared`, `satisfied`, or have a valid `approved-exception` with a named approver, approval link and unexpired review date. Expired or undocumented exceptions and uncommitted source changes fail. It never creates the tag or GitHub release for the maintainer.

An npm owner must configure a **Trusted Publisher for `@bloxwap/hig`** with repository **bloxwap/hig**, workflow **publish.yml**, and environment **npm-release**. The GitHub `npm-release` environment is configured with `joeblau` as required reviewer. The eight 0.1.x `@bloxwap/hig-*` packages had their trusted publishers configured and read back using authenticated owner access on 2026-10-27, and 0.1.2 was published through them. `@bloxwap/hig` 0.2.0 was published manually by the owner, so its registry metadata names no `trustedPublisher`; the first workflow release of `@bloxwap/hig` must confirm its npm setting. Changing this workflow alone does not configure npm. The token-published [0.1.0](https://github.com/bloxwap/hig/releases/tag/v0.1.0) and [0.1.1](https://github.com/bloxwap/hig/releases/tag/v0.1.1) releases predate this migration; their exact source commits are the recorded legacy exceptions below.

Publication uses `contents: read`, `id-token: write`, OIDC trusted publishing and `npm publish --provenance`. The transitional `NPM_TOKEN` fallback is removed. Release 0.1.2's registry metadata identifies GitHub Actions and each package's configured `trustedPublisher` ID; signed provenance is verified separately. Provenance alone does not identify the authentication method. The shared organization secret is not deleted because other repositories use it; this workflow no longer references it. The ephemeral hosted runner uses Node 24.22.1 and explicitly installs npm@11.6.1 (the repository's `packageManager` pin), satisfying the [npm trusted-publishing CLI minimum of 11.5.1](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/). The self-hosted release jobs use job-local npm, the existing CPython setup, and the native-font cache. Browser installation and consumer checks run on the minis; the publication runner needs neither Python nor Playwright.

Only after those gates does the workflow publish the exact verified `@bloxwap/hig` tarball. An already published version is logged and skipped so an interrupted run can resume. Successful publishes are recorded in `artifacts/published-packages.txt`; the workflow uploads this manifest as publication evidence. Registry lanes verify provenance for the release set regardless of the manifest. Registry smoke always checks every tarball's SHA-256 against the verified artifact, checks the SLSA statement's exact source commit, workflow, tag, package and SHA-512 digest, and runs `npm audit signatures` to verify the registry signatures and provenance bundles. Provenance remains required when an interrupted publication resumes and skips existing packages, and when the smoke runs without a publish manifest. The only legacy exemptions are token-published 0.1.0 at source `bdf8d07014fea5e69ea51a061b82707661a9d701` and 0.1.1 at source `6f4dd060e0985be644d255154aa7a0277cdde27f`; a supplied missing or invalid manifest fails closed. The manifest is uploaded with the verification artifacts.

Five self-hosted registry lanes then run independent web/SSR, Next hydration/font, and all three supported native Metro/Expo profiles against registry versions. Each lane verifies hashes, signatures and provenance before its consumer, and all lanes must pass. Running `smoke:registry` locally without a lane selector still executes every consumer.

Newly published exact versions can briefly return npm metadata `E404` while registry visibility catches up. That lookup retries at most thirty-one times, ten seconds apart (five minutes of bounded visibility retries), with a 15-second limit per npm command. Other npm errors, malformed metadata, unavailable tarballs, hash mismatches and consumer failures still fail normally. An exhausted metadata-visibility retry requires investigation; once the version is visible, rerun the unchanged release tag. A published package defect requires a corrected new version. Automation never unpublishes or overwrites a registry version, and a skipped version with different bytes still fails the registry hash check.


## Installation and citation
Source: docs/installation.md

# Installation and citation

HIG ships as one npm package, `@bloxwap/hig`. Every surface is a subpath export of it: tokens, contracts, React and React Native components, the chart adapter, feedback, native fonts and OG fonts. Local dry-run tarballs and CI artifacts remain available for testing unreleased changes. Registry releases verify the exact package hash and independent web, Next and native consumers.

```sh
npm install @bloxwap/hig@0.8.1
```

| Entry | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `@bloxwap/hig/tokens`, `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/css` | Semantic tokens and the role CSS |
| `@bloxwap/hig/contracts` | Platform-neutral types, formatting, feedback, announcements, messages and the generated avatar face |
| `@bloxwap/hig/react/<component>`, `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` | Web components and their scoped CSS |
| `@bloxwap/hig/native/<component>` | React Native components |
| `@bloxwap/hig/chart` | `AltimeterChart` live price chart and `OutcomeChart`; `PriceChart` and `chartTheme` for `@bloxwap/chart` |
| `@bloxwap/hig/feedback`, `@bloxwap/hig/feedback/<adapter>` | Optional sound and haptic feedback |
| `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts` | Static native TTFs and their manifest |
| `@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts`, `@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts/node` | Satori / `next/og` card faces |

Every renderer, device and overlay peer is optional, so install only the peers of the entries you import. The one required peer is `@bloxwap/chart` `^0.3.0` (see [Optional chart, sound and haptics](#optional-chart-sound-and-haptics)).

### Moving from the 0.1 packages

HIG 0.1 published eight packages: `@bloxwap/hig-tokens`, `-contracts`, `-react`, `-native`, `-chart`, `-feedback`, `-native-fonts` and `-og-fonts`. From 0.2.0 they are deprecated on npm in favour of `@bloxwap/hig`. Replace them with the one dependency and change the hyphen after `hig` to a slash in every import. Entry names and exports are unchanged:

| 0.1 import | 0.2 import |
| --- | --- |
| `@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css` | `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/css` |
| `@bloxwap/hig-react/button` | `@bloxwap/hig/react/button` |
| `@bloxwap/hig-native/provider` | `@bloxwap/hig/native/provider` |
| `@bloxwap/hig-chart` | `@bloxwap/hig/chart` |
| `@bloxwap/hig-og-fonts/node` | `@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts/node` |

In Next, list `'@bloxwap/hig'` in `transpilePackages` or `serverExternalPackages` instead of the old package names.

## Shared UI icons (next release)

Web and native components use `@bloxwap/icons` from [bloxwap/icons](https://github.com/bloxwap/icons). Install `@bloxwap/icons@^0.1.0` alongside HIG when using these components. It remains an optional peer so contracts, tokens, fonts and other independent entries do not require it.

Native icons use `expo-image`. Run `npx expo install expo-image` in the host app, then rebuild the development client so its native module is linked. Web icons render inline SVG; native icons render a tinted local SVG image. HIG keeps its icons decorative, with the surrounding control or text providing the accessible name.

## React / Vite

Run `npm ci && npm run build && npm run smoke:packed`. The smoke script installs tarballs into an independent temporary consumer and builds the fixture. For a host app install `@bloxwap/hig` plus compatible React/DOM peers. Import `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/css` and `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` once; import individual components such as `@bloxwap/hig/react/button`. Pin @bloxwap/font 0.1.4 and choose only the required families/scripts using asset URL @font-face rules named `'Bloxwap Sans'` and `'Bloxwap Mono'`; HIG controls read `--hig-font-sans`/`--hig-font-mono`, which fall back to those literal families. The included fixture has Sans and Mono only, and its browser smoke checks that `.hig-button` and `.hig-number` render loaded Bloxwap faces. Never copy font binaries or component folders.

### Component CSS and the opt-in base

All three stylesheet exports (`tokens/css`, `react/css`, and `react/css/base`) ship TypeScript declarations. No local `declare module` shim is needed, including with `noUncheckedSideEffectImports` enabled. CI checks bare imports from the packed package with TypeScript 6.0.3 and 7.0.2 in Bundler and NodeNext resolution modes.

`@bloxwap/hig/react/css` styles HIG components only. Every rule is scoped to a HIG class, for example `.hig-button`, `.hig-table` cells, `.hig-range` or `.hig-surface[data-severity]`. The box-sizing and focus ring rules use `:where()` on HIG classes, so they keep the specificity of a bare element rule and host CSS can still override them. Loading the file has no effect on plain `table`, `th`, `td`, `input[type=range]`, `[data-severity]` or the focus outline of a non-HIG element. Hosts that load HIG on some routes only can rely on this: Next.js keeps a route's stylesheet after a client navigation, and the scoped file then has no side effects on the other routes (#95).

The page-wide element defaults are a separate, opt-in entry, `@bloxwap/hig/react/css/base`:

| Rule | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `* { box-sizing: border-box }` | Border-box sizing on every element |
| `:focus-visible` | The 2px `--hig-focus` ring with a 3px offset on every focusable element |
| `table`, `th`, `td` | Collapsed borders, full width, 12px cells with a `--hig-border` rule |
| `input[type='range']` | `--hig-action` accent, 48px minimum height, full width |

Import the base only when HIG owns the whole page, and import it before the component CSS:

```ts
import '@bloxwap/hig/tokens/css';
import '@bloxwap/hig/react/css/base'; // optional: page-wide element defaults
import '@bloxwap/hig/react/css';
```

These are the rules that `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` applied to the whole page before #95, so a host that adds the base sees no change. The HIG docs site and the web and Next fixtures import it. HIG components look the same with or without the base. `npm run smoke:packed-react-css` checks this. It installs the packed tokens, contracts and React tarballs into an empty consumer and renders Table, Slider, Button and Alert to static markup. Then, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, it compares three script-free pages: tokens only, tokens plus `@bloxwap/hig/react/css`, and tokens plus the base and the component CSS. The plain table, cells, range, box-sizing, `[data-severity]` and keyboard focus outline must compute the same with the component CSS as with tokens only. The base page must change them, which proves the check can see a leak. The components must compute the same with and without the base. `npm run smoke:packed-boundaries` also checks that both entries resolve through package exports in a bundler and that the component CSS has no selector outside HIG classes.

### Radix overlay peers and Fumadocs

The four Radix packages are optional peers with caret ranges: `@radix-ui/react-dialog ^1.1.15`, `@radix-ui/react-popover ^1.1.15`, `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu ^2.1.16` and `@radix-ui/react-tooltip ^1.2.8`. Install them only for `@bloxwap/hig/react/overlay`, `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks`, or `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/trade-entry` (dialog only for the blocks). `@bloxwap/hig/react/blocks/swap-sheet` presents the swap panel in a gesture sheet and needs `vaul`, like `gesture-sheet`; `blocks/swap-panel-block` itself needs no overlay peer. Hosts that already use Radix, such as Fumadocs, share their copy: `npm run smoke:packed-fumadocs` installs the packed React tarball next to fumadocs-ui 16.17.3 with strict peers and `npm ci`, asserts every `@radix-ui/*` package appears once, and renders the overlays on the resolved current releases. The workspace fixtures keep testing the lower bounds. Do not set `legacy-peer-deps` for HIG.

The separate optional `@bloxwap/hig/react/gesture-sheet` entry requires `vaul ^1.1.2`; Vaul brings its Radix Dialog dependency. Ordinary overlay and action entries do not load Vaul. Retain the host's existing input repositioning, handle-only, background scaling and viewport layout flags; see [gesture sheet composition](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/overlays/#optional-web-gesture-backend). `npm run smoke:packed-boundaries` verifies both absence in core consumers and resolution of the gesture entry after the explicit backend install.

### Sonner toasts

`@bloxwap/hig/react/toast` exports `Toaster`, `toast()` and `dismissToast()`, which raise the HIG toast capsule through [Sonner](https://sonner.emilkowal.ski/). `@bloxwap/hig/native/toast` exports the same names for React Native, on HIG's own host; see [Status & feedback](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/status/#transient-toasts-toaster-and-toast). `sonner ^2.0.0` is an optional peer needed only by `@bloxwap/hig/react/toast`; no other entry loads it. Mount `<Toaster/>` once inside `HIGProvider`: while it is mounted, `InstallCommand` raises its copy result as a toast. Without a mounted toaster `InstallCommand` shows the result inline, as before. The controlled `Toast` in `@bloxwap/hig/react/status` needs no backend.

### Confetti

`@bloxwap/hig/react/confetti` and `@bloxwap/hig/native/confetti` export `confetti()` and `Confetti`, HIG's own confetti with canvas-confetti's options and no third-party package. The web entry needs no peer and no stylesheet. The native entry uses the optional Reanimated and Worklets peers, like `animated-number`. Both read the flight from `@bloxwap/hig/contracts/confetti`. See [Confetti](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/status/#confetti).

### Wallet address QR codes

`@bloxwap/hig/react/wallet-address` and `@bloxwap/hig/native/wallet-address` export `WalletAddress`, which draws its QR code with [Cuer](https://cuer.sh). `cuer` (`>=0.0.3 <0.1.0`) is an optional peer needed only by those two entries; the native entry also needs `react-native-svg`. `VerticalAddress` is in the `data` entries and needs neither. A host without `cuer` (or, on native, without `react-native-svg`) imports the same `WalletAddress` from `@bloxwap/hig/react/wallet-address-core` or `@bloxwap/hig/native/wallet-address-core`, which need neither peer, and passes its own drawing of the code as `qr`.

`@bloxwap/hig/react/qr-code` and `@bloxwap/hig/native/qr-code` export `QRCode`, a QR code in the same style that HIG encodes itself: no `cuer`, and on native only `react-native-svg`. On web the `wallet-address-core` entry draws it when no `qr` is passed; on native pass it as `qr`. See the [financial data chapter](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/financial-data/#qrcode).

### Generated avatars

`@bloxwap/hig/react/avatar` and `@bloxwap/hig/native/avatar` export `Avatar`, which can draw a face generated from a seed such as a wallet address. The native entry draws it with `react-native-svg`, an optional peer needed there. A native host without that peer keeps importing `Avatar` from `@bloxwap/hig/native/status`, which shows the image or the initials and loads no SVG. See [Status & feedback](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/status/#avatar).

## Brand accent

Pass `primaryColor` to the web or native `HIGProvider` to theme primary actions
for another brand, for example `<HIGProvider primaryColor='#ff0000'>` for a red
Tap Trade TV theme. Use the brand's opaque sRGB hex (`#RGB` or `#RRGGBB`).
HIG selects readable primary button text and inherits the accent through nested
providers. Omit it to keep Bloxwap green. See [primary brand colour](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/platform/#primary-brand-colour)
for portal styling, native colour spaces, and contrast guidance.

## SSR and Next client boundaries

Run `npm run smoke:ssr`, `npm run build:next` and `npm run smoke:packed-next`. Token/formatting imports and button/provider SSR are deterministic. Components with hooks carry `use client` in their emitted modules. In Next, import HIG CSS in the app layout (or in the route layouts that use HIG; the component CSS is scoped, see above) and put interactive example state in a client component; keep wallet/network logic with the host. Next's published Bloxwap font loaders remain owned upstream.

Fonts in Next: put the `@bloxwap/font` loader variables on `<html>`, for example `<html className={`${BloxwapSans.variable} ${BloxwapMono.variable}`}>`. The loaders register hashed family names, so HIG never matches a literal `'Bloxwap Sans'` there. Instead `--hig-font-sans` and `--hig-font-mono` in `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/css` resolve `var(--font-bloxwap-sans)` and `var(--font-bloxwap-mono)` first and fall back to the literal families. No bridge CSS is needed. If a host keeps its own variable names, override the roles on `:root` after importing the tokens CSS: `:root { --hig-font-sans: var(--my-sans), 'Bloxwap Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; }`. The variables must be defined on `<html>` (not `<body>`), because the roles resolve on `:root`. `npm run smoke:packed-next` serves the packed consumer and checks, in Chromium, that `.hig-button` and `.hig-number` compute to a loaded Bloxwap face (`document.fonts.check` plus the `FontFace` status). Next 16.4.0 (webpack), React 19.2 and the published Bloxwap Sans Next loader are verified in the dedicated production fixture; other Next versions require host checks. Verify hydration, stable IDs and StrictMode before adopting a host version.

## Open Graph card fonts

Satori, `next/og` `ImageResponse` and `@vercel/og` read TTF/OTF but not WOFF2, and `@bloxwap/font` ships only WOFF2. Docs and marketing sites that render OG cards install `@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts` as a build-time dev dependency. Do not use `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts` for this (#99). The package holds five static Latin faces: Bloxwap Sans 400, 500, 700 and 900, and Bloxwap Mono 500. These are the faces the chart, sfx, agent-cli and tapsiren cards use. It packs to about 0.84 MB; the native fonts package is 4.4 MB. `npm run generate:fonts` copies the five faces byte for byte from `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts`, so each SHA-256 in its manifest equals the native manifest entry. The release dry run records the packed size in `packedSizes.ogFonts` and fails at 1,000,000 B.

Node runtime (route handlers with `export const runtime = 'nodejs'`, or static OG export scripts):

```tsx
import {ImageResponse} from 'next/og';
import {loadOgFonts} from '@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts/node';

const fonts = await loadOgFonts(); // {name, data, weight, style}[]; throws if any TTF's SHA-256 differs from the manifest
export function GET() {
  return new ImageResponse(<div style={{display: 'flex', fontFamily: 'Bloxwap Sans', fontWeight: 700}}>Bloxwap</div>, {width: 1200, height: 630, fonts});
}
```

This works in a Next 16 route handler with the default Turbopack build and with `next build --webpack`. Turbopack copies the five faces into `.next/server`, so `output: 'standalone'` works even after you move it. webpack reads the faces from `node_modules/@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts/fonts` at the absolute path it had at build time. If a webpack standalone build runs from another directory, add `serverExternalPackages: ['@bloxwap/hig']` to `next.config`. Earlier 0.1.0 candidate builds made each face's path from a template URL, and under Turbopack every face read the same file. The route then failed with `BloxwapSans.ttf: SHA-256 f969fd1e… does not match the manifest`.

Pass a subset if you need fewer faces: `loadOgFonts(ogFonts.filter(f => f.weight >= 700))`, with `ogFonts` imported from `@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts`. Edge and Workers runtimes cannot read `node_modules` at request time. Copy `@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts/fonts/<asset>` into a gitignored build folder at build time. Before you write each file, check it against `fontManifest.outputs[asset]` (from the package root, or as JSON at `@bloxwap/hig/og-fonts/manifest`), as tapsiren's `copy-og-fonts.mjs` does. Plain Node ESM scripts outside Next import `next/og.js`, because `next` has no exports map. `npm run smoke:packed-og` installs the packed tarball next to `next@16.4.0` in a clean consumer. It hashes every exported TTF against both manifests and renders 1200×630 PNG cards through `ImageResponse`: each Sans weight must render differently, and none may match the default font. It also requires `readOgFont` to reject a tampered face. It then builds an `app/og/route.tsx` handler with the code above and checks it four ways: Turbopack and `--webpack`, each under `next start`; Turbopack `output: 'standalone'`; and webpack standalone with `serverExternalPackages`. Each standalone build is moved to another directory with the consumer's `node_modules` hidden. Every face must come back with its own SHA-256, and every card must match the plain Node render byte for byte. Results go to `evidence/packed-og-smoke.json`.

## Expo / React Native

Run `npm run smoke:packed-native` after packed artifacts are built, or `npm run start -w hig-native-fixture` for the device gallery. Matrix: RN 0.81.5 with Expo SDK 54 and React 19.1.0, and RN 0.83.10 with Expo SDK 55 and React 19.2.0 (#68), Metro as locked. `npm run smoke:packed-native -- --profile rn-0.83` installs the same fixture with the SDK 55 versions from `fixtures/native/profiles.json`; CI exports both consumers for Android and iOS. `@bloxwap/hig/native` declares `react-native` `^0.81.5 || ^0.83.10`, so RN 0.82 and 0.84+ are outside the tested range. Native consumers install the tokens/contracts/native packages; optional feedback installs its package and explicit Expo backend peers. Slider and SVG peers are only needed by their family entries. Import `@bloxwap/hig/native/button`, not the DOM renderer. Dynamic Type remains enabled; native targets stay 48. Keyboard/safe-area/back behavior belongs to the native host and its supported OS.

The optional `gesture-sheet` entry uses Gorhom Bottom Sheet, Gesture Handler, Safe Area Context, Reanimated and Worklets, with `GestureHandlerRootView`, `SafeAreaProvider` and `BottomSheetModalProvider` supplied by the host. The optional `animated-number` entry uses Reanimated and Worklets for per-place motion; ordinary `data` readouts remain engine-free. The optional `toast` entry uses Reanimated, Worklets, Gesture Handler and Safe Area Context, with `GestureHandlerRootView` and `SafeAreaProvider` supplied by the host. The optional `confetti` entry uses Reanimated and Worklets too. Install only the peers for the entries used, at versions compatible with the host's Expo/RN SDK.

Install Expo native peers with `npx expo install` (for example, on SDK 54, `expo-asset ~12.0.13` and `expo-constants ~18.0.14` alongside `expo-font`/`expo-audio`; on SDK 55, `expo-asset ~55.0.20` and `expo-constants ~55.0.17`). Expo 54 autolinking links the copy resolved from the app root; a hoisted SDK 57 `expo-asset` pulled by `expo-audio`'s `*` peer compiles away and the app fails at launch with `Cannot find native module 'ExpoAsset'` (observed on the iOS Simulator). `verifyExpoNativeModules` in `scripts/native-compatibility.mjs` guards the fixture and packed consumer. `HIGProvider` follows the OS layout direction (`I18nManager.isRTL`) unless `direction` is passed. On RN 0.83 Android, a per-app RTL locale (for example Arabic set in the system's app language settings) does not set `I18nManager.isRTL`, so pass `direction` explicitly there (#86).

`@bloxwap/hig/native` ships one small Android library (`android/`, `com.bloxwap.hig.HIGPackage`) that React Native and Expo autolinking pick up in development and release builds (`npx expo prebuild`, `npx expo run:android`). It adds Android set-progress to `Slider`; nothing else depends on it, and in Expo Go the Slider falls back to increment/decrement only. iOS needs no native code.

Simulator/emulator verification: `scripts/native-sim/` builds the packed candidate gallery as real Release apps and drives them with XCUITest (iOS Simulator) and UiAutomation instrumentation, uiautomator and TalkBack (Android emulator). `prepare-app.sh <app-dir> <udid> rn-0.83` builds the RN 0.83 / Expo 55 gallery, and `compare-runs.mjs` compares it with an RN 0.81.5 run of the same candidate. Results and residual physical-hardware limits are in `evidence/native-sim/` (RN 0.83: `evidence/native-sim/rn-0.83/`).

WOFF2 is not a native font asset. `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts` ships 15 static Bloxwap Sans/Mono (plus Korean and Simplified Chinese Sans) TTFs generated reproducibly from pinned Font 0.1.2 sources, with a typed `fontManifest` export and `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts/manifest`. Install it alongside the tokens, contracts and native packages, then `require('@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts/fonts/BloxwapSans.ttf')` and register the faces with expo-font before setting the native provider fontFamily, as the gallery does. `@bloxwap/hig/tokens` no longer contains font binaries (#64); see [native font migration](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/migration/native/#native-fonts-moved-out-of-hig-tokens). Rasterization on physical displays remains part of #55. New repositories follow `docs/governance/new-repository.md`.

## Tokens only / plain CSS / Tailwind

Install the tokens package alone and import CSS variables or typed tokens. No React/RN/audio peer is required. Plain HTML uses semantic `--hig-*` roles.

`@bloxwap/hig/tokens/css` defines every role a plain CSS host needs, so nobody has to read the manifest or generate role files:

| Roles | Example | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Color | `--hig-surface`, `--hig-action` | sRGB, then OKLCH/P3 in `@supports` |
| Space | `--hig-space-md` | `xs`–`xxxl`, `section`, in rem |
| Safe area | `--hig-safe-area-toastOffset` | `chromeGutter` `sheetContentGutter` `toastOffset` `fullscreenMin` `axisChromeTop` `axisChromeBottom`, in rem; offsets added on top of device insets, see [safe area](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/safe-area/) |
| Font | `--hig-font-sans`, `--hig-font-mono` | `@bloxwap/font` Next variable, then literal family |
| Radius | `--hig-radius-md`, `--hig-radius-pill` | `sm` `md` `lg` `xl` in rem; `pill` 9999px |
| Type | `--hig-type-body-size`, `--hig-type-body-line-height`, `--hig-type-body-weight`, `--hig-type-body` | `caption` `label` `body` `title` `display`; the bare role is a `font` shorthand in Sans |
| Motion | `--hig-motion-duration-base`, `--hig-motion-easing-standard` | `fast` `base` `slow` ms; 0ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` or `[data-hig-motion='reduced']` |
| Density | `--hig-density-control`, `--hig-density-compact-gap` | `control` `target` `gap` per mode; the unprefixed roles follow `[data-hig-density='compact']` |

```css
@import '@bloxwap/hig/tokens/css';
.card { border-radius: var(--hig-radius-lg); padding: var(--hig-space-lg); font: var(--hig-type-body); }
.card h2 { font: var(--hig-type-title); }
.card button { min-height: var(--hig-density-control); transition: background var(--hig-motion-duration-fast) var(--hig-motion-easing-standard); }
```

`npm run smoke:packed-css` proves this path. It installs only the packed `@bloxwap/hig` tarball into an empty consumer, links `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/css` from a script-free HTML page whose own stylesheet uses nothing but the roles, and checks the computed radius, type, motion and density values in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including 0ms durations under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and `[data-hig-motion='reduced']` and the compact values under `[data-hig-density='compact']`. It fails if the page requests anything other than the HTML, its stylesheet and the token CSS, so the manifest is never read.

Tailwind may reference these values through host configuration; HIG does not require content scans or a shadcn registry. Native uses dp and explicit hex/channel maps; do not feed CSS functions or rename rem to dp. The audited monorepo web/native rem roots are both 16; HIG supports StyleSheet rather than claiming a verified NativeWind consumer. See the source-reconciliation chapter for native font generation and registration.

## Optional chart, sound and haptics

`npm run smoke:packed-compat` checks the packed package with the minimum versions computed from its web peer ranges: chart 0.3.0, haptic 0.2.0, and sfx 0.2.0. CI runs this alongside the current-version tests. It checks consumer types and adapter source against those installed peers, renders chart and haptic entries on the server, and invokes the sound adapter without browser globals.

Chart is DOM-only and lazy. The adapter is the `@bloxwap/hig/chart` entry (#96): install `@bloxwap/chart` `^0.3.0` and supply a textual summary. `@bloxwap/chart` is the only required peer of `@bloxwap/hig`, and no other entry imports it. It is never optional, so a host with a workspace `@bloxwap/chart` (like bloxwap/chart) can regenerate its lockfile from scratch with strict peers and keep the workspace link. See the [charts chapter](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/components/chart/). Native uses labeled readouts/lists. Feedback install paths, preferences, iOS physical-tap limitations and Expo backends are in the feedback chapters. Keep essential outcome text available with both channels off.

## Stable citations and upgrades

Cite “Bloxwap HIG <installed package version>, chapter/anchor” plus an immutable GitHub commit permalink. Branch and docs preview links are mutable. Upgrade tokens, contracts, renderer, docs/examples and semantic cue mapping together; compare API behavior and adopt behind a rollback flag. Token appearance and accessibility behavior changes require semver review. The GitHub release links the immutable source tag and the registry validation workflow.

The native fixture pins React **19.1.0**, matching the RN 0.81.5 renderer exactly; the RN 0.83 profile pins **19.2.0**, matching the RN 0.83.10 renderer. Web/Next/Fumadocs fixtures use React 19.2.0. Metro explicitly resolves every native `react`/`react/*` import to the native fixture's version so shared-workspace code cannot load web React. Quality and packed-native checks compare the installed version to the version RN's Paper and Fabric renderers are built for (RN 0.83 no longer throws on a mismatch, so the check reads the renderer build itself); a successful Metro bundle alone does not prove runtime compatibility. The packed check also fails when a declared `@bloxwap/hig/native` or `@bloxwap/hig/feedback` peer range rejects a version the consumer installed.

Chapter titles have no independent version stamps. The generated site and LLM export use the workspace `package.json` version. Cite the version you consumed and an immutable commit permalink; the live site can contain unreleased changes.

`planning/anchors.json` records every rendered guide heading ID using Fumadocs’ GitHub slugger. CI compares it with the latest released `v*` tag containing that manifest (stable tags only). Until a release contains it, CI bootstraps from the committed manifest at `HEAD`, comparing it with freshly parsed chapters; regeneration alone cannot hide a heading rename. The initial manifest establishes the baseline for pre-manifest releases.

A removed anchor requires an entry in `planning/renamed-anchors.json` under `renamedAnchors`, keyed by the old `/docs/guides/chapter/#anchor`, with `to` naming an existing replacement and `note` explaining the migration. This committed map is the deprecation record; prefer retaining the old heading or an explicit heading ID when possible. CI validates replacement targets and notes, checks generated-manifest drift, and checks links and TOC IDs against the built HTML.


## Native application pilot (#35)
Source: docs/migration/native.md

# Native application pilot (#35)

Owner: Joe Blau (accepted in #57). Status on 2026-10-15: [monorepo#4540](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/pull/4540) migrates the app's settings, entry, logout, sound card and demo number to HIG `0.1.0-candidate.shac32771dc`, with one HIG feedback controller and 15 duplicate fonts removed. It loads the faces from `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts` (#64) and passes translated `messages` (#62). It also drops the local Switch, Alert and Text workarounds (#67), and passes `direction` to `HIGProvider` on Android (#86). It was verified on the iOS Simulator and Android emulator and merged as `2f636e8fe` on 2026-10-16. Physical-device certification retains the dated owner-attested exception in #55. Subsequent native rollout and registry adoption are merged in monorepo#4620/#4629/#4737. Merged [monorepo#4826](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/pull/4826) adopts HIG 0.1.2 on RN 0.88 / Expo 58 and removes the temporary ref cast, closing #4776.

Workarounds the app can drop at its next candidate refresh (a candidate built from `74f4f6a` or later; tracked in #115):

- **Busy Button name (#94):** delete the `HigActionButton` wrapper's `higButtonAccessibilityLabel`. Button now sets the name itself: `{label} · {busy}` on iOS and `{label}` on Android, where React Native adds its own busy word, so Korean no longer reads `처리 중` twice.
- **Display P3 (#93):** set `colorSpace='display-p3'` on the root `HIGProvider` and drop the local `nativeColors.iosDisplayP3` lookup for the Button fill (see [Native colour space](#native-colour-space-93)).
- **Button text (#92):** the label and busy suffix now follow the provider `maxFontSizeMultiplier` and use the 600 face. Re-capture the large-text and fr/ko screens.
- **Direction (#86):** `localeDirection` from `@bloxwap/hig/native/provider` can replace the app's own direction lookup. HIG is certified on React Native 0.83.10 / Expo SDK 55 (#68). No tactile, audible or VoiceOver observation is claimed.

Pilot: font registration → dp/sRGB token mapping → amount/selection/review sheet → visible async outcome → independent feedback settings. The Expo gallery proves candidate packaging and contract examples, not the owning app's native build.

Checklist:
- [ ] Record actual RN/Expo/Metro/autolinking versions, source commit, old ui-native/token/font/audio wrappers, screenshots and native bundle/assets/latency baseline.
- [ ] Register the pinned static TTF faces from `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts` and its typed `fontManifest`; register before setting family. Do not treat WOFF2 or an invented native family as success.
- [ ] Map dp and legacy NativeWind rem roots explicitly. Keep Dynamic Type, 48 targets, logical RTL layout, safe areas, keyboard avoidance, native back and labelled fields/errors.
- [ ] On RN 0.83, pass `HIGProvider direction={localeDirection(getLocales()[0])}` if the app supports RTL: an Android per-app Arabic or Hebrew locale does not reach `I18nManager.isRTL` ([localization](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/foundations/localization/#native-direction-from-the-host-locale), #86).
- [ ] Preview native import codemods, using individual switch/checkbox/range entries; wire optional SVG/Slider/Expo audio/haptic peers only where used. Retain platform-specific descriptions and host callbacks.
- [ ] Preserve raw financial strings, order/network logic, stable list identity and quiet live numbers. Use labelled list/readout native chart alternative unless a real supported native engine is reviewed.
- [ ] Read old sound/haptic settings with a host migration adapter before writing v1 key. Keep explicit false choices, volume and motion independent; handle corrupt/missing storage conservatively.
- [ ] Hook AppState/interruption/background and dispose cached players/listeners. Test muted channels, missing assets, backend rejection, repeated values, busy/disabled, canceled scroll/drag and unsupported hardware.
- [ ] Build the real app for iOS and Android. Observe large text, long translations, Arabic/Hebrew RTL, VoiceOver/TalkBack, orientation, keyboard/sheets, reduced motion and every feedback combination on devices.
- [ ] Record actual device/OS/settings and audible/tactile output, latency, silent-mode/interruption/background behavior. Reuse upstream haptic#9 review; simulator/mocks remain API evidence only.
- [ ] Remove duplicated source/assets/backend wrappers after device builds confirm references and autolinking are gone; quantify before/after sizes with equal toolchain/data.
- [ ] Link owning rollout PR and remaining version/exception work into the matrix.

## Native fonts moved out of hig-tokens

Issue #64. Up to `0.1.0-candidate.sha7c67a07c`, `@bloxwap/hig/tokens` shipped the 15 static TTFs under `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/fonts/*`. Web-only consumers never served them, but they made up most of the tarball. They now live in `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts`. The bytes, file names, registration keys and SHA-256 hashes are unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `require('@bloxwap/hig/tokens/fonts/BloxwapSans.ttf')` | `require('@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts/fonts/BloxwapSans.ttf')` |
| `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/fonts/manifest.json` | `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts/manifest`, or the typed `fontManifest` export |
| `@bloxwap/hig/tokens/fonts/OFL.txt` | `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts/fonts/OFL.txt` |

- **Expo / React Native:** add the `bloxwap-hig-native-fonts-*.tgz` tarball next to tokens, contracts and native (with a matching `overrides` entry when vendoring), then replace the import prefix. `nativeFont(fontManifest, 'BloxwapSans', 600)` from `@bloxwap/hig/contracts` returns the registration key. Hashes you already pinned stay valid.
- **Satori / OG images in web repositories:** these also read static TTFs (bloxwap/chart's OG card is one). Install `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts` as a build-time dependency for that script only, or read the TTF from `@bloxwap/font` if it ships one. Never copy the faces into the repository.
- **Web-only hosts:** remove nothing. They keep loading fonts from `@bloxwap/font`, and their tokens tarball shrinks. `npm run release:dry-run` fails if any web or shared tarball contains `.ttf`, `.otf` or `.woff*` files, and it records the packed sizes in `packedSizes` in the release report.
- **Coordination:** monorepo#4540 (merged) already loads the faces from `@bloxwap/hig/native-fonts`.

## Native colour space (#93)

Up to `0.1.0-candidate.shaac27cf7`, HIG native components always painted `nativeSrgb` hex values. On an iOS host whose React Native default colour space is Display P3, those values were read as P3 channels, so the Switch track, Alert accent, Text, Surface and the other components painted warning, negative and info more saturated than the token. HIG now selects one of its own tables through the provider:

```tsx
// iOS hosts whose app delegate returns .displayP3 from defaultColorSpace() (bloxwap/monorepo apps/mobile/plugins/with-ios-display-p3.js).
<HIGProvider colorSpace='display-p3'>{app}</HIGProvider>
```

- **Display P3 hosts** set `colorSpace='display-p3'` on the root `HIGProvider`. iOS then paints `nativeColors.iosDisplayP3`, and Android and web keep `nativeSrgb`, so the prop can be set unconditionally. Nested providers inherit it.
- **Host-drawn colour** next to HIG components: drop local `nativeColors.iosDisplayP3` lookups and per-platform selection and read `useColors()` from `@bloxwap/hig/native/provider`. Delete wrappers that only existed to pass a P3 colour into Button `style`.
- **sRGB hosts** change nothing. The default is `srgb` and renders the same values as before.
- Raw colours are still not accepted. `colorSpace` takes only `'srgb'` or `'display-p3'`, and any other value falls back to sRGB.

Rollback: host feature flag restores old renderer/backends and previous lockfile. Persisted business data and feedback choices retain old-compatible fields during staged rollout; avoid one-way preference deletion. Keep old static assets until both physical platforms pass.

| Surface | Pilot and HIG mapping | Preserve | Owner work remaining |

## Partial adoption: scoped component CSS and the opt-in base (#95)

`@bloxwap/hig/react/css` now styles HIG components only, so a product can load it on the routes it migrates and leave the rest of the site alone. Next.js keeps a route's stylesheet after a client navigation. Before #95 the file also set page-wide rules (`* { box-sizing }`, a global `:focus-visible` ring, `table`/`th`/`td` and `input[type=range]` defaults), and these reached routes that never imported HIG. Those rules are now the opt-in entry `@bloxwap/hig/react/css/base` (see [installation](https://bloxwap.github.io/hig/docs/guides/installation/#component-css-and-the-opt-in-base)).

- **Whole-page adopters** (bloxwap.app, bloxwap.pro, docs sites): add `import '@bloxwap/hig/react/css/base'` before `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` to keep the current look of plain tables, ranges and focus rings. HIG components need no change.
- **Partial adopters**: import only `@bloxwap/hig/react/css` in the HIG routes, and delete any host reset that undid the old global rules. taptradetv loads HIG only on `/sponsors` ([taptradetv#188](https://github.com/bloxwap/taptradetv/pull/188), #59). The registry refresh in [taptradetv#253](https://github.com/bloxwap/taptradetv/pull/253) includes #95 and removes the obsolete `th, td` reset in `apps/web/app/sponsors/sponsors-hig.css`. The `/schedule` calendar then keeps its own cell styles after a navigation from `/sponsors`, and non-HIG routes keep the host's focus ring.
- Before removing a reset, verify with a client navigation from a HIG route to a non-HIG route in a production build. Compare the computed styles of tables, ranges and focus rings, not only screenshots.

Rollback: keep the previous artifact lockfile and original UI behind a host feature flag. Revert the pilot switch/lockfile; keep raw settings/business data unchanged. Do not remove legacy files until the pilot is certified. The adoption matrix, not this kit, records which surfaces are migrated.

- [ ] Execute that repo's production/static build and distinctive demo. Verify asset paths, keyboard/search/copy/mobile nav, loading/error/offline states, large text/RTL, and muted feedback.
